title: Version narrative frozen on v1.1.0 / 'releases stay on v1' across README, web docs, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, CHANGELOG, RELEASING
description: Every prose statement about which version is canonical will be false at v3.0.0. README.md:22-27 ('This development tree documents the planned v1.1 line. The currently published canonical stable release is v1.0.0...'), README.md:59-72 ('Today, @latest selects the published v1.0.0 stable release'), README.md:467-477 ('installable releases stay on v1. The v1.1.0 line is preceded by...A future true v2 requires a deliberate module-path and API migration'), web/docs/index.html:46-50 and 125-135 ('currently v1.0.0', '@latest resolves to the highest published v1.x.y tag'), CONTRIBUTING.md:174-186 ('The module path has no major suffix, so releases must remain on v1'), SECURITY.md:10-16 (supported-versions table rows 'Latest stable v1 release', 'Current announced v1 release candidate', 'Older v1 releases'), CHANGELOG.md:3-4 ('semantic versioning on the canonical github.com/brumbelow/layerleak v1 module line'), CHANGELOG.md:125-130 ('v1.1.0 contains and supersedes their work'), RELEASING.md:7-30 ('Valid release inputs are v1.<minor>.<patch>...The workflow rejects v2 and v3 tags...The stable v1.1.0 release will restore the GitHub latest designation'). The GitHub release-notes template in .github/workflows/container-release.yml:1043-1045 repeats 'Canonical Go module releases continue on v1.x.'
evidence: README.md:469-471: 'The canonical module path is `github.com/brumbelow/layerleak`, so installable releases stay on v1. The v1.1.0 line is preceded by one or more v1.1.0 release candidates.' CONTRIBUTING.md:182: 'The module path has no major suffix, so releases must remain on v1.' RELEASING.md:16-17: 'The workflow rejects v2 and v3 tags because those majors require `/v2` or `/v3` in the module path.'
proposed_fix: Replace every instance with one shared paragraph (use verbatim in README 'Version history', web/docs hero note, CHANGELOG preamble; abbreviate in CONTRIBUTING/SECURITY/RELEASING): "Layerleak's canonical Go module is `github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3`, and v3.0.0 is the first release on it. Two earlier lines exist and are frozen. v1.0.0 (2026-04-03) is the only release ever published on the root module path `github.com/brumbelow/layerleak`, so `go install github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest` will always resolve to that build and should no longer be used. The v2.0.0-v2.5.0 GitHub/container releases were tagged without the `/v2` module-path suffix Go requires, so they were never installable Go modules and that major version cannot be reused; they remain for history. Rather than repair either line, the project moved to `/v3`, which contains and supersedes all of that work. Container images continue at `ghcr.io/brumbelow/layerleak`, where `v3.0.0` and `latest` name the same signed digest." Delete the 'planned v1.1 line'/'frozen labels' sentences entirely; a major release does not need the RC-freeze explanation in user docs (keep it in RELEASING only). Update SECURITY table rows to 'Latest stable v3 release', 'Current announced v3 release candidate', 'v1.0.0 (root module) - Unsupported; migrate to /v3', 'Historical v2.0.0-v2.5.0 tags - Unsupported and not valid Go modules'. Update the workflow release-notes text (CI area) to match.
verifier_note: Every cited line checks out: README.md:22-27 and :469-477 ('installable releases stay on v1'), web/docs/index.html:46-50 and :125-135, CONTRIBUTING.md:182 ('releases must remain on v1'), SECURITY.md:12-14 table rows, CHANGELOG.md:3-4 and :129-130, RELEASING.md:9-17 and :27-30, container-release.yml:1043-1045. All become false at v3.0.0. Also in scope for the same edit: web/docs/index.html:75 status strip and container-release.yml:9 input description 'Exact v1 release, for example v1.1.0-rc.1 or v1.1.0'. Proposed narrative paragraph is accurate (GitHub API confirms tags v1.0.0-beta.1, v1.0.0, v2.0.0-beta, v2.0.0, v2.1.0, v2.1.1, v2.5.0 and latest release v2.5.0).

title: All go install / go list / clone-and-build commands use the root module path; v3 requires github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3
description: Once go.mod says `module github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3`, `go install github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest` (README.md:54, :63-64; web/docs/index.html:75 status strip, :115, :130; CONTRIBUTING.md:179; RELEASING.md:234, :238, :283-284) keeps resolving to v1.0.0 forever, and `go install github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@v3.0.0` fails with 'module github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@v3.0.0 found... but does not contain package' / invalid version. The docs never mention that the binary is still named `layerleak` (Go strips the /vN suffix when naming the executable), which is the first thing a user will ask. The post-publication checks in RELEASING.md:283-289 (`go install github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest installs v1.1.0`) become impossible to satisfy.
evidence: README.md:54: 'go install github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest'; README.md:63-64: 'go install github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@v1.0.0' / '...@v1.1.0-rc.1'; web/docs/index.html:75: 'github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest'; RELEASING.md:284: '`go install github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest` installs v1.1.0'
proposed_fix: As proposed, plus: README.md:57 'The module root is the canonical install target' and web/docs/index.html:110-111 'The module root is the supported CLI entrypoint' remain true but should say 'the module root at github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3' so readers do not conflate the repository root path with the module path.
verifier_note: README.md:54, :63-64, web/docs/index.html:75, :115, :130, CONTRIBUTING.md:179, RELEASING.md:234-239 and :283-284 all use the root path. With `module github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3`, `go install github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest` resolves to v1.0.0 forever and `@v3.0.0` on the root path is an invalid version. The binary-name note is correct: Go drops the major-version suffix when naming the installed executable. The RELEASING post-publication check and the workflow's Go-proxy check (container-release.yml:1165-1180, hard-coded `github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@${RELEASE_VERSION}`) must change together, as stated.

title: go.mod module directive must become github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3
description: The module directive is the root of the migration. Without the /v3 suffix in the go.mod of the tagged commit, proxy.golang.org rejects any v3 tag exactly the way it rejects the v2 tags today.
evidence: go.mod:1 `module github.com/brumbelow/layerleak`. Proxy probe of the poisoned v2 path shows the failure mode: `go list -m -versions github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v2` -> "invalid version: go.mod has non-.../v2 module path \"github.com/brumbelow/layerleak\" (and .../v2/go.mod does not exist) at revision v2.5.0".
proposed_fix: Run `go mod edit -module github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3` (result: `module github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3`). Keep `go 1.25.13` and all require blocks unchanged. Validated in a scratch copy: `go list -m` prints github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3, go build/vet/tidy -diff pass, go.sum byte-identical.
verifier_note: go.mod:1 is `module github.com/brumbelow/layerleak`. Re-probed proxy: `go list -m -versions github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v2` -> `invalid version: go.mod has non-.../v2 module path "github.com/brumbelow/layerleak" (and .../v2/go.mod does not exist) at revision v2.5.0`; `gh api contents/go.mod?ref=v2.5.0` confirms the v2.5.0 tag's go.mod is the root path. `/v3` is clean (`no matching versions for query "latest"`). Reproduced `go mod edit -module` in a scratch copy: go.sum byte-identical, build/vet/tidy -diff pass.

title: Release validate job's go.mod module check must expect /v3
description: The validate job reads go.mod from the control-plane checkout (main) and refuses to release unless it equals the old root path.
evidence: container-release.yml:111-114 `if [[ "$(awk '$1 == "module" { print $2 }' go.mod)" != "github.com/brumbelow/layerleak" ]]; then echo "The root Go module path is not release-compatible."`
proposed_fix: Replace the expected value with `github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3`. Optionally also assert the major suffix matches the requested version major (`v3`) so a future /v4 move cannot be released with a stale check.
verifier_note: container-release.yml:111-114 compares the awk'd module line against the root path. The control-plane checkout (lines 56-60, fetch-depth 0, default ref) is main for stable and the source commit for an RC (enforced at 170-174), so go.mod will carry /v3 in both cases and the check fails as written.

title: Release workflow version regexes, tag glob and input text are v1-only
description: Five places pin the accepted version shape to v1: the version regex, the stable-candidate regex, the increasing-stable-version loop (regex, tag glob, re-match) and the workflow_dispatch input description. `v3.0.0-rc.1` is rejected at line 103 today.
evidence: line 9 `description: Exact v1 release, for example v1.1.0-rc.1 or v1.1.0`; line 103 `=~ ^v1\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(-rc\.[1-9][0-9]*)?$`; line 104 `Version must be a canonical v1 stable or RC tag.`; line 180 `=~ ^v1\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)-rc\.[1-9][0-9]*$`; line 181 `A stable release requires an accepted v1 RC tag.`; line 201 `=~ ^v1\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$`; line 210 `done < <(git tag --list 'v1.*')`; line 213 `[[ "${REQUESTED_VERSION}" =~ ^v1\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$ ]]`.
proposed_fix: Replace `v1\.` with `v3\.` in lines 103, 180, 201, 213; change line 210 to `git tag --list 'v3.*'`; line 9 -> `Exact v3 release, for example v3.0.0-rc.1 or v3.0.0`; line 104 -> `Version must be a canonical v3 stable or RC tag.`; line 181 -> `A stable release requires an accepted v3 RC tag.` Preferably hoist a single `RELEASE_MAJOR: v3` env and build the regexes from it so the next major is a one-line change. With no v3 stable tags the loop leaves latest_stable empty and correctly skips the ordering check for v3.0.0.
verifier_note: Re-grepped: lines 9, 103, 104, 180, 181, 201, 210, 213 are the complete set of v1-pinned regexes/globs/text (other `v1`/`v2`/`v3` hits at 335 `type=provenance,...,version=v1`, 656/729 SPDX, 755 cosign v3.0.2 are unrelated). Read lines 196-220: with `git tag --list 'v3.*'` and no v3 stable tag, `latest_stable` stays empty and the ordering guard is skipped, as claimed.

title: Post-release Go proxy checks install/list the root module instead of /v3
description: After the move, `go install github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@v3.0.0-rc.1` fails (the root module has no such version) and `go list -m github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest` keeps returning v1.0.0, so the post-release job would fail (or, for stable, spin for five minutes then fail).
evidence: line 1165 `go install "github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@${RELEASE_VERSION}"`; line 1176 and 1180 `go list -m -f '{{.Version}}' github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest`. Proxy probe: `go list -m -versions github.com/brumbelow/layerleak` -> `v1.0.0-beta v1.0.0-beta.1 v1.0.0`.
proposed_fix: Use `github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3@${RELEASE_VERSION}` at 1165 and `github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3@latest` at 1176 and 1180 (or a `MODULE_PATH` env). The installed binary is still named `layerleak` (Go strips the major-version element), so line 1174 keeps working.
verifier_note: Lines 1165, 1176, 1180 use the root path. Post-release runs inside the released-source checkout (lines 1118-1122) so the main module will be /v3; verified from inside the /v3 scratch module that `go list -m github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3@latest` is sent to the proxy (404 today, not a main-module error) and that `go list -m github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest` returns v1.0.0. `GOBIN=... go install .` in the /v3 module produced a binary named `layerleak`, so line 1174 keeps working.

title: Post-release RC assertion `latest_module != RELEASE_VERSION` will fail for the first /v3 RC
description: (d) Go's @latest query returns the highest release version, or the highest prerelease when the module has no release versions. github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3 has no versions at all today, so after v3.0.0-rc.1 is published `go list -m .../v3@latest` returns exactly v3.0.0-rc.1 and the workflow's RC guard fails the run after the release is already public. RELEASING.md's RC-acceptance text ("@latest remains the previous stable") is likewise untrue for the first v3 RC. GHCR `:latest` is unaffected (latest_before is captured from the registry, which currently points at the v2.5.0 image, and RC never moves it).
evidence: lines 1175-1177 `if [[ "${PRERELEASE}" == true ]]; then latest_module="$(... go list -m -f '{{.Version}}' github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest)"; test "${latest_module}" != "${RELEASE_VERSION}"`. Proxy probe today: `go list -m github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3@latest` -> `404 Not Found ... no matching versions for query "latest"` (no versions exist, so the first tag becomes @latest). RELEASING.md:244 `exact RC installation succeeds while @latest remains the previous stable`.
proposed_fix: Keep the auditor's stable_exists logic but wrap the @latest query so a 404 (`no matching versions`) is treated as `absent`, retry until the module's version list contains RELEASE_VERSION, and only then assert: PRERELEASE && !stable_exists -> latest == RELEASE_VERSION; PRERELEASE && stable_exists -> latest != RELEASE_VERSION; stable -> latest == RELEASE_VERSION. Budget the retry for the documented 30-minute cache window (see MIG-23/MIG-27). Update RELEASING.md:244 and README accordingly.
verifier_note: Go's `latest` query selects the highest release version, else the highest prerelease when no release exists; /v3 has no versions (`no matching versions for query "latest"`), so after rc.1 is published `.../v3@latest` == v3.0.0-rc.1 and `test "${latest_module}" != "${RELEASE_VERSION}"` (line 1177) fails. Additional failure mode the auditor missed: proxy.golang.org documents that "if someone requested the version before the tag was pushed, it may take up to 30 minutes for the mirror's cache to expire"; both the auditor and this verification already requested `/v3/@v/list` and `@latest`, so the first `go list -m .../v3@latest` after publication may still return the cached 404. Under `set -euo pipefail` a failing command substitution in `latest_module="$(...)"` aborts the step, so the RC job fails either way.

title: release-preflight.py VERSION regex and error string are v1-only
description: The tag handoff validator and candidate validator both build on VERSION; `python3 scripts/release-preflight.py tag --version v3.0.0-rc.1` fails with 'invalid canonical v1 version' today, which blocks the validate job (line 123) and the publish job (line 973).

title: 3.0.0 requires the /v3 module path and every v1-only release gate must accept v3
description: The product decision behind 3.0.0 is to restore a canonical `go install ...@latest` line after the poisoned v2 tag space. That is only possible by moving the module to github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3. Today every release gate and every user-facing document is pinned to v1: the workflow regex, the preflight regex, RELEASING's version policy, and the README's install commands and 'installable releases stay on v1' statement. Shipping 3.0.0 without all of these changing would produce an unpublishable or falsely documented release.
evidence: go.mod: `module github.com/brumbelow/layerleak` / `go 1.25.13`. .github/workflows/container-release.yml:103: `if [[ ! "${REQUESTED_VERSION}" =~ ^v1\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(-rc\.[1-9][0-9]*)?$ ]]` and :210 `git tag --list 'v1.*'`. scripts/release-preflight.py:19: `VERSION = r'v1\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)'`. RELEASING.md:16-17: 'The workflow rejects v2 and v3 tags because those majors require `/v2` or `/v3` in the module path.' README.md:469-470: 'so installable releases stay on v1.' README.md:54: `go install github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest`. web/docs/openapi.yaml:4: `version: 1.1.0`. CHANGELOG.md:8: `## [v1.1.0]`.
proposed_fix: Add to the single v3 migration PR: (a) container-release.yml:111 compare against `github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3`; (b) verify.yml:40 `test "$(go list -m)" = "github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3"`; (c) container-release.yml:1040 `-f previous_tag_name=v1.0.0` and RELEASING.md:28 'Generate new release notes from v1.0.0' must become the previous canonical stable (v3.0.0 notes from v1.0.0 would span the whole history; decide explicitly and document); (d) README.md:5 Go badge and :53 'requires Go 1.25.13 or newer' re-verified against the chosen minimum. Everything else as proposed.
verifier_note: Every quoted gate verified: go.mod `module github.com/brumbelow/layerleak`; container-release.yml:103 `^v1\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)...` and :210 `git tag --list 'v1.*'`; release-preflight.py:19 `VERSION = r'v1\...'`; RELEASING.md:16-17; README.md:54 `go install github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest` and :469-470 'installable releases stay on v1'; openapi.yaml:4 `version: 1.1.0`; CHANGELOG.md:8 `## [v1.1.0]`. The fix is incomplete, though: two further module-identity gates pin the un-suffixed path and would fail the very PR that moves to /v3 — container-release.yml:111 `awk '$1 == "module"...' != "github.com/brumbelow/layerleak"` and verify.yml:40 `test "$(go list -m)" = "github.com/brumbelow/layerleak"` (see PRD-23). CUT-LINE OPINION: I agree 3.0.0 should be the contract release — module path (PRD-01/23), cmd/scanner removal (PRD-02), the single-file local output (PRD-03, with the raw-secret caveat), result schema v2 + API versioning statement (PRD-04), honest error text in local output (PRD-05), exit code 3 + --fail-on (PRD-06), detector-id cleanup incl. the Name()/emitted-id mismatch (PRD-07/26), `version` (PRD-12), and lint/Makefile (PRD-21). I would NOT put private-registry auth in 3.0.0 (PRD-08 → 3.1): it is additive, it needs its own soak, it interacts with the egress allowlist and with an unauthenticated API, and without credential helpers it covers fewer registries than claimed. SARIF (PRD-09) can stay in 3.0.0 because it is a pure encoder that depends only on PRD-07/PRD-12 which are in scope. That yields roughly the author's ~16-day breaking-only cut plus ~3 days for SARIF, and keeps the RC soak focused on the module-path and schema changes that cannot be fixed in a patch.

title: OpenAPI info.version is frozen at 1.1.0; must become 3.0.0
description: The published OpenAPI document advertises `version: 1.1.0`, a version that was never released. At v3.0.0 the spec, the docs-site link text, and README would all be stale on the same day the release ships.
evidence:
web/docs/openapi.yaml:2-4:
  info:
    title: Layerleak API
    version: 1.1.0
Also README.md:388 and web/docs/index.html:411 link to "the versioned OpenAPI 3.1 specification" with no version gate.

title: Release workflow and preflight accept only v1 versions; every regex, glob and description must move to v3
description: The dispatch input description, version regex, candidate regex, latest-stable computation and preflight VERSION constant are all hard-coded to major 1, so a v3.0.0-rc.1 dispatch fails at the first validation step ('Version must be a canonical v1 stable or RC tag'). The same constant lives in scripts/release-preflight.py and every fixture in scripts/tests/test_release_preflight.py uses v1.1.0-rc.1.
evidence: container-release.yml:9 `description: Exact v1 release, for example v1.1.0-rc.1 or v1.1.0`; :103 `=~ ^v1\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(-rc\.[1-9][0-9]*)?$`; :180 `=~ ^v1\.(...)-rc\.[1-9][0-9]*$`; :201/:213 `=~ ^v1\.`; :210 `done < <(git tag --list 'v1.*')`; scripts/release-preflight.py:19 `VERSION = r'v1\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)'`; :111 `raise ValueError('invalid canonical v1 version')`; test fixtures lines 138,161,166-243 all use 'v1.1.0-rc.1'.

title: Post-release Go-proxy checks use the v1 module path, and the RC '@latest must differ' assertion is false for the first v3 RC
description: post-release installs and lists `github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@...`; for a /v3 module those queries must use `github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3`. Independently, Go resolves `@latest` to the highest release version, or if the module has none, the highest pre-release. The /v3 module will have zero release versions when v3.0.0-rc.1 publishes, so `go list -m .../v3@latest` returns v3.0.0-rc.1 and `test "${latest_module}" != "${RELEASE_VERSION}"` fails, marking a successful RC publication as a failed run. RELEASING.md's RC acceptance bullet ('@latest remains the previous stable') and README lines 67-69 encode the same false expectation for a new major.
evidence: container-release.yml:1165 `go install "github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@${RELEASE_VERSION}"`; :1176 `latest_module="$(... go list -m -f '{{.Version}}' github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest)"`; :1177 `test "${latest_module}" != "${RELEASE_VERSION}"`; RELEASING.md 'exact RC installation succeeds while `@latest` remains the previous stable'. Go module query semantics: '@latest ... prefers release versions over pre-release versions; if no release versions exist the highest pre-release is selected'.
proposed_fix: Use `github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3` in all three places. For the RC branch compute the expected answer from the proxy, not local tags: `stable="$(GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org go list -m -versions github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3 | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -E '^v3\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | sort -V | tail -1)"`; if `stable` is empty require `latest_module == RELEASE_VERSION` (first RC of the major) else require `latest_module == stable`. Update RELEASING.md RC acceptance and README lines 67-69 to describe the first-RC behaviour.
verifier_note: Lines 1165/1176/1180 use the bare path. I confirmed Go's @latest semantics empirically: `go list -m -versions github.com/brumbelow/layerleak` -> `v1.0.0-beta v1.0.0-beta.1 v1.0.0` and `@latest` -> v1.0.0 (prefers release over pre-release). For the fresh /v3 path there is no release version, so @latest == v3.0.0-rc.1 and line 1177 `test != RELEASE_VERSION` fails the run. I also tested the auditor's implicit assumption that `go list -m <main module>@latest` works from inside the checkout: it does (returned v1.0.0 from /home/user/layerleak), so no cwd change is needed. One gap in the fix: the post-release checkout (line 1119) is fetch-depth 1 without tags, so 'if any stable v3.* tag exists' cannot be read from local git.

title: Reviewed GitHub CLI pin 2.100.0 has two advisories that weaken exactly the attestation policy the workflow relies on

title: The protected release pipeline has never executed and cannot be rehearsed in a fork
description: The Actions history for container-release.yml contains only four legacy push-triggered runs (v2.0.0-v2.5.0, ~1m50s each) from the previous workflow; the current 1231-line workflow_dispatch pipeline (validate, reusable verify, stage-image, scan, supply-chain, smoke, protected publish, post-release) has zero runs. title: keyword_entropy never fires on unquoted KEY=VALUE because '=' is in the candidate charset
description: entropyCandidateExpression is `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9+/=_-]{19,}`. Because '=' is inside the class, FindAllStringIndex (line 400) returns the entire `DB_PASSWORD=q7Y8...` line as ONE leftmost-longest candidate; its prefix is empty, hasAssignedValuePrefix fails (line 626) and no value-only candidate is ever tried. The dominant secret shapes in images are therefore invisible to the generic detector: .env files, `export KEY=VALUE` in shell scripts, Dockerfile `ENV KEY=VALUE`/`RUN export ...` history lines, Java .properties (`db.password=`), INI/my.cnf (`password=`). Only quoted (`KEY="v"`) or spaced (`KEY = v`) variants work. Dockerfile legacy `ENV KEY value` (space form) also fails because whitespace is not an assignment marker.
evidence: Probe (scratch copy of Default()): `.env unquoted KEY=VALUE random => <none>`; `.env spaced KEY = VALUE => keyword_entropy[14:48]`; `.env quoted KEY="VALUE" => keyword_entropy[13:47]`; `java properties db.password= => <none>`; `my.cnf password= => <none>`; `bare password= => <none>`; `shell export unquoted => <none>` vs `shell export quoted => keyword_entropy`; `history RUN export unquoted => <none>`; `history ENV unquoted => <none>`; `Dockerfile ENV KEY value (space form) history => <none>`. Code: detectors.go:433 `entropyCandidateExpression = regexp.MustCompile(`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9+/=_-]{19,}`)`, :400 `candidates := entropyCandidateExpression.FindAllStringIndex(line.Value, -1)`, :626 `if !hasAssignedValuePrefix(prefix) { return false }`.
proposed_fix: Fix as proposed (drop '=' from the repeating class of entropyCandidateExpression and of the assigned_sensitive_value value regex at detectors.go:64; allow only trailing '={0,2}'). Note that once '=' is removed, env/label inputs automatically produce value-only spans (prefix 'KEY=' satisfies hasAssignedValuePrefix), so this change alone also changes DET-03 behaviour and must ship with DET-05 (hex values) and the DET-38 priority fix below, and the env_* corpus fixtures must drop their duplicate keyword_entropy expectations.
verifier_note: Reproduced in a scratch copy of Default(): '.env unquoted DB_PASSWORD=<rnd>' => <none>, 'properties db.password=' => <none>, 'export API_TOKEN=' => <none>, history 'RUN export' and 'ENV KEY value' => <none>, while spaced/quoted variants fire keyword_entropy. Root cause is exactly detectors.go:433 ('=' inside the repeating class makes the whole KEY=VALUE token the leftmost-longest candidate) plus :626. Also found that labels with dotted keys (com.example.token=<rnd>, Key=com.example.token) yield <none> because the candidate 'token=<rnd>' has prefix 'com.example.' which is neither an assignment nor standalone.

description: hasAssignedValuePrefix trims trailing whitespace, then trailing quotes, then checks for `:=`, `=>`, `=` or `:` suffix. When a space separates the operator from the opening quote (canonical pretty JSON, quoted YAML, TOML/HCL, Python, JS/TS object literals, Go struct literals, Ruby/PHP hashes) the string after quote-stripping ends in a space and every suffix test fails. title: Env/label/config sources report the whole `KEY=VALUE` line as the secret: wrong span, key name in redacted_value, duplicate finding, fingerprint differs from the same secret in a file
description: For metadata sources the scanner passes `Content: "KEY=VALUE"` with `Key: KEY` (scan.go:697-703). Because '=' is in the candidate/value classes (DET-01) the only candidate is the entire line, and hasEntropyContext accepts it via `sensitiveKey(key) && isStandaloneValue(...)` (line 623); keyValueDetector does the same at line 332. Result: (a) Match.Value/Fingerprint are computed over `DB_PASSWORD=<secret>`, so the same secret found in a .env file (value-only) gets a different fingerprint, breaking cross-source dedup, unique_fingerprints and finding history; (b) every env secret that also hits a specific rule yields two findings (`GH_TOKEN=ghp_...` -> keyword_entropy[0:49] + github_token[9:49]), inflating total_findings/unique_fingerprints; the corpus fixtures env_* encode this by expecting both detectors; (c) redacted_value becomes `DB_***...B5` and match_start is 0. Coupling: the probe shows hex32 `CLIENT_SECRET` env values are detected 100% only because the key name inflates entropy; a value-only span drops that to ~16% unless DET-05 ships too.

Fingerprints: `env : keyword_entropy value="DB_PASSWORD=q7Y8..." fp=6c3f6a1a6f2b redacted="DB_*****...B5"` vs `file : keyword_entropy value="q7Y8..." fp=fd2038336474` (= fp of the secret alone). Corpus real_positives/env_anthropic_key_actionable.json: `"expected_detectors": ["anthropic_api_key", "keyword_entropy"]`. Hex-rate probe: `hex32 env CLIENT_SECRET (assigned_sensitive_value only) -> 100.0%` vs `.env file CLIENT_SECRET="v" (keyword_entropy) -> 16.3%`.
proposed_fix: Removing '=' from the candidate classes (DET-01) already yields value-only spans for 'KEY=VALUE' env/label content; additionally make keyValueDetector/contextEntropyDetector strip a leading '<Key>=' / '<Key>:' when input.Key is set so dotted label keys work, and lower priorityForKeyValueDetector("assigned_sensitive_value") below priorityLocal (see DET-38) or identical-span collisions after the fix will be labelled assigned_sensitive_value instead of github_token. title: Entropy threshold 3.75 bits rejects most hex secrets (32-hex pass rate 15%, 40-hex 34%, UUID 40%)
description: passesEntropy requires Shannon entropy ≥ 3.75 bits over the observed characters. A random hex string cannot exceed 4 bits and its plug-in entropy for n samples is ≈ 4 − 15/(2n·ln2), i.e. ~3.66 for 32 chars, so most genuine 32/40-hex API keys (Datadog, Twilio, Mailgun, Algolia, Facebook app secrets, Rails master.key, many OAuth client secrets) fail. The same gate is used by looksLikeAssignedSensitiveValue (structured.go:355-358) for assigned_sensitive_value, terraform_cloud_token, docker_config_identitytoken and the cloudflare/vercel key-value rules, and by looksLikeAWSSessionToken.
evidence: Monte Carlo (20k trials each): `random hex len=32 passesEntropy(>=3.75) rate = 15.3%`, `len=37 26.1%`, `len=40 33.6%`, `len=64 85.2%`, `random uuid 40.5%`, vs `random alnum len=20 96.1%`. End-to-end: `.env file CLIENT_SECRET="<hex32>" (keyword_entropy) -> 16.3%`, `yaml api_key: <hex32> -> 16.7%`, `hex40 .env -> 34.1%`; `DD_API_KEY hex32 in .env file => <none>`. Code: detectors.go:840 `return entropy >= 3.75`.
proposed_fix: Alphabet-aware threshold as proposed, but (1) also relax isLowercaseSeparatorCandidate (DET-37) or UUID-shaped tokens still never pass, and (2) add a guard for hex that is a content digest (preceded by sha1:/sha256:/md5= or in lock files) to limit the false-positive increase; add deterministic random-hex fixtures.
verifier_note: Monte Carlo (20k each): hex32 passesEntropy 15.3%, hex40 33.6%, hex64 85.1%, uuid 40.4%, alnum20 96%. End to end: quoted hex32 CLIENT_SECRET in .env detected 14.9%; unquoted hex32 DD_API_KEY in a .env file 0.0% (no Key, kv detector silent, keyword_entropy fails entropy). Threshold at detectors.go:840 confirmed.

title: age_secret_key regex is lowercase-only; real age identities are uppercase Bech32 so the detector can never match one
description: The rule is `\bAGE-SECRET-KEY-1[a-z0-9]{58}\b`. The age spec (C2SP age.md) encodes identities as Bech32 with HRP `AGE-SECRET-KEY-` and the canonical example is `AGE-SECRET-KEY-1<redacted>` (uppercase; Bech32 is all-upper or all-lower and the HRP here is upper). age-keygen output and SOPS key files (`~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt`, common in images) are therefore never detected. The unit test at detectors_test.go:244 uses a lowercase fixture that no real tool produces.
evidence: Probe: `age real uppercase key (AGE-SECRET-KEY-1<redacted>) => <none>`; `age lowercase (test fixture shape) => age_secret_key[0:74]`. Spec text fetched: identities are "encoded as Bech32 with HRP `AGE-SECRET-KEY-`", example uppercase. gitleaks rule: `AGE-SECRET-KEY-1[QPZRY9X8GF2TVDW0S3JN54KHCE6MUA7L]{58}`.
proposed_fix: Use the Bech32 charset in both cases since Bech32 permits all-lower too: \bAGE-SECRET-KEY-1(?:[QPZRY9X8GF2TVDW0S3JN54KHCE6MUA7L]{58}|[qpzry9x8gf2tvdw0s3jn54khce6mua7l]{58})\b; fix detectors_test.go:244 to an uppercase fixture and add the sops keys.txt corpus case.

title: Redact() reveals 5 characters of every value ≥7 runes (71% of a 7-char password); with the unsalted fingerprint short passwords are fully recoverable
description: Redact masks fully only when len ≤ 6; otherwise it keeps 3 leading and 2 trailing runes regardless of length. netrc_password and pypirc_password accept 4-character values (detectors.go:84-85 `hasMinPrintableLength(4)`), git_credentials_password has no minimum, and basic-auth/URL passwords are commonly 8-12 chars. A 7-char password shows 5/7 characters; combined with `fingerprint = sha256(value)` (DET-09) the remaining 2 characters are a 36²-guess brute force against a published hash. redacted_value is persisted in `findings.redacted_value`, returned by the API and written to the 'always-redacted' scan record, contradicting README's redaction guarantee.
evidence: Probe: `Redact("hunter2") = "hun**r2" visible=5/7 (71%)`, `Redact("abcdefgh") = "abc***gh" (62%)`, `Redact("Passw0rd12") = "Pas*****12" (50%)`, `Redact("abcdefghijkl") = "abc*******kl" (42%)`. Code findings.go:321-325: `if len(runes) <= 6 { return strings.Repeat("*", len(runes)) }` / `return string(runes[:3]) + strings.Repeat("*", len(runes)-5) + string(runes[len(runes)-2:])`.
proposed_fix: As proposed (full mask below 12 runes, prefix-only reveal above); additionally cap the asterisk run (e.g. fixed 8) so length is not disclosed, and update the listed tests/fixtures and CHANGELOG.
verifier_note: Probe: Redact("hunter2")="hun**r2", Redact("abcdefgh")="abc***gh", Redact("Passw0rd12")="Pas*****12"; netrc/pypirc accept 4-char values and git_credentials_password has no minimum. The asterisk count also discloses exact length. title: Scan throughput is ~0.6 MB/s: ~80 sequential full-content regex passes whose leading \b or (?i) disable Go's literal-prefix fast path
description: Set.Scan runs every detector over the whole content; each regexDetector calls FindAllStringSubmatchIndex on the full input. Go's regexp only skips ahead with strings.Index when the pattern has a literal prefix; a leading `\b` (most token rules) or `(?i)` (AccountKey, aws secret, kv rules) yields `LiteralPrefix() == ""` and forces the NFA over every byte. A 1 MiB file (the MAX_FILE_BYTES default) costs ~1.7 s; 200 MB of text (a node_modules-heavy image) ≈ 6 minutes per platform, which pushes API request deadlines and scan-duration bounds into partial coverage and is a cheap DoS lever for hostile images.
evidence: 4 MiB secret-free text: `scanned 4194412 bytes in 6.73s => 0.6 MB/s, matches=0`. CPU profile: `regexp.(*machine).match 88.30% cum`, `regexp.lazyFlag.match 8.76%`, `regexp/syntax.IsWordChar 4.78%`. Per pattern on the same 4 MiB: `\bglpat-[A-Za-z0-9\-_]{20,}\b 77ms literalPrefix=""` vs `glpat-...\b 1ms literalPrefix="glpat-"`; `\bgh[pousr]_... 77ms` vs `gh[pousr]_... 3ms`; `(?i)AccountKey=... 108ms` vs `AccountKey=... 1ms`; aws secret regex 284ms; discord_bot_token 137ms; `strings.Contains(4MB, "glpat-") = 1.36ms`. Per-detector top: keyword_entropy 524ms, aws_secret_access_key 277ms, discord_webhook 191ms, heroku_api_key 168ms.
proposed_fix: As proposed (required-literal prefilter + post-match boundary check instead of leading \b). Also hoist the regexp.MustCompile in looksLikeAWSAccessKeyID (structured.go:330) to package level; it is recompiled on every call.
verifier_note: Reproduced: 4 MiB secret-free text scanned in 6.57s => 0.64 MB/s with 0 matches. '\bglpat-...' 86ms vs 'glpat-...' 1ms (LiteralPrefix "" vs "glpat-"); '(?i)AccountKey=' 102ms vs 'AccountKey=' <1ms. Top detectors: keyword_entropy 519ms, aws_secret_access_key 246ms, heroku_api_key 183ms, discord_bot_token 173ms, discord_webhook 173ms. Go's Prog.Prefix() skips only Nop/Capture, so a leading EmptyWidth (\b) or (?i) disables the strings.Index fast path.

title: CLI chmods any pre-existing LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR (and symlink targets) to 0700
description: publishResultJSON unconditionally runs os.Chmod(dir, 0o700) on the findings directory and on <dir>/scans after MkdirAll, regardless of whether the CLI created the directory. If a user points LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR at an existing shared directory (a team share, $HOME, a CI workspace) every scan silently strips group/other permissions from it. os.Chmod follows symlinks, so a symlinked findings dir changes the permissions of the link target. The behaviour is codified by assertPrivateArtifacts(t, dir, ...) in results_test.go:280 which asserts the caller-supplied dir ends up 0700.
proposed_fix: Fix as proposed, but apply it in publishResultJSON so both the findings dir and the scans/ subdir get the same treatment (os.Lstat first: refuse or resolve symlinks, Mkdir 0700 only when absent, never Chmod a pre-existing directory; optionally warn when an existing dir is group/world-accessible). Update results_test.go:280 so assertPrivateArtifacts only asserts on files and on directories the test did not pre-create, and add a test that a pre-existing 0755 dir keeps its mode. title: Foreign/Windows layers in a multi-arch index are classified as an integrity failure that aborts the scan and cannot be accepted by --allow-partial
description: SelectDescriptors keeps every non-attestation platform manifest, including windows/* entries. Their layers use application/vnd.docker.image.rootfs.foreign.diff.tar.gzip (or OCI nondistributable types), which manifest.IsLayerMediaType rejects, so ValidateImageManifest returns an IntegrityError (descriptor_media_type_mismatch). Scan treats IsIntegrityError as fatal: it finalizes and returns the error, skipping every platform after the Windows one, and cli.canAcceptPartial refuses integrity errors even with --allow-partial. Result: `layerleak scan golang:1.22` (all platforms) exits 1 with a message implying registry tampering, and the Replay foreign-layer branch (state.go:131-136) is unreachable dead code. Foreign layers are legitimately unscannable, but they are an unsupported-platform condition, not an integrity violation.
evidence: Probe (scratchpad copy, index = linux/amd64 + windows/amd64 whose layer[0] is foreign.diff.tar.gzip): `err=validate image manifest sha256:427f...: descriptor_media_type_mismatch for "layer[0]": expected "supported OCI media type", got "application/vnd.docker.image.rootfs.foreign.diff.tar.gzip"`; `status=partial completed=1 failed=1`. scan.go:287: `if limits.IsExceeded(err) || manifest.IsIntegrityError(err) || isCancellationError(err) || ctx.Err() != nil { finalizeResult(...); return result, err }`. integrity.go:136-140 validates each layer with IsLayerMediaType; document.go:355-362 excludes foreign types. cli/scan.go:321: `... || manifest.IsIntegrityError(err) { return false }`.
proposed_fix: Proposed fix is sound. Two additions: (1) a Windows image referenced directly (single manifest root, e.g. mcr.microsoft.com/windows/nanoserver) fails earlier at verifyRootDocument -> ValidateDocument (scan.go:1014, integrity.go:118), so the media-type acceptance must apply to root validation too and Replay's foreign branch (state.go:131) should return a typed UnsupportedLayerError that scan.go:287 does not treat as fatal; (2) whichever policy is chosen (skip non-linux platforms by default vs. report as unsupported/partial), make canAcceptPartial (cli/scan.go:321) and mustPreserveScanError (jobs/scan.go:717) consistent with it.
verifier_note: Reproduced in a scratchpad copy with an index of linux/amd64 + windows/amd64(foreign layer) + linux/arm64: Scan returned `validate image manifest ...: descriptor_media_type_mismatch for "layer[0]" ... foreign.diff.tar.gzip`, manifest.IsIntegrityError(err)=true, ManifestCount=3 but PlatformResults=2 (the trailing linux/arm64 platform was never scanned). Code path is unambiguous: document.go:291-299 IsScannableManifestDescriptor keeps windows manifests; integrity.go:136-140 validates every layer with IsLayerMediaType, which document.go:355-362 restricts to non-foreign types; scan.go:287 aborts on IsIntegrityError; cli/scan.go:321 refuses integrity errors under --allow-partial; jobs/scan.go:717 mustPreserveScanError also propagates it. state.go:131-133 foreign branch is unreachable because validation runs first in resolveImageManifest (scan.go:486/506). Release-blocking stands.

description: The result is the product's public contract (stdout JSON, local record, API `result`, stored `scan_runs.result`) yet it is documented only informally in OpenAPI and the Pages site. OpenAPI currently promises the result only ever changes additively within API v1, so a v2 schema must either be reconciled with that promise or the promise rewritten — this is a release-time correctness issue.

title: Private registry authentication — there is currently no credential path at all; IN 3.0.0 (fallback 3.1)
description: Value: very high. Every CLI/README surface says 'public', and the code confirms the registry client only performs anonymous bearer-token exchange: the token request is executed with an empty Authorization, no username/password, no docker config.json, no `LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_TOKEN`. A secret scanner that cannot scan an organization's own private images (GHCR private, Docker Hub private, ECR private, Artifact Registry) is limited to auditing third-party images, which is the smaller use case. Risk: medium — credentials must never reach logs, token cache keys must be identity-scoped, and the existing egress policy (private hosts blocked unless allowlisted) must remain in force. Effort m. Verdict: IN 3.0.0 as the headline reason to upgrade; it is additive so it can slip to 3.1 without breaking anything if schedule demands.
evidence: internal/registry/client.go:489 `response, err := c.executeRequest(requestCtx, http.MethodGet, parsedRealm.String(), "", "")` (token endpoint called with no credentials); :510-513 token payload has only `token`/`access_token`; `grep -n 'Username|Password|SetBasicAuth|credential' internal/registry/*.go internal/scanservice/*.go` returns nothing. internal/cli/scan.go:40 `Short: "Scan a public OCI image reference from any supported registry"`; internal/cli/root.go:41 `Short: "Scan public OCI images for likely secrets"`. README.md:7-8 'resolves public image references'. CHANGELOG.md:76 'egress policy rejects credentials' refers to userinfo in URLs, not an auth feature.
proposed_fix: Design for 3.0.0: (1) credential sources in precedence order: `--username` + `--password-stdin` (never `--password`), env `LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_USERNAME`/`LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_PASSWORD` (or `LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as a pre-issued bearer), then `$DOCKER_CONFIG/config.json` `auths` entries (base64 `auth` and plain username/password only — no credential helpers in 3.0); (2) in `fetchToken`, send HTTP Basic to the realm when credentials are present and include a hash of the identity in `bearerChallenge.cacheKey()` so anonymous and authenticated tokens never mix; (3) for registries that answer 401 with `Basic` instead of `Bearer`, retry with Basic directly; (4) redact `Authorization`, `username`, `password` in all logging and error text (extend `sanitizeProgressValue`); (5) API: add optional `registry_credentials_ref`? No — keep the API public-only in 3.0 and document it; (6) update `Short` texts, README 'Security model' and the `--all-tags` warning ('every public tag' → 'every tag'). Tests: httptest registry requiring Basic on /token, a token-cache-isolation test, and a log-redaction test.
verifier_note: Premise fully confirmed: client.go:417 `executeRequest(ctx, method, targetURL, accept, token)` only ever sets `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; fetchToken (:450-) calls `c.executeRequest(requestCtx, http.MethodGet, parsedRealm.String(), "", "")` and decodes only `token`/`access_token`; grep for Username/Password/SetBasicAuth/credential/DOCKER_CONFIG across internal/registry, scanservice and config returns nothing; scan.go:40 and root.go:41 say 'public'. The value is real, but I move it to 3.1 (the author's own fallback) for three reasons the proposal underweights: (1) most private registries that matter (ECR, GCR/Artifact Registry) authenticate through docker credential HELPERS, which the design explicitly excludes, so the 3.0 feature would cover Docker Hub/GHCR-style static logins only; (2) the egress policy (checked_ok) blocks private/loopback hosts unless allowlisted, so on-prem private registries still need a second feature; (3) the API would then carry registry credentials with no authentication of its own (PRD-16 is also 3.1). Shipping credential handling on the same RC as the module-path and schema churn dilutes the 72-hour soak. New placement: 3.1, as the headline of that minor.

title: SARIF 2.1.0 output for GitHub code scanning — IN 3.0.0 (fallback 3.1)
description: Value: high — `--format sarif` lets any GitHub Actions user upload results with `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` and get findings as code-scanning alerts with no glue code; it is the de facto integration format for gitleaks, trivy and grype. Effort m: the finding model already carries everything SARIF needs (rule id = detector, level from confidence, message = redacted value + context, `file_path`/`line_number`/`layer_digest` for locations, `fingerprint` for `partialFingerprints`). Risk: low — pure output encoder; validate against the OASIS schema in CI. Depends on PRD-07 (stable rule ids) and pairs with PRD-03's `--output`.
evidence: internal/cli/scan.go:295-301 `parseOutputFormat` accepts only `summary` and `json`. internal/findings/findings.go:82-98 public Finding fields: `detector_name`, `confidence`, `disposition`, `file_path`, `layer_digest`, `line_number`, `redacted_value`, `fingerprint`, `context_snippet`, `match_start/match_end`. No `sarif` string anywhere in README.md, CHANGELOG.md or docs/ (grep).

Locations use `artifactLocation.uri = file_path` with `uriBaseId` = image reference (files inside images are not repo paths; document that GitHub will show them as external). Wire `--format sarif`, encourage `--output results.sarif --no-save`. Validate a fixture against sarif-schema-2.1.0.json in verify.yml. Document a copy-paste Actions job in README.

One caveat for the fix: `line_number`/`file_path` are omitempty and absent for env/label/history findings (findings.go:89-92), so SARIF `locations` must be optional and `physicalLocation` emitted only for file sources; and GitHub shows non-repo `artifactLocation.uri` values as unmatched files, which the proposal already acknowledges.

title: IP-pinning transport sends CONNECT to an IP literal, so hostname-policy HTTPS proxies refuse every registry request
description: pinnedTransport.RoundTrip rewrites request.URL.Host to the first resolved IP (`request.URL.Host = net.JoinHostPort(addresses[0].IP.String(), port)`) and only then applies the configured Proxy. When HTTPS_PROXY is set, Go issues `CONNECT 1.2.3.4:443` instead of `CONNECT registry-1.docker.io:443`. Proxies that enforce destination policy by hostname (Squid dstdomain ACLs, Zscaler, this sandbox's agent proxy) reject or reset the tunnel, so layerleak cannot reach any registry in exactly the environments that rely on a proxy. Reproduced end-to-end: `LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR=<scratch> go run . scan alpine:3.20 --platform linux/amd64` fails with `perform registry request: Get "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/library/alpine/manifests/3.20": read tcp 127.0.0.1:44020->127.0.0.1:40687: read: connection reset by peer` (40687 is the proxy port), a control program using http.DefaultTransport through the same proxy gets `401 Unauthorized proto: HTTP/2.0`, and `curl --connect-to registry-1.docker.io:443:100.61.84.91:443 https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/` (emulating the IP-literal CONNECT) fails with `Recv failure: Connection reset by peer` while the hostname form returns 401. The proxy status page logged `connect_rejected ... gateway answered 403 to CONNECT (policy denial)`.
evidence: client.go:1062-1070: `request.URL.Host = net.JoinHostPort(addresses[0].IP.String(), port)`; client.go:1080-1088: `if t.base.Proxy != nil { proxyURL, proxyErr := t.base.Proxy(originalRequest) ... transport.Proxy = func(*http.Request) (*url.URL, error) { return proxyURL, nil } }`. CLI run: `perform registry request: Get "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/library/alpine/manifests/3.20": read tcp 127.0.0.1:44020->127.0.0.1:40687: read: connection reset by peer` vs control `default transport status: 401 Unauthorized proto: HTTP/2.0`.
proposed_fix: The proposed fix is right but incomplete in two respects. (a) Behind a proxy the local DNS lookup must also be skipped: validateOutboundURL (client.go:354) and pinnedTransport.RoundTrip (1054) both call resolveOutbound, which requires the registry hostname to resolve locally; proxy-only networks often cannot resolve external names, so hostname-CONNECT alone still fails with `resolve registry host ...: no such host`. When t.base.Proxy(originalRequest) returns non-nil, keep the hostname in URL.Host, skip resolveOutbound for that request (the proxy is the egress control), and still apply the allowlist/http-scheme checks. Keep calling Proxy with the original hostname request so NO_PROXY matching works. (b) Fix docs: README has no proxy guidance at all (grep 'proxy' README.md -> none) and web/docs/index.html:243-246 tells users to set LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_BASE_URL when 'forcing traffic through a proxy', which is not a proxy mechanism. Add a test with an httptest proxy asserting the CONNECT target is the hostname and that no LookupIP call happens when a proxy is selected.
verifier_note: Reproduced two ways. (1) Live: `LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR=<scratch> go run . scan alpine:3.20 --platform linux/amd64` with the sandbox HTTPS_PROXY fails `perform registry request: Get "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/library/alpine/manifests/3.20": read tcp 127.0.0.1:48040->127.0.0.1:40687: read: connection reset by peer`. (2) Offline, deterministic: a probe with an httptest fake proxy installed via base.Proxy and LookupIP returning 93.184.216.34 shows the pinned transport issues `CONNECT 93.184.216.34:443` (r.URL.Host and r.Host both the IP literal) while the stock transport control issues `CONNECT registry.example:443`. Mechanism is client.go:1070 (URL.Host rewritten to IP) + 1080-1088 (proxy applied after the rewrite); Go builds the CONNECT target from URL.Host. Kind would better be `bug` than `compat`: proxied deployments cannot scan anything. Not pre-existing-safe to ignore, but the fix depends on the policy question the auditor raised, so release_blocking=false is defensible.

title: Registry client fails behind an HTTPS proxy: pinned transport sends CONNECT to an IP literal
description: `layerleak scan alpine:3.20` fails twice (also with GODEBUG=tlsmlkem=0) with `read tcp 127.0.0.1:57704->127.0.0.1:40687: read: connection reset by peer` while a plain `http.Client{}` GET of https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/ through the same HTTPS_PROXY returns 401 and `curl` returns 401. pinnedTransport.RoundTrip resolves the host itself and rewrites `request.URL.Host = net.JoinHostPort(addresses[0].IP.String(), port)` before handing the request to an http.Transport whose Proxy is still set, so the CONNECT request names a bare IP (the proxy relay log records `ws_closed_mid_exchange 98.87.179.53:443 tunnel closed (code 1006) after 6s; 1526 B sent, 39 B received`). Proxies that enforce hostname policy, or that must do their own DNS (split-horizon/corporate egress), close the tunnel. Client-side DNS pinning is meaningless when a proxy makes the upstream connection anyway. A faithful reproduction probe (IP-literal URL + ServerName through the proxy) was denied by the sandbox, hence medium confidence.
evidence: client.go:1067-1089: `request.URL.Host = net.JoinHostPort(addresses[0].IP.String(), port)` ... `if t.base.Proxy != nil { proxyURL, proxyErr := t.base.Proxy(originalRequest) ... transport.Proxy = func(*http.Request) (*url.URL, error) { return proxyURL, nil } }`. Scan stderr: `layerleak: Error: perform registry request: Get "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/library/alpine/manifests/3.20": read tcp 127.0.0.1:48248->127.0.0.1:40687: read: connection reset by peer`. Probe `go run` with default transport: `status 401`.
proposed_fix: In pinnedTransport.RoundTrip, call t.base.Proxy(originalRequest) first; when it returns a non-nil proxy URL, keep request.URL.Host as the original hostname (skip the IP rewrite, let the proxy resolve) and only apply IP pinning for direct connections. Add a unit test with httptest CONNECT proxy asserting the CONNECT target is the hostname when a proxy is configured, and document that DNS pinning is bypassed when HTTPS_PROXY is set.

title: classifyScanError misattributes nested registry timeouts/cancellations to the API deadline (504/408)
description: The handler classifies any error satisfying `errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)` as 504 `scan_timeout` ("the scan exceeded its configured deadline") and any `context.Canceled` as 408 `scan_canceled`. But the registry client wraps every request in its own `context.WithTimeout` (LAYERLEAK_HTTP_TIMEOUT, 30 s default) and wraps the resulting `*url.Error` with `%w`; jobs.mustPreserveScanError deliberately propagates such errors unchanged. A 30 s registry stall during tag listing or manifest resolution therefore returns 504 claiming the 30-minute API deadline was hit, instead of 502 `scan_failed` (upstream). 408 is also semantically wrong for cancellation: RFC 9110 408 means the server timed out waiting for the request; a canceled request context means the client is gone (nobody receives the body) or the server is shutting down.
evidence:
internal/api/handler.go:740-743:
  case errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
      return http.StatusGatewayTimeout, "scan_timeout", "the scan exceeded its configured deadline"
  case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled):
      return http.StatusRequestTimeout, "scan_canceled", "the scan was canceled"
internal/registry/client.go:176: requestCtx, cancel := c.withRequestTimeout(ctx)
internal/registry/client.go:536: return context.WithTimeout(ctx, c.requestTimeout)
internal/registry/client.go:360: return nil, fmt.Errorf("perform registry request: %w", err)
internal/jobs/scan.go:717-718: func mustPreserveScanError(err error) bool { return errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) || ... }
proposed_fix: Change classifyScanError(err) to classifyScanError(err, scanCtx, request.Context()): return 504 scan_timeout only when errors.Is(scanCtx.Err(), context.DeadlineExceeded); treat cancellation only when request.Context().Err()!=nil (client gone: log and write nothing useful, or 503 server_shutting_down when draining per API-04); everything else including nested DeadlineExceeded/Canceled becomes 502 scan_failed (optionally an additive `registry_timeout` code). Keep TestHandleScanEnforcesTimeout passing (contextScanner returns ctx.Err() after scanCtx expires, so it still maps to 504) and add the nested-deadline unit test. Update openapi.yaml 408/504 descriptions accordingly.
verifier_note: Reproduced against the real handler in a scratch copy: a scanner returning `&scanservice.Error{Err: fmt.Errorf("perform registry request: %w", context.DeadlineExceeded)}` while the request context was alive (ctx.Err()==nil) produced 504 scan_timeout. The chain is realistic: registry/client.go:176,536 wrap each request in context.WithTimeout(requestTimeout); client.go:360 wraps with %w; jobs/scan.go:250 and :319 deliberately return such errors unchanged via mustPreserveScanError (scan.go:717). Also, the registry retry loop (client.go:419-439) keeps the final attempt's error, so a stalled registry still surfaces DeadlineExceeded. 408 for cancellation is a misuse per RFC 9110 §15.5.9.

title: Graceful shutdown cannot drain a 30-minute scan: no context cancellation, readiness stays 200, scan lost, exit 1
description: On SIGTERM, `server.Shutdown` gets a 30 s deadline (LAYERLEAK_API_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT) while scans may run 30 m. Shutdown closes listeners and waits for idle connections but, per net/http docs, never cancels in-flight request contexts, so the scan keeps running; after 30 s Shutdown returns ctx error, Run returns it, `defer store.Close()` runs, main exits 1 and the client gets a connection reset with nothing persisted. During those 30 s `/readyz` still returns 200 so load balancers keep routing to a process that has closed its listener. Docker's default stop grace is 10 s, so in Compose the process is usually SIGKILLed anyway.
proposed_fix: (1) Add a draining flag set via server.RegisterOnShutdown (or before calling Shutdown) that makes /readyz return 503 not_ready; sleep a configurable pre-stop delay before Shutdown so orchestrators deprioritise the pod. (2) Give the handler a base context (http.Server.BaseContext) that is cancelled when draining starts so in-flight scans abort promptly, mapping the result to 503 server_shutting_down (together with API-03). (3) For scans that already completed, persist with context.WithoutCancel + DatabaseWriteTimeout (see API-23) instead of discarding. (4) Add stop_grace_period >= LAYERLEAK_API_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT to docker-compose.yml and document the relationship in README.md:258. (5) Extract server construction from Run() so a test can drive shutdown with a fake signal.
verifier_note: run.go:94-98 gives Shutdown a 30 s budget (config.go:97) versus a 30 m scan budget (config.go:73); handler.go:329 derives scanCtx only from request.Context(); net/http Shutdown never cancels handler contexts; docker-compose.yml has no stop_grace_period (Docker default 10 s). One correction to the description: Shutdown closes the listener immediately, so new /readyz probes get connection refused rather than 200 — the real gap is the absence of a pre-stop drain window (readyz->503 while still serving) and any way to stop or persist in-flight scans. Severity stands.

title: No access logging or metrics: requests are invisible unless they fail
description: The middleware sets headers and recovers panics but logs nothing per request. Only failures log (error_type, code, status, request_id). Operators cannot see request volume, latency, which routes are hit, or correlate an X-Request-ID with a route and status. There is no /metrics endpoint.

Optionally expose Prometheus metrics on a separate admin listener (LAYERLEAK_API_METRICS_ADDR) so they are not reachable from the public API port.

title: Add an asynchronous scan-job model (202 Accepted + polling) alongside the 30-minute synchronous POST
description: POST /api/v1/scans holds one HTTP request open for up to 30 minutes and sends no bytes until the end. Typical intermediaries (nginx proxy_read_timeout 60 s, AWS ALB/GCP LB idle 60 s, Cloudflare 100 s) will drop it. When the client disconnects, Go cancels request.Context(), the scan aborts, and scanservice refuses to persist (ctx.Err() != nil), so all work is lost and the 408 body is written to a dead socket. A 202 model removes all three problems and is purely additive within /api/v1.

internal/api/handler.go:329: scanCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(request.Context(), h.options.ScanTimeout)
internal/scanservice/service.go:118-124:
  if ctx != nil && ctx.Err() != nil { ... return outcome, wrapScanError(ctx.Err()) }
web/docs/openapi.yaml:72: summary: Run and persist a synchronous image scan
proposed_fix: As proposed. Also update openapi.yaml:54 and README.md:330 if migration 0005 changes the exact-schema readiness version, and document proxy idle-timeout caveats for the synchronous endpoint. Consider shipping API-23 (detached save context) first as the cheap fix for the lost-result half of this problem.

HTTP/1 client disconnect cancels the request context once the body is consumed, so a dropped 30-minute POST loses all work. The proposed 202 model is additive within /api/v1.

title: Offer opt-in bearer-token authentication for /api/v1
description: The API triggers outbound registry traffic and 30-minute CPU/network work per request with no authentication; docs say to put it behind a gateway. An opt-in shared-token mode is cheap, additive, and removes the most common misconfiguration (binding 0.0.0.0 without a proxy, which docker-compose.yml already does inside the container network).
evidence:
web/docs/openapi.yaml:8-9: The API has no built-in authentication or authorization. Deploy it only on a private network or behind an authenticated gateway.
README.md:45-47 same statement; docker-compose.yml:24: LAYERLEAK_API_ADDR: 0.0.0.0:8080
proposed_fix: Add `LAYERLEAK_API_BEARER_TOKENS` (comma-separated; empty = disabled, current behaviour). Middleware: parse `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, compare with `crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` against each configured token (or store SHA-256 of tokens), on failure return 401 JSON `{error:{code:"unauthorized"}}` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="layerleak"`. Exempt /health and /livez; make /readyz exemption configurable. Never log tokens. Log a startup warning when auth is disabled and the address is not loopback. Document in openapi.yaml with `securitySchemes: bearerAuth` and per-operation `security`. Keep the gateway recommendation; this is defence in depth, not RBAC.

Still the single biggest foot-gun; the constant-time shared-token design is sound and additive.

title: Handler/runtime test gaps: not-found scan, storage errors, panic, HEAD/OPTIONS, real-server long scan and disconnect, Run() shutdown, healthcheck success path

title: CI verifies with Go 1.25.13 (EOL, not even the last 1.25 patch) while the shipped container is compiled with Go 1.27.1
description: Every setup-go step uses go-version-file, so tests, race tests, govulncheck and the license audit run on Go 1.25.13. The Dockerfile builds the release image with golang:1.27.1, so the vulnerability gate and tests exercise a different compiler/runtime than the artifact that ships, and the README badge advertises 'Go 1.25.13+'.

title: post-release assumes proxy.golang.org publishes within five minutes and uses a substring version check
description: Both proxy loops allow 30 x 10 s = 5 minutes inside a 15-minute job. proxy.golang.org documents that if the module version was requested before the tag was pushed (which the RC acceptance/README commands make likely for `@latest`), 'it may take up to 30 minutes for the mirror's cache to expire'. A cache miss turns a successful publication into a failed run that must be re-run (Re-run failed jobs works, but RELEASING does not say so). The version assertion `grep -F "${RELEASE_VERSION}"` is a substring match, so `v3.0.0` also accepts `v3.0.0-rc.1` output.
evidence: :1164 `for attempt in {1..30}; do ... sleep 10`; :1169 `echo "The Go proxy did not publish ${RELEASE_VERSION} within five minutes."`; :1111 `timeout-minutes: 15`; :1174 `"${install_bin}/layerleak" --version | grep -F "${RELEASE_VERSION}"`; proxy.golang.org: 'it may take up to 30 minutes for the mirror's cache to expire and fresh data about the version to become available'.
proposed_fix: Raise the `@latest` loop to ~35 minutes (e.g. 70 x 30 s) and the job timeout to 45; keep the explicit-version loop shorter since explicit fetches are served within a minute. Replace the substring check with an exact comparison, e.g. `test "$("${install_bin}/layerleak" --version | awk '{print $NF}')" = "${RELEASE_VERSION}"`. Document in RELEASING.md 'Failure and recovery' that a post-release failure is retried with 'Re-run failed jobs' without re-approval of publication.
verifier_note: Lines 1164-1173 and 1179-1189 are 30x10 s loops inside a 15-minute job; proxy.golang.org's FAQ (fetched) states 'if someone requested the version before the tag was pushed, it may take up to 30 minutes for the mirror's cache to expire'. `grep -F` at 1174 is a substring match. I ran `go run . --version` -> `layerleak version dev`, so the proposed `awk '{print $NF}'` exact comparison matches the real output format, and internal/cli/version.go falls back to debug.ReadBuildInfo Main.Version for `go install module@version` binaries, so the installed binary will print the tag.

title: Release ships only the API container; add signed, attested prebuilt CLI binaries (and plan a Homebrew tap and CLI image)
description: The CLI is `go install` only. The code cross-compiles cleanly for darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, windows/amd64, windows/arm64 and linux/arm64 (verified locally), so a binary matrix is feasible. A plain `go build` matrix is preferable to goreleaser here: goreleaser would introduce an unreviewed, unpinned tool into a workflow whose policy is checksum-pinned reviewed tools, and it wants to own release creation, which conflicts with the protected publish job and immutable releases. Homebrew and a CLI image need extra design because the workflow deliberately uses only GITHUB_TOKEN and a single IMAGE_NAME.
evidence: `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -o /dev/null .` -> rc=0 (same for darwin/amd64, windows/amd64, windows/arm64, linux/arm64); publish job downloads `pattern: release-*` (:950) and attaches `release-assets/*` (:1080); internal/cli/root.go:35-36 `// Version is the build-time version string, set via -ldflags. var Version = "dev"`; RELEASING.md 'The workflow uses only `GITHUB_TOKEN` and GitHub's OIDC token.'
proposed_fix: Add a `build-cli` job after `supply-chain` and before `publish` (needs: validate, verify): checkout source_sha, setup-go from go.mod, matrix over 6 GOOS/GOARCH pairs, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(date -d "${source_date}" +%s) CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags "-s -w -X github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3/internal/cli.Version=${RELEASE_VERSION}" -o dist/layerleak_${RELEASE_VERSION}_${GOOS}_${GOARCH}[.exe]`, tar.gz/zip, `sha256sum > cli-SHA256SUMS`, `actions/attest` with `subject-checksums: cli-SHA256SUMS` (build provenance) and `cosign sign-blob --yes --bundle <file>.sigstore.json` for each archive; upload as artifact `release-cli` so the existing `release-*` download and SHA256SUMS steps include it. In post-release, rebuild one target in a clean module cache and `cmp` digests (reproducibility) and `cosign verify-blob --bundle ... --certificate-identity <workflow identity>`. Homebrew: create `brumbelow/homebrew-tap` with a formula pointing at the release archives; update it from a workflow inside the tap repo triggered on `release: published` via the tap's own token (keeps this repo's GITHUB_TOKEN-only policy) or document `brew install go && go install .../v3@latest` as the interim path. CLI image: add a `cli` stage in the Dockerfile (scratch + CA certs + layerleak, USER 10001) published as `ghcr.io/brumbelow/layerleak-cli`; because the workflow is single-image throughout (IMAGE_NAME env, digest outputs, manifest schema_version 1), plan this as a 3.1 change with a matrix over image names and `schema_version: 2` in release-manifest.json.
verifier_note: Reproduced cross-compiles for darwin/arm64 and windows/amd64 (`go build -trimpath -o /dev/null .` rc=0). internal/cli/root.go:35-36 `var Version = "dev"` matches the proposed -X path. publish downloads `pattern: release-*` (line 950) so a `release-cli` artifact flows into SHA256SUMS and `gh release create release-assets/*` without further changes. Reasoning about goreleaser vs the checksum-pinned policy is sound.

title: Go 1.25 is out of support; CI tests on 1.25.13 while the image ships 1.27.1 and docs promise 1.25.13+
description: go.mod declares `go 1.25.13` with no toolchain directive. All workflows (verify.yml lines 33/90/148/209/373, codacy.yml:109, container-release.yml:1135) use `go-version-file: go.mod`, so every test, race, lint, license and CLI-install job runs Go 1.25.13. `curl https://go.dev/dl/?mode=json` today returns only go1.27.1 and go1.26.8, i.e. Go 1.25 no longer receives security fixes. The Dockerfile builds the published binaries with `golang:1.27.1-bookworm`, so the toolchain that is tested is never the toolchain that ships. README badge (line 5), README line 51, CONTRIBUTING.md:9 and web/docs/index.html:79 all state a 1.25.13 minimum, which at 3.0.0 would advertise an unsupported floor.
evidence: go.mod:3 `go 1.25.13`; Dockerfile:5 `FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM golang:1.27.1-bookworm@sha256:648f...`; verify.yml:33 `go-version-file: go.mod`; `go version` -> go1.25.13; go.dev/dl?mode=json -> ['go1.27.1', 'go1.26.8']; README.md:51 `Layerleak requires Go 1.25.13 or newer.`; setup-go README: "If the toolchain directive is present, its version is used"
proposed_fix: Bump go.mod to `go 1.26.0` plus `toolchain go1.27.1` (or simply `go 1.27.1` if a 1.27 floor is acceptable) and update README.md:5/51, CONTRIBUTING.md:9, web/docs/index.html:79. Do NOT rely on 'let Dependabot move both together': Dependabot's gomod ecosystem does not update the `go`/`toolchain` directives, only the Dockerfile golang image, so they will drift again. Add a consistency gate instead, e.g. in verify.yml's quality job or scripts/release-preflight.py: `test "go$(awk '$1=="toolchain"{sub(/^go/,"",$2);print $2}' go.mod)" = "$(sed -n 's/^FROM .*golang:\([0-9.]*\)-.*/go\1/p' Dockerfile)"`. Re-run govulncheck after the bump.
verifier_note: Facts confirmed: go.mod:3 `go 1.25.13` with no toolchain line; verify.yml:33/90/148/209/373, codacy.yml:109 and container-release.yml:1135 all use `go-version-file: go.mod` with setup-go v7; `go version` here is go1.25.13; `curl https://go.dev/dl/?mode=json` returns ['go1.27.1','go1.26.8']; Dockerfile:5 builds with golang:1.27.1-bookworm; README.md:5/51, CONTRIBUTING.md:9, web/docs/index.html:79 all say 1.25.13. setup-go's README confirms 'If the toolchain directive is present, its version is used'. Further evidence of drift: running govulncheck required `go run golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest`, which printed 'golang.org/x/vuln@v1.8.0 requires go >= 1.26.0; switching to go1.26.8'. However this is not a bug, a security hole or a false statement: the shipped image is already built on a supported toolchain and 'Go 1.25.13 or newer' is a floor, not a claim about support. It is a CI/toolchain hygiene mismatch (tests never run on the toolchain that ships) that should be fixed before v3.0.0-rc.1 because the rc freezes the toolchain set, but it is not release-blocking in the strict sense of rule 4.

title: .env.example ships a live default-credential DSN; the documented quickstart exports it and makes every CLI scan exit 1 without local Postgres
description: README.md:186-195 tells users to `cp .env.example .env; set -a; . ./.env; set +a` before running Layerleak. .env.example line 65 sets `LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/layerleak?sslmode=disable` (README table says the default is empty). internal/cli/storage.go opens a Postgres store whenever DatabaseURL is non-empty and NewPostgresStore pings at startup, so on any machine without a local PostgreSQL using the `postgres:postgres` superuser credentials every `layerleak scan` fails persistence, which README:163 documents as exit code 1 with `storage_unavailable`. It also normalizes hard-coded superuser credentials in a security tool's example. `LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR=findings` (line 12) likewise overrides the documented `auto` default (README:206).
evidence: .env.example:65 `LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/layerleak?sslmode=disable`; internal/cli/storage.go:11-15 `if strings.TrimSpace(cfg.DatabaseURL) == "" { return storage.NewNoopStore(), nil } return storage.NewPostgresStore(...)`; internal/storage/postgres.go:50-53 `if err := db.PingContext(ctx); err != nil { ... return nil, fmt.Errorf("ping postgres: %w", err) }`; README.md:163 `A database-save failure also returns exit code `1``
proposed_fix: Set `LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_URL=` (empty) in .env.example with a commented example using a non-superuser role, leave `LAYERLEAK_MIGRATIONS_DIR=` empty with a comment that the container default is /app/migrations and checkouts should use `$PWD/migrations`, and keep `LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR=findings` or blank (equivalent). Mirror in web/docs/index.html:196/226. Add a test that parses .env.example, applies it with t.Setenv and asserts Load() equals the no-env defaults (CFG-16).
verifier_note: README.md:186-195 instructs `cp .env.example .env; set -a; . ./.env; set +a` as THE way to configure a checkout; .env.example:65 then exports `LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/layerleak?sslmode=disable`; internal/cli/storage.go:11-15 opens a Postgres store whenever DatabaseURL is non-empty and postgres.go:50-53 pings at construction. The failure mode is slightly different from the description: scan.go:109-118 calls openStore before the scan starts and returns the error, so the CLI aborts immediately (no scan, no artifacts) rather than scanning and recording `storage_unavailable` as README:163 describes for save-time failures. The LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR=findings sub-claim is moot: results.go:181-199 resolves a relative value against the repo root, which is exactly the unset default. Additional drift in the same file: .env.example:72 `LAYERLEAK_MIGRATIONS_DIR=/app/migrations` is a container path, so a sourced .env breaks `go run ./cmd/migrate` from a checkout unless the user re-exports it as README:278 does.
