No code warns about cleartext (grep for sslmode in *.go returns nothing).

title: Database password is only accepted embedded in the URL; lib/pq already honors PGPASSWORD/PGPASSFILE, enabling secrets-friendly compose
description: Compose interpolates `${LAYERLEAK_DB_PASSWORD}` into three URLs unescaped (lines 44, 96, 121), so reserved characters break the DSN (README:429-430 admits this) and the password is visible in `docker inspect` of three containers plus the db container's POSTGRES_PASSWORD. lib/pq v1.12.3's connector reads PGPASSWORD and PGPASSFILE for fields absent from the DSN, so the password can be dropped from the URL today, and a `_FILE`/PGPASSFILE path allows Docker/Compose secrets and Kubernetes secret mounts without touching config.go.
evidence: docker-compose.yml:44 `LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_URL: postgres://${LAYERLEAK_DB_USER:-layerleak}:${LAYERLEAK_DB_PASSWORD:?set LAYERLEAK_DB_PASSWORD in .env}@db:5432/...`; README.md:429-430 `If a database password contains reserved URL characters, percent-encode it`; $GOMODCACHE/github.com/lib/pq@v1.12.3/connector.go:286 `Password string `postgres:"password" env:"PGPASSWORD"``, :291 `Passfile string `postgres:"passfile" env:"PGPASSFILE"``
proposed_fix: In compose, set `LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_URL: postgres://${LAYERLEAK_DB_USER}@db:5432/${LAYERLEAK_DB_NAME}?sslmode=disable` plus `PGPASSWORD: ${LAYERLEAK_DB_PASSWORD}` (or better, a compose `secrets:` entry mounted at /run/secrets/db_password with `PGPASSFILE`-style handling and `POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE` for the db service). Document PGPASSWORD/PGPASSFILE support in the README table. For 3.0.0 consider adding `LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_URL_FILE` in config.go for parity with other secret-file conventions.
verifier_note: Verified in the module cache: $GOMODCACHE/github.com/lib/pq@v1.12.3/connector.go:286 `Password string \`postgres:"password" env:"PGPASSWORD"\`` and :291 `Passfile string \`postgres:"passfile" env:"PGPASSFILE"\``. Both NewPostgresStore (postgres.go:38) and RunMigrations (migrate.go:74) open via sql.Open("postgres", url) so the env fallback applies to api, migrate and purge. storage.PostgresConfig.Validate (storage.go:220-243) requires scheme, host and database name but not a password, so a password-less URL passes validation. compose:44/96/121 interpolate the password unescaped three times as described; README:429-430 confirms the percent-encoding caveat.

title: Web docs claim in-toto attestation manifests are skipped; an index entry with that media type is an integrity error that aborts the whole scan
description: web/docs/index.html says "Attestation and provenance manifests (for example application/vnd.in-toto+json) are skipped instead of counted as platform scan failures." The code only skips descriptors whose media type is an image manifest AND carry the vnd.docker.reference.type=attestation-manifest annotation, a non-empty artifactType, or platform unknown/unknown (document.go IsAttestationDescriptor:301-316). A descriptor whose mediaType is application/vnd.in-toto+json fails IsManifestMediaType, so ValidateImageIndex (integrity.go:155) returns IntegrityMediaTypeMismatch; scanner/scan.go:1014 calls ValidateDocument on the root and scan.go:287 treats any IntegrityError as fatal for all remaining platforms, and --allow-partial cannot accept it. The DOC auditor raised this as an open question; nobody confirmed it. Confirmed with a scratch-copy probe test.
evidence: Probe (scratch copy, internal/manifest): ValidateImageIndex error: descriptor_media_type_mismatch for "manifest[1]": expected "supported OCI media type", got "application/vnd.in-toto+json". Code: document.go:302 `if !IsManifestMediaType(descriptor.MediaType) { return false }`; scan.go:287 `if limits.IsExceeded(err) || manifest.IsIntegrityError(err) || ...  { finalizeResult(...); return result, err }`.
proposed_fix: Either (a) make the docs true: in IsAttestationDescriptor/ValidateImageIndex treat descriptors with non-image media types (application/vnd.in-toto+json, application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json, artifact manifests) as skippable with a `manifest_skipped` diagnostic instead of an IntegrityError (aligns with REG-11), or (b) rewrite the sentence to say only BuildKit attestation-manifest entries (annotation vnd.docker.reference.type=attestation-manifest, artifactType, or unknown/unknown platform) are skipped and that any other non-image index entry fails the scan. Add a document_test.go case for an in-toto media-type descriptor either way.

title: Compose api service has no stop_grace_period, so Docker SIGKILLs the API after 10 s while LAYERLEAK_API_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT defaults to 30 s
description: api.Run handles SIGTERM via signal.NotifyContext and calls server.Shutdown with cfg.APIShutdownTimeout (default 30s, run.go:78-99). `docker compose stop/down` and `docker stop` send SIGTERM and then SIGKILL after the default 10-second grace period. docker-compose.yml sets LAYERLEAK_API_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT but no stop_grace_period, so in the shipped deployment the graceful drain is cut off at 10 s regardless of the configured 30 s, and an in-flight scan's SaveScan transaction is killed mid-flight. API-04 analysed Shutdown itself but no auditor checked the orchestrator grace period against it; README's deploy section does not mention terminationGracePeriodSeconds for Kubernetes either.
evidence: docker-compose.yml:35 `LAYERLEAK_API_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT: ${LAYERLEAK_API_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT:-30s}`; `grep -n stop_grace_period docker-compose.yml` -> no match; run.go:93-96 `shutdownCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), cfg.APIShutdownTimeout); ... server.Shutdown(shutdownCtx)`.
proposed_fix: Add `stop_grace_period: 35s` (shutdown timeout + margin, or `${LAYERLEAK_API_STOP_GRACE:-35s}`) to the api service in docker-compose.yml, and add one sentence to README's deployment section: the orchestrator's termination grace period must exceed LAYERLEAK_API_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT (Kubernetes terminationGracePeriodSeconds, docker stop -t). Consider the same for the migrate/purge tool services.

title: Several proposed detector fixes change finding fingerprints, which are the database identity (UNIQUE(manifest_digest, fingerprint)); no auditor assessed the upgrade impact
description: DET-03 (value-only spans for env/label findings), DET-07 and DET-20 (capture-boundary fixes), DET-12 (full GitLab token), DET-26/PRD-07 (detector renames) and especially DET-09 (keyed HMAC fingerprints) all change the fingerprint or detector_name emitted for the same secret. findings are keyed by UNIQUE (manifest_digest, fingerprint) and finding_occurrences by a 15-column identity that includes detector_name, so after upgrading to 3.0.0 a rescan of an already-recorded image inserts a second findings row for the same secret while the legacy row keeps stale first_seen/last_seen and remains counted by the API list endpoints and scan_runs.unique_fingerprints. Raw values are not retained by default, so no migration can recompute old fingerprints. The DET, DB and PRD areas each touched part of this (DET open question on HMAC, DB open question on 0005, PRD-13 baseline keyed by fingerprint) but no finding states the operator-visible consequence or the required CHANGELOG/UPGRADING text.
evidence: migrations/0001_initial.up.sql:59-64 `fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL, ... UNIQUE (manifest_digest, fingerprint)`; migrations/0003_scan_runs.up.sql:20 `unique_fingerprints INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`; DET-03/DET-09/DET-12/DET-26 and PRD-07/PRD-13 titles in the area digests.
proposed_fix: Before the RC decide the fingerprint contract for v3: (1) keep the unsalted sha256-of-value fingerprint (stable across installs, needed by PRD-13 baseline files and PRD-09 SARIF partialFingerprints) and reject DET-09's per-database HMAC, or adopt HMAC and accept that baselines are per-install; (2) add a `fingerprint_version` (or `detector_schema_version`) column in a 0005 migration so old and new rows are distinguishable, and have the API/CLI mark legacy rows; (3) write the UPGRADING/CHANGELOG paragraph: 'Finding identities for env/label/metadata findings and the listed detectors change in 3.0.0; historical rows are retained and a rescan creates new rows.' Also ensure the detector rename table (PRD-07) is applied to finding_occurrences.detector_name by migration or read-time mapping, not left split.

title: context_snippet leaks undetected repeats of a matched secret inside the ±24-byte window
description: contextSnippet redacts only detector spans (n.spans, built from matches). exactValueSpans (line 588) — which redacts every textual occurrence of a match value — is applied only to provenance (file path / metadata key) in sanitizedProvenance, never to content. Any second copy of the secret that no detector matched (context-requiring detectors only match assignment positions; e.g. `token: X X`, CSV columns, `KEY=X # was X`) is printed in clear up to 24 bytes. The 'redacted context only' promise in openapi.yaml (`context_snippet: description: Redacted context only.`) is therefore not met.
evidence: Probe with Default() then NewDetailedNormalizer: content `token: Xk9fL2mQ8vR4tY7wZ1aB3cD5 Xk9fL2mQ8vR4tY7wZ1aB3cD5` -> matches: 1 (`keyword_entropy [7:31]`); output `context_snippet="token: [REDACTED] Xk9fL2mQ8vR4tY7wZ1aB3cD"` — 23 of the 24 secret characters visible. Code: findings.go:381-399 only consults `n.spans`; findings.go:564-565 `spans := mergeSensitiveSpans(value, provenanceMatches); spans = append(spans, exactValueSpans(value, contentMatches)...)` exists only in sanitizedProvenance.
proposed_fix: As proposed: merge exactValueSpans(input.Content, matches) into normalizer.spans in NewDetailedNormalizerWithProvenance (dedupe by value; skip values shorter than ~8 bytes to avoid over-redaction). Add the property test.
verifier_note: Reproduced: 'token: X X' => matches=1, context_snippet="token: [REDACTED] Xk9fL2mQ8vR4tY7wZ1aB3cD" (23/24 chars); 'DB_PASSWORD="X" # X' => snippet shows 20 chars of the repeat; a copy on the next line also leaks 22 chars. The leak is real and contradicts openapi 'Redacted context only', but it requires an undetected second copy of the same value within 24 bytes of a context-gated match (self-identifying tokens are matched everywhere), so medium rather than high. Still cheap and appropriate to fix before 3.0.0.

title: basic_auth_url host class swallows trailing delimiters: single-line JSON is missed and quoting junk pollutes value/fingerprint
description: `https?://[^/\s:@]+:[^/\s@]+@[^/\s]+` lets the host consume `"}`, `",`, `')`, `';`. Go's url.Parse rejects `}` (and `\`, `|`) in a host, so looksLikeBasicAuthURL returns false and compact JSON like `{"registry":"https://u:p@host"}` yields no finding. When the trailing characters are accepted by url.Parse (`"` `,` `'` `)` `;` are allowed) they become part of Match.Value, so the same URL gets a different fingerprint depending on surrounding quoting and redacted_value ends with the junk.
evidence: Probe: `basic auth url in single-line JSON ({"registry":"https://deploy:Sup3rS3cretPw@registry.internal"}) => <none>`; `followed by comma quote => basic_auth_url[15:63]="https://deploy:Sup3rS3cretPw@registry.internal\","`; `followed by paren => ...registry.internal')`; `followed by semicolon => ...registry.internal';`; `bare => [0:46]` (clean). Code: detectors.go:86 and looksLikeBasicAuthURL lines 565-588 (`parsed, err := url.Parse(value); if err != nil { return false }`).
proposed_fix: Restrict host to [A-Za-z0-9.\-_~%\[\]:]+ and exclude quotes from user/password classes as proposed; make the scheme case-insensitive ((?i:https?)) and lower-case it before looksLikeBasicAuthURL's scheme check; add compact-JSON and quoted YAML fixtures.
verifier_note: Probe: {"registry":"https://deploy:Sup3rS3cretPw@registry.internal"} => <none> (Go url.Parse rejects '}' in host); followed by '",' => basic_auth_url value ends with '",' (fingerprint differs from the bare URL); bare and '/path' forms are clean. Also HTTPS:// (uppercase scheme) => <none>.

title: Fingerprint is an unsalted SHA-256 of the raw secret, published in JSON/API/DB — an offline verification oracle for low-entropy secrets
description: `Fingerprint(value) = hex(sha256(value))` is exposed in every finding (openapi `fingerprint`), stored in `findings.fingerprint`, and used as the cross-run identity. Anyone with read access to findings can confirm a guessed secret, and short passwords (netrc/pypirc ≥4 chars, basic-auth passwords) can be recovered by dictionary/brute force even from 'redacted' output; DET-08 makes this worse. A 3.0 release is the natural point to change fingerprint semantics because every fingerprint changes.
evidence: findings.go:328-331 `func Fingerprint(value string) string { sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(value)); return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]) }`; web/docs/openapi.yaml:849 `fingerprint: type: string`; storage upserts by fingerprint (internal/storage/postgres.go:396-457 region). README/openapi make no statement that fingerprints are keyed.
proposed_fix: If adopting HMAC, keep cross-run stability per database via a stored key; at minimum document the oracle and truncate to 128 bits. Either path requires a 3.0.0 compatibility note since every fingerprint changes.
verifier_note: findings.go:328-331 is a plain sha256 of the raw value; it is exposed in JSON/API and used as the DB identity (storage upsert by fingerprint). For low-entropy passwords this is an unsalted hash published alongside a partial reveal (DET-08). Keyed fingerprints are a design change with real costs (cross-database comparability, key management), so medium and not blocking is right.

title: Context regexes (aws_secret_access_key, twilio_auth_token, heroku, snyk) do not allow a closing quote between key and separator, so JSON `"key": "value"` is missed
description: Patterns of the form `key\s*(?:=|:|=>)\s*["']?(value)` accept a quote before the value but not after the key. In JSON (`{"aws_secret_access_key": "wJalr..."}`) the character after the key is `"`, so the regex fails; with DET-02 also failing, an AWS secret key in a JSON/YAML-quoted-key config produces no finding at all.
evidence: Probe: `aws secret in JSON quoted key => <none>`, `aws secret in yaml quoted key ("aws_secret_access_key": wJalr...) => <none>`, `aws secret yaml plain => aws_secret_access_key[23:63]`; `twilio auth token JSON quoted key => <none>` vs yaml plain detected; `snyk token JSON quoted key => <none>`; `heroku uuid quoted json => <none>`. Code: detectors.go:74 `(?i)(?:aws[_-]?secret[_-]?access[_-]?key|secret[_-]?access[_-]?key)\s*(?:=|:|=>)\s*["']?([A-Za-z0-9/+=]{40})`, :110 twilio, structured.go:29 and :38 `\b...(?:key|token)\b\s*(?:=|:|=>)\s*["']?(uuid)\b`.
proposed_fix: As proposed; build the four patterns from one helper so they stay consistent and add a trailing boundary.
verifier_note: Probe: {"aws_secret_access_key": "wJalr..."} => <none>; YAML plain => aws_secret_access_key[23:63]; {"heroku_api_key": "<uuid>"} => <none>. Patterns at detectors.go:74, :110 and structured.go:29/:38 have no ["']? after the key.

title: pem_private_key misses PGP private key blocks and any key without an END marker
description: The regex requires the literal `PRIVATE KEY-----` right after the type words, so `-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----` never matches, and it requires a matching END marker, so a key truncated by LAYERLEAK_MAX_FILE_BYTES (1 MiB default), a partially written file, or a lone header in a log/script is not reported. gitleaks' rule accepts `PRIVATE KEY(?: BLOCK)?`.
evidence: Probe: `PGP private key block => <none>`; `truncated PEM (no END) => <none>`; `private key header only (BEGIN marker) => <none>`; OpenSSH/EC/RSA/JSON-escaped GCP keys detected. Code: detectors.go:67 `(?s)-----BEGIN [A-Z0-9 ]*PRIVATE KEY-----.*?-----END [A-Z0-9 ]*PRIVATE KEY-----`.
proposed_fix: As proposed.
verifier_note: Probe: '-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----...END...' => <none>; truncated RSA PEM without END => <none>. detectors.go:67 requires 'PRIVATE KEY-----' immediately and a matching END.

title: GitLab routable PATs are captured only up to the first '.', leaving the version/length/CRC tail in plaintext and fingerprinting a partial token
description: GitLab ≥17.7 issues routable tokens `glpat-<payload 27–300 base64url>.<2 base36 version>.<2 base36 length + 7 base36 CRC>` (GitLab MR 'Make PersonalAccessToken#token routable'; GitLab's own detector `glpat-[0-9a-zA-Z_-]{27,300}\.[0-9a-z]{2}[0-9a-z]{7}\b`). The rule `\bglpat-[A-Za-z0-9\-_]{20,}\b` stops at the '.', so Match.Value omits the tail, context_snippet shows `[REDACTED].01.0w1bd93a1`, and the fingerprint is of a prefix rather than the token.
evidence: Probe: `gitlab routable pat (glpat-<redacted>) => gitlab_token[13:39]="glpat-<redacted>"` (tail `.01.0w1bd93a1` excluded). Code detectors.go:69.
proposed_fix: \bglpat-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,300}(?:\.[0-9a-z]{2}\.[0-9a-z]{9})?\b (2-char base36 version, then 2-char base36 length + 7-char CRC). Apply the same optional tail to the other gl*- rules GitLab routes, and add a routable-token fixture asserting the full value is redacted.
verifier_note: Probe: glpat-<redacted> => gitlab_token[13:39] (tail excluded). GitLab source lib/authn/token_field/generator/routable_token.rb assembles "#{prefix}#{base64_payload}.#{token_version}.#{base64_payload_length}" + 7-char CRC, i.e. TWO dots with 2 chars after the first and 2+7=9 chars after the second. The auditor's proposed tail '\.[0-9a-z]{2}\.[0-9a-z]{7}' is wrong (7 instead of 9), and the gitleaks one-dot regex they cited disagrees with GitLab's own generator.

title: Suppression heuristics hide real secrets: placeholder markers judged on whole lines/paths, strong 'spec/e2e/mock/stubs' path markers, 'EXAMPLE' substring on whole URL values
description: ExampleReason calls hasPlaceholderMarkerSignal(filePath, key, line, value): any of 21 markers anywhere in the source line (including trailing comments) or in the file path flips a real secret to disposition=example. TestPathReason treats `spec`, `specs`, `e2e`, `acceptance`, `stubs`, `mock`, `mocks`, `fixture` as decisive; OpenAPI `spec/` directories, RPM `SPECS/`, and e2e configs ship in production images. hasKnownDummyValueSignal applies `strings.Contains(upper, "EXAMPLE")` to the whole matched value, so URL-shaped values with 'example' in the hostname are suppressed. Suppressed findings do not count toward total_findings or exit code 2 and are hidden by default in the API (`?disposition` defaults to actionable), so these are effective false negatives.
evidence: Classify probe (github_token, real-shaped value): `/app/.env "GH_TOKEN=ghp_... # TODO replace this with vault lookup" => example/placeholder_marker`; `... # dummy account for CI => example/placeholder_marker`; `/app/node_modules/@faker-js/faker/.npmrc => example/placeholder_marker`; `/app/config/spec/production.yaml => example/test_path`; `/usr/src/packages/SPECS/app.env => example/test_path`; `/app/e2e/prod.env => example/test_path`; basic_auth_url value `https://deploy:RealPassw0rd@git.examplecorp.internal/repo.git => example/known_dummy_value`. Code: policy.go:55 `if hasPlaceholderMarkerSignal(filePath, key, line, value)`, :84-85 marker list, :191 `if strings.Contains(upper, "EXAMPLE")`.
proposed_fix: As proposed; additionally treat '.template' as a weak signal rather than decisive, since *.conf.template files are shipped in production images.
verifier_note: ExampleReason probes: '/app/.env' line with '# TODO replace this with vault lookup' => placeholder_marker; '/app/node_modules/@faker-js/faker/.npmrc' => placeholder_marker ('fake' in path); '/app/config/spec/production.yaml', '/usr/src/packages/SPECS/app.env', '/app/e2e/prod.env' => test_path; basic_auth_url value with host git.examplecorp.internal => known_dummy_value; also '/etc/nginx/nginx.conf.template' => example_path (envsubst templates are common in production images). Suppressed findings do not count toward total_findings/exit 2.

title: No format/negative/property coverage that would have caught DET-01..08; corpus covers ~15 of 80 detectors; brittle Len()==80 assertion
description: detectors_test.go has one positive string per detector and a few negatives; there is no unquoted .env `KEY=VALUE` case, no pretty-JSON/quoted-YAML/TOML case, no CRLF/BOM/quoted structured-parser case, no realistic age key, no PGP/truncated PEM, no throughput benchmark; findings_test.go has no short-value Redact test and no 'secret never appears in any public field' property test (would have caught DET-04); the corpus has 31 fixtures for 80 detectors and no false-positive fixtures (sha256 digests, UUID request IDs, base64 images). `TestDefaultSetContainsOnlyNativeRules` hard-codes `Len() != 80`.

Every DET-01..08 probe in this verification would have failed against a reasonable fixture.

title: Coverage gap: Kubernetes and cloud-CLI state files (kubeconfig client-key-data/password, gcloud ADC refresh tokens, Azure token caches, AWS SSO cache)
description: kubeconfig_token covers only `token:`; `client-key-data:` (base64 PEM, `LS0tLS1CRUdJTi` prefix), `client-certificate-data`, and `password:` under users are ignored, and the PEM detector cannot see base64-encoded keys. `~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json` refresh tokens (`1//0[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}`), `~/.config/gcloud/access_tokens.db`, `~/.azure/accessTokens.json`/`msal_token_cache.json`, and `~/.aws/sso/cache/*.json` accessToken are not covered. These files are routinely baked into CI/build images.

title: Coverage gap: HTTP header credentials (Authorization: Basic/Bearer, X-Api-Key, PRIVATE-TOKEN) in configs and RUN history
description: `Authorization: Basic <base64>` and `Authorization: Bearer <opaque>` are not assignments (prefix ends with 'Basic'/'Bearer'), so hasAssignedValuePrefix rejects them and no dedicated rule exists. They appear in `RUN curl -H` history lines, nginx/haproxy/Caddy configs, `.curlrc`/`.wgetrc`, and Kubernetes ingress annotations. looksLikeBase64Credential (decode and require ':') already exists but is only used for .npmrc `_auth`.

Code detectors.go:637-652 hasAssignedValuePrefix has no branch for header syntax; looksLikeBase64Credential used only at line 81.

verifier_note: hasAssignedValuePrefix (detectors.go:637-652) has no header branch; the only Authorization-style rules are okta (SSWS) and heroku HRKU-. looksLikeBase64Credential is used only at line 81.

title: Freshen existing vendor rules: Slack xapp-<redacted>, GitLab glptt-<redacted> GR1348941, OpenAI sk-<redacted> (+T3BlbkFJ marker), Notion ntn_, SonarQube squ_<redacted>, Grafana glc_, Sentry sntrys_, New Relic NRII/NRIQ/NRAL, PlanetScale pscale_pw_, CircleCI CCIPRJ_, Datadog 40-hex app key, Twilio SK keys
description: Several rules lag current vendor formats: slack_token covers xoxa/b/p/r/s only (Slack docs list `xapp-`, `xoxe.xapp-`, `xwfp-`; gitleaks adds `xoxe-`); OpenAI lacks `sk-<redacted>` (documented service-account prefix) and could use the `T3BlbkFJ` (base64 'OpenAI') marker as a validator; Notion moved to `ntn_` on 2024-09-25 (`\bntn_[0-9]{11}[A-Za-z0-9]{35}\b`); SonarQube on-prem tokens are `(squ|sqp|sqa)_[0-9a-f]{40}` while only SonarCloud `sqco_` exists; GitLab documents glptt-, gloas-, glagent-, glsoat-, glffct-, glimt-, glcbt-, glrtr-, glwt-, glft-; datadog_api_key's value regex is exactly 32 hex so 40-hex APP keys are never matched; Twilio API keys `SK[0-9a-f]{32}` are absent.

Code: detectors.go:70 slack, :92 openai, :106 notion, :133 sonarcloud, :102-105 datadog `\b[a-f0-9]{32}\b`.

verifier_note: gitleaks.toml fetched corroborates: openai sk-(proj|svcacct|admin) with T3BlbkFJ marker, notion ntn_[0-9]{11}[A-Za-z0-9]{35}, slack xapp-\d-[A-Z0-9]+-\d+-[a-z0-9]+, slack xox[pe], sonar squ_<redacted> with 40 chars, databricks (?:-\d)?. title: Coverage gap: OS/framework secrets baked into images (/etc/shadow and .htpasswd hashes, Laravel APP_KEY, Django/Flask SECRET_KEY with punctuation, Rails master.key/secret_key_base, WordPress define(), XML <password>)
description: A root password hash in `/etc/shadow` or an `.htpasswd` file is a classic image finding and is not detected. `APP_KEY=base64:...` has no keyword ('app_key' is not in secretKeywordExpression) so Laravel keys are missed even in env. Django/Flask `SECRET_KEY = 'x!7$k9@p2#...'` contains punctuation outside the candidate class so it is fragmented and missed. Rails `config/master.key` is a bare 32-hex file with no keyword. WordPress `define('DB_PASSWORD', '...')` and XML `<password>...</password>` are not assignment shapes for hasAssignedValuePrefix.
evidence: Probe: `etc shadow root hash => <none>`; `Laravel APP_KEY env => <none>`; `django secret key => <none>`; `django secret key strong => <none>`; `rails master.key bare hex => <none>`; `php define DB_PASSWORD => <none>`; `maven settings.xml <password> => <none>`. Code detectors.go:432 keyword list lacks `app[_-]?key`, `master[_-]?key`, `signing[_-]?key`, `encryption[_-]?key`; :433 candidate class excludes `!@#$%^&*()`.
proposed_fix: As proposed.
verifier_note: secretKeywordExpression (detectors.go:432) lacks app_key/master_key/encryption_key; candidate class excludes punctuation; no /etc/shadow or .htpasswd rule exists.

title: Trailing \b after a character class containing '-' makes fixed-length rules miss tokens ending in '-' and variable-length rules truncate them
description: Go's \b requires a word/non-word transition. When a token's last character is '-' (1/64 of base64url positions) and it is followed by a quote, space or end of input, there is no boundary. Fixed-length rules (google_api_key {35}, square_application_secret {43}, square_oauth_token {22}) therefore fail entirely; variable-length rules (jwt, anthropic_api_key, gitlab_token, gitlab_deploy_token, gitlab_runner_token, hashicorp_vault_token, sendgrid_api_key, pypi_api_token, fly_api_token, mapbox_secret_token) silently drop the final character, so Match.Value, fingerprint and the redacted span are of a truncated token and the last character stays in plaintext in context_snippet. ~1.5% of real Google API keys are missed outright.
evidence: Probe: '"AIza<redacted>"' => <none>; 'GOOGLE_API_KEY=AIza<redacted>' => <none>; same key ending in 'e' => google_api_key[15:54]; 'sq0csp-' + 42 A + '- next' => <none>; 'sk-ant-<redacted>' + 30 a + '- next' => anthropic_api_key[0:43] (44-char token truncated to 43); JWT with signature ending '-' => jwt[0:71] (dash excluded). Code: detectors.go:76 `\bAIza[0-9A-Za-z\-_]{35}\b`, :113 `\bsq0csp-[0-9A-Za-z_-]{43}\b`, :83 jwt, :91 anthropic.
proposed_fix: Replace trailing \b on every rule whose class contains '-' or '.' with an explicit terminator group, as google_oauth_access_token already does: e.g. `\b(AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35})(?:[^0-9A-Za-z_-]|$)` with group 1; same for sq0csp-/sq0atp-/jwt/sk-ant-<redacted> Add a table test that appends '-' as the last token char followed by '"' and asserts a full-length match. Combine with the DET-14 prefilter refactor since both touch every prefix rule.

title: isLowercaseSeparatorCandidate suppresses every lowercase+digit value containing '-', '_' or '/', so UUID-shaped and lowercase base64url secrets are never found by keyword_entropy
description: shouldSuppressEntropyCandidate rejects any candidate made only of lowercase letters, digits and -/_// (line 666 -> 681-696) regardless of context, entropy or length. This blanket rule (intended for 'base-passwd/user-change-gecos'-style words, which looksLikeWordCompound already handles) discards UUID-shaped tokens (Postmark, Rollbar, Pusher, any OAuth client secret rendered as UUID), Mailgun 'key-<32 lowercase alnum>' keys, and lowercase base64url tokens with '_' even when the line says password/token/api_key. It compounds DET-05: fixing the entropy threshold alone will not make UUID secrets detectable.
evidence: Probe: '/app/.env' 'MAILGUN_API_KEY="key-3ax6xnjp29jd6fds4gc373sgvjxteol0"' => <none>; '/app/config.yaml' 'postmark_token: 7f3c2a1e-9b8d-4c6f-a5e2-1d0b9c8a7f6e' => <none>; '/app/.env' 'API_TOKEN="a9f3k2m8x1q7z4w6v0b5n3c8j2h6g4d1s7_t9"' => <none>. Code detectors.go:666 `if isLowercaseSeparatorCandidate(value) { return true }` and :681-696.
proposed_fix: Delete the isLowercaseSeparatorCandidate gate (looksLikeWordCompound + looksPathLikeCandidate already cover the wordy cases in TestKeywordEntropySuppressesWordyCandidates) or restrict it to values with digitCount <= 2; add positive fixtures for a quoted Mailgun key and a UUID-shaped token under a password/token key, and keep the existing negative word-compound tests green.

title: Verification snippets pin version=v1.1.0(-rc.1) in README, SECURITY and RELEASING
description: Copy-paste verification blocks hard-code the version: README.md:438 `version=v1.1.0-rc.1`, SECURITY.md:106 `version=v1.1.0`, RELEASING.md:312 `version=v1.1.0`. `gh release verify v1.1.0` will fail with 'release not found' at 3.0.0. The three blocks are also byte-for-byte duplicates that have already been edited independently (README's uses `docker buildx imagetools inspect --format '{{json .Manifest.Digest}}'`, the other two take the digest from release-manifest.json).
evidence: SECURITY.md:105-107: 'image=ghcr.io/brumbelow/layerleak\nversion=v1.1.0\ndigest=\'sha256:<digest-from-release-manifest>\''
proposed_fix: Change to `version=v3.0.0` in all three; keep one canonical block in SECURITY.md 'Verify release integrity' and have README and RELEASING link to it instead of duplicating (README keeps only the two-line docker pull/inspect). Add to validate_docs.py (or a small shell check in verify.yml) a grep that fails if `version=v1.` or `@v1.` appears outside CHANGELOG history sections.
verifier_note: README.md:438 `version=v1.1.0-rc.1`, SECURITY.md:106 `version=v1.1.0`, RELEASING.md:312 `version=v1.1.0` confirmed. README's block differs from the other two (digest via `docker buildx imagetools inspect --format`, no `sha256sum --check`), so the three are already independently edited copies. Consolidating into SECURITY.md is sound.

title: Published demo command cannot run: 'vulnerableHost' is rejected as a non-lowercase repository, and the transcript shows repository-only phases and omits summary rows the CLI prints
description: web/docs/index.html:461 and demo-data.json:4/:52 present `layerleak scan vulnerableHost:latest --platform linux/amd64` as the example command. Running it against the current binary fails before any network call: `parse image reference: invalid reference format: repository name (library/vulnerableHost) must be lowercase` (exit 1). The replayed transcript is also not what the CLI prints for a single tagged reference: frames 2-3 show 'Phase: Listing Tags / Status: Listing repository tags' and 'Resolving Tags', but internal/jobs/scan.go only emits ProgressPhaseListingTags/ResolvingTags inside scanRepository (lines 286-309); scanSingleReference never does. The final summary frame (demo-data.json:82) omits 'Tags Enumerated/Tags Resolved/Tags Failed' rows, yet internal/cli/scan.go:389-395 appends them whenever `result.TagsEnumerated > 0`, which is 1 for a tagged reference (scanSingleReference sets TagsEnumerated: len(tags)). The frame also truncates the digest with '...' in the platform table, which renderSummaryTargets does not do (sanitizeProgressValue only collapses whitespace). The docs page (web/docs/index.html:457-459) claims the transcript 'shows the current result status, coverage, findings-array path, and companion scan-record path', so this is presented as representative output, not art.
evidence: $ go run . scan vulnerableHost:latest --progress off -> 'parse image reference: invalid reference format: repository name (library/vulnerableHost) must be lowercase'; internal/cli/scan.go:389: 'if result.TagsEnumerated > 0 || result.Mode == "repository" {' appends Tags Enumerated/Resolved/Failed; demo-data.json:57: '"status": "listing repository tags", "terminal": "...Phase:      Listing Tags...'
proposed_fix: As proposed. One nuance: the `[sha256:8dbedc1c4a77...]` truncation inside the progress frames is legitimate (shortDigest at progress.go:319-324 appends '...'); only the final summary table should show the full digest. The generated-transcript test should therefore render both progress frames (via the real renderer) and renderSummary so neither is hand-typed.
verifier_note: Reproduced: `go run . scan vulnerableHost:latest --progress off` prints 'parse image reference: invalid reference format: repository name (library/vulnerableHost) must be lowercase'. scannedTags (internal/jobs/scan.go:599-604) returns ["latest"] for a tagged reference, so scanSingleReference sets TagsEnumerated=1 and summaryRows (internal/cli/scan.go:389-395) appends the three Tags rows the demo omits. ListingTags/ResolvingTags are emitted only in scanRepository (scan.go:287, :302). renderSummaryTargets uses sanitizeProgressValue (progress.go:393-398), which never truncates, so the 60-char digest in the demo's platform table is invented.

title: Docs 'Results' section lists API aggregation fields as CLI result fields; no document describes the actual result JSON or scan-record JSON
description: web/docs/index.html:287-312 under 'Results' (the CLI section) lists 'Per-finding fields: manifest_digest, fingerprint, redacted_value, occurrence_count, actionable_occurrence_count, suppressed_occurrence_count, first_seen_at, last_seen_at'. Those are `findingSummaryItem` fields from internal/api/handler.go:110-121 (and it omits that struct's `id` and `detectors`); none of occurrence_count/actionable_/first_seen_at exist in the CLI JSON `findings[]` element, which is findings.Finding (internal/findings/findings.go:82-98: detector_name, confidence, disposition, disposition_reason, source_type, manifest_digest, platform, file_path, layer_digest, key, line_number, redacted_value, fingerprint, context_snippet, match_start, match_end, present_in_final_image). The 'Per-occurrence fields' list omits key, match_start, match_end, manifest_digest, fingerprint. Nothing anywhere documents the top-level result object (result_schema_version, status, mode, requested/resolved reference, tag_results[], targets[].platform_results[], the 12 coverage counters at internal/scanner/scan.go:57-68, diagnostics{code,scope,subject,message,limit,observed}), nor the scan record (internal/cli/results.go: record_schema_version, created_at, result, persistence{status: saved|failed|disabled, scan_run_id, error_code, error_message}), nor the findings-array file's extra fields (value, raw_context_snippet, source_location, occurrence_count/suppressed_occurrence_count which appear only for low-confidence file groups capped at 3 per persistedLowConfidenceGroupCap). README.md:174 'deduplicated occurrence counts' overstates that last behavior.
evidence: web/docs/index.html:305-309: 'occurrence_count actionable_occurrence_count suppressed_occurrence_count' vs internal/findings/findings.go:82-98 (no such fields); internal/cli/results.go:44-45: 'OccurrenceCount int `json:"occurrence_count,omitempty"`' set only in capPersistedLowConfidenceFindings for Confidence == "low" && FilePath != ""
proposed_fix: Add `web/docs/schemas/result.schema.json` and `web/docs/schemas/scan-record.schema.json` (JSON Schema 2020-12) generated from the Go types (a small `go run ./internal/tools/schemagen` or hand-written and enforced by a Go test that marshals fixture results and validates them), link them from README 'Results' and the docs page, and make the OpenAPI `ScanResult` schema `$ref` the same document so API and CLI cannot diverge. Rewrite the docs 'Results' section to list the real Finding fields and move the API summary fields under the HTTP API section. Correct README.md:174 to 'per-file occurrence counts for repeated low-confidence matches (capped at three retained occurrences per file group)'.
verifier_note: web/docs/index.html:303-312 'Per-finding fields' match findingSummaryItem (internal/api/handler.go:110-121) minus id/detectors; the DB findings table (migrations/0001_initial.up.sql:56-64) has no count columns, so these are API aggregation fields, not persistence columns. The 'Per-occurrence' list includes source_location, which is json:"-" on DetailedFinding (findings.go:101-104) and appears only in the findings-array file (results.go:36), and omits key/match_start/match_end that findings.Finding (findings.go:82-98) emits. occurrence_count in the file is set only in capPersistedLowConfidenceFindings (results.go:123-143). Separately, open question 3 is resolved: IsAttestationDescriptor (internal/manifest/document.go:301-316) also treats a non-empty artifactType or an unknown/unknown platform as an attestation, so the docs sentence at web/docs/index.html:164-166 is acceptable as written.

title: web/docs configuration block omits 16 variables README documents (all API_* server bounds, DATABASE_* pool/timeouts, MIGRATIONS_DIR); README and site duplicate content with no consistency check
description: web/docs/index.html:195-226 lists 32 variables. Compared with internal/config/config.go and README.md:203-267 it lacks LAYERLEAK_API_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES, API_SCAN_TIMEOUT, API_MAX_CONCURRENT_SCANS, API_READ_HEADER_TIMEOUT, API_READ_TIMEOUT, API_RESPONSE_WRITE_TIMEOUT, API_IDLE_TIMEOUT, API_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT, API_READINESS_TIMEOUT, DATABASE_MAX_OPEN_CONNS, DATABASE_MAX_IDLE_CONNS, DATABASE_CONN_MAX_LIFETIME, DATABASE_CONN_MAX_IDLE_TIME, DATABASE_QUERY_TIMEOUT, DATABASE_WRITE_TIMEOUT, MIGRATIONS_DIR. README, .env.example and the site each maintain their own copy; validate_docs.py checks links and OpenAPI but never cross-checks env names or defaults, so the three already disagree and will again after every config change.
evidence: web/docs/index.html:195-226 (config <pre> block) contains no 'LAYERLEAK_API_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES' / 'LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_MAX_OPEN_CONNS' / 'LAYERLEAK_MIGRATIONS_DIR'; README.md:251 '| `LAYERLEAK_API_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` | `16384` |', README.md:261 '| `LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_MAX_OPEN_CONNS` | `10` |'

Exclude FINDINGS_DIR, DATABASE_URL and the LAYERLEAK_DB_*/API_HOST/API_PORT/IMAGE keys from the equality assertion, or compare only the keys config.go parses with a non-empty default.

title: 3.0.0 needs an explicit wire/CLI compatibility statement: does /api/v1, result_schema_version 1, record_schema_version 1, exit codes and findings-array format survive the major bump?
description: CONTRIBUTING.md:128-133 says field removals, exit-code changes and API path changes 'require an intentional compatibility decision and release note', and CHANGELOG's Compatibility section (83-94) lists only behavior changes from the v1.1 work. A major version signals breakage; users will assume `/api/v1` and the JSON schema changed unless told otherwise. Conversely, if the maintainer wants to use the major to clean up (e.g. drop the legacy findings-array file in favor of the scan record, rename `suppressed_findings_count`/`suppressed_example_findings` inconsistencies, make `platform` a string, remove `Key`/`source_key` naming split between CLI JSON (`key`) and DB (`source_key`)), this is the only cheap moment and the docs must say so. Today no document states either decision.
evidence: internal/jobs/scan.go:206: 'ResultSchemaVersion:    1,'; internal/cli/results.go: 'record := localScanRecord{RecordSchemaVersion: 1, ...'; CHANGELOG.md:83-94 Compatibility section has no line about module path, API version or schema versions
proposed_fix: Decide and write a 'What 3.0.0 does and does not break' block in CHANGELOG Compatibility, README 'Version history' and the upgrade guide (DOC-18): recommended default is 'module path only: /api/v1 paths, result_schema_version 1, record_schema_version 1, exit codes 0/1/2, findings-array file and env-var names are unchanged; the major exists because Go forbids reusing v2 and the root path is frozen at v1.0.0'. If any field/flag is renamed, bump result_schema_version to 2 and record_schema_version to 2 in the same release and document the mapping. Add a CONTRIBUTING 'Major-version policy' paragraph.
verifier_note: CONTRIBUTING.md:128-133 requires an explicit compatibility decision for path/field/exit-code changes; CHANGELOG.md:83-94 Compatibility section has no module-path, /api/v1 or schema-version statement; internal/jobs/scan.go:206 ResultSchemaVersion 1; openapi.yaml:534 'Additive result fields may be introduced within API v1'. A major bump without a stated wire contract is a real ambiguity for automation authors.

title: Pages workflow only asserts files exist and deploys from every main push independently of CI, so published docs can be broken and can never match a released version
description: pages.yml:28-39 runs ten `test -f` lines and then uploads/deploys `./web`. It does not run scripts/validate_docs.py, the Python unit tests or the Playwright demo tests (those live only in verify.yml:77-132, reached via test.yml), and it is triggered by `push: branches: [main] paths: web/**` (lines 4-8) with no `workflow_run`/`needs` on CI, so a red CI and a green Pages deploy can happen on the same commit. Because it always deploys HEAD of main, the site at brumbelow.github.io/layerleak/docs/ documents unreleased behavior; RELEASING.md:289 lists 'Pages serves the matching docs and OpenAPI file' as a post-publication check that nothing enforces, and after 3.0.0 ships the first merged PR will make the published OpenAPI disagree with the released binary. There is no version indicator or older-version path on the site.
evidence:
.github/workflows/pages.yml:28-39: 'name: Verify Pages artifact
 run: |
 test -f web/index.html
 ... test -f web/.nojekyll'; pages.yml:4-8: 'on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "web/**"'
proposed_fix: Replace the existence check with the real gate: set up Python from requirements-docs.lock and run `python -m unittest scripts/test_validate_docs.py && python scripts/validate_docs.py` (and optionally the Playwright test) in the build job, or trigger pages.yml with `workflow_run: workflows: [CI] types: [completed]` and `if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`. Add docs versioning: publish `web/` to `docs/v3/` (and `docs/latest/` -> copy) from the release workflow's publish job on stable tags, keep `docs/dev/` from main, add a small version banner/switcher and a `<meta name="layerleak-version">` emitted from CHANGELOG. Add the Pages deploy URL to release-manifest.json so RELEASING's 'Pages serves the matching docs' check becomes verifiable (`curl .../docs/v3/openapi.yaml | grep 'version: 3.0.0'`).
verifier_note: pages.yml:4-9 triggers on push to main for web/** and pages.yml itself; :28-39 runs only `test -f` checks; no workflow_run/needs dependency on CI (test.yml). verify.yml runs validate_docs.py, the Python tests and Playwright (verify.yml:103-132), but Pages does not wait for it. The site therefore always documents HEAD of main, so RELEASING.md:289 'Pages serves the matching docs and OpenAPI file' is unenforced and false after the first post-release merge.

title: Documentation set missing for a 3.0.0: architecture overview, detector catalog, threat model, API operations runbook, false-positive/suppression FAQ, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, security.txt
description: The docs/ tree contains only two dated v1.1 working records and an alert ledger; README is a 490-line monolith. Gaps observed while cross-checking code: (a) no architecture page although the package graph is clean (registry -> manifest -> layers -> detectors -> findings/detectionpolicy -> scanner -> jobs -> scanservice -> storage/api/cli); (b) no detector catalog even though findings carry `detector_name` and `confidence` and CHANGELOG.md:87-89 warns identifiers changed; detectors.Default() (internal/detectors/detectors.go:56) is a declarative list that could be rendered; (c) no threat model, although README 'Security model' and SECURITY 'Security boundaries' list controls without attacker/asset framing; (d) no operations runbook for the API (sizing with MAX_CONCURRENT_SCANS=1, timeouts interplay, readiness vs liveness, structured log fields `request_id`/`error_type`, backup/restore, purge procedure, schema drift errors); (e) no FAQ explaining dispositions (`example`, `example_path` at demo-data.json:421-422 and internal/detectionpolicy/policy.go:84-85 directory heuristics) or how to handle false positives (there is no suppression flag or allowlist, which is itself a product gap worth stating); (f) no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md for AI-assisted contributors despite the repo's strict conventions (pinned actions, hostile-input rules, table-driven tests); (g) no RFC 9116 `/.well-known/security.txt` on Pages even though SECURITY.md:44-45 invites encrypted reports without publishing a key.
evidence: ls docs -> 'plans  release-readiness-2026-09-09.md  reviews'; SECURITY.md:44-45: 'Encrypt particularly sensitive details before sending and ask for a suitable public key if needed.' (no key published); internal/detectionpolicy/policy.go:84-85: case "test", "tests", "__tests__", "testdata", "fixture", "fixtures", "mock", "mocks", "__mocks__", "spec", "specs", "e2e", "acceptance", "stubs"
proposed_fix: Create docs/ as a real tree with an index: docs/README.md; docs/architecture.md (package graph + data flow + where limits are enforced); docs/detectors.md generated by a `go test` golden (`go run ./internal/tools/detector-catalog` or a test that fails when detectors.Default() differs from the checked-in table: name, confidence, gating path/key, example redacted shape); docs/threat-model.md (assets: credentials in images, operator DB; adversaries: malicious registry/image, SSRF via registry redirects, API abuser; controls mapped to README bullets); docs/operations.md (runbook); docs/faq.md (dispositions, `disposition_reason` values, why there is no allowlist yet and how to filter by fingerprint); CLAUDE.md at repo root (build/test commands from CONTRIBUTING, hard rules: never weaken limits, pin SHAs, no live secrets in fixtures, update README+openapi+web+CHANGELOG together); web/.well-known/security.txt with Contact: mailto:admin@brumbelow.org, Policy: link to SECURITY.md, Expires: one year, and optionally Encryption: link to a published key. Link all of these from README's bullet list at lines 16-20.
verifier_note: `ls docs` shows only plans/, release-readiness-2026-09-09.md and reviews/; no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md at root; web/.well-known does not exist; SECURITY.md:44-45 invites encrypted reports without publishing a key; detectionpolicy/policy.go:84-85 and :136 directory heuristics are undocumented. Effort 'l' is realistic; none of it is release-blocking.

title: Findings-dir heuristic writes into whatever Go project the user happens to be in; relative values ignore cwd
description: resolveFindingsDir walks up from cwd to the nearest go.mod and uses <that root>/findings; a relative LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR is also joined to that root, not to cwd. For an installed binary this means `cd ~/src/some-go-service && layerleak scan nginx` silently creates ~/src/some-go-service/findings/ (untracked files in an unrelated repo), and the shipped .env.example value LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR=findings lands somewhere that depends on where go.mod is, not where the user runs. The heuristic only makes sense for developing layerleak itself (its own /findings/ is gitignored). There is also no flag to choose the directory or to skip writing artifacts at all, so even `--format json | jq` always writes two files.
evidence: results.go:187-195 joins a relative value to repoRoot(); results.go:198-207 default = <go.mod root>/findings; results.go:210-227 repoRoot walks parents for go.mod. Probe: cwd=.../001/sub/deeper relative(out)=.../001/out default=.../001/findings (both outside cwd). .env.example:12 LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR=findings. README.md:152-154 documents the go.mod walk but not that relative values are re-rooted.
proposed_fix: For 3.0.0: drop the go.mod walk. Default to an explicit, predictable location (e.g. $XDG_DATA_HOME/layerleak/findings or ./layerleak-findings under cwd), resolve relative LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR against cwd, add --output-dir/-o and --no-artifacts (or --output-dir '') flags, and keep the repo's own dev convenience via a documented env value. Update README 'Results and secret handling', .env.example and CHANGELOG under 3.0.0 breaking changes; adjust TestResolveFindingsDirDefaultsToRepoRootFindings.

title: --all-tags sweep stopped early drops unscanned targets from per-target accounting
description: scanRepository sets TargetCount = len(groupList) before the loop, but when the findings budget is exhausted before the next target (line 377-382), when a target hits a max_findings/max_raw_finding_bytes diagnostic (451-454), or when a limit/integrity/cancellation error aborts the loop (427-435), the remaining targets are never appended to result.Targets and are not counted as failed/partial/skipped. The invariant target_count == completed+partial+failed is violated, the DB scan record (BuildScanRecord iterates publicResult.Targets) has no rows for the skipped digests, and their TagResults remain status "resolved" as if nothing was wrong. Overall status is correctly 'partial' via Coverage.Complete=false, but consumers cannot tell which tags were not scanned without parsing the diagnostic.

Existing test TestScanRepositoryAppliesMaxFindingsAcrossTargets (scan_test.go:539) only uses 2 tags so the gap is invisible.

Probe: "PROBE5 err=registry request failed: status=404 Not Found stdoutLen=0". description: The default --format summary prints counts and a per-target/per-platform table only; the detector name, redacted value, file path/env key, layer and line of each finding are never shown. title: --platform is silently ignored for single-manifest images; scan reports completed for a different platform
description: The platform selector is only applied when the root document is an index (manifest.SelectDescriptors at scanner/scan.go:199). For a plain image manifest the sole target is appended unconditionally (:189-197) and verifyPlatformProvenance (:1102-1122) compares only descriptor vs config platforms, which is vacuous because a single manifest has no descriptor platform. So `layerleak scan app:latest --platform linux/arm64` against an amd64-only image scans amd64, reports status completed and exits 0/2 as if the restriction were honoured. The flag help (cli/scan.go:283) says 'Scan only the specified platform' and the CLI validates the selector (:55-59) but never checks the outcome.

Add scanner and CLI tests for the single-manifest mismatch; note the behaviour change in CHANGELOG 3.0.0.

title: --format json neutralises every error and diagnostic message to 'scan step failed', unlike summary mode and the API
description: stdout JSON is produced from scanservice.RedactedResult(result), which applies the scan-history storage policy (record.go:263-300): every target/platform `error` and every diagnostic `message` becomes the literal 'scan step failed', including benign coverage diagnostics such as files_skipped_oversize and max_findings_exceeded. The API renders those same codes with descriptive safe text (handler.go:951-960 safeDiagnosticMessage) and `--format summary` prints the raw registry error for the same run, so the CLI's machine-readable output is the least informative surface. README.md:127 calls it a 'stable JSON result' and :144-147 describe diagnostics without mentioning that messages are neutralised; CHANGELOG.md:66 documents neutral wording only for API storage failures.
evidence: Probe (partial fixture, same run twice): json platform_error="scan step failed", json diagnostic code=manifest_failed message="scan step failed"; summary tail: 'linux/arm64  sha256:bbbb...  0  registry request failed: status=404 Not Found'. cli/scan.go:253 encoder.Encode(scanservice.RedactedResult(result)); record.go:285-300 sanitizedDiagnostics/storedErrorMessage.
proposed_fix: Decide the CLI policy explicitly for 3.0.0: either emit the un-neutralised (control-character-sanitised) messages on stdout, since the same text is already printed to stderr and the summary table, or at minimum reuse the API's safeDiagnosticMessage(code) mapping so coverage diagnostics stay meaningful. Share the function from scanservice, document the policy in README 'Results and secret handling', and add a CLI test asserting json and summary agree.

title: Old-GNU sparse ('S') and GNU contiguous ('7') regular files are silently dropped as "other" while coverage reports complete
description: archive/tar keeps Typeflag TypeGNUSparse for old-GNU sparse entries (reader.go handleSparseFile) and presents the logical content through the normal entry reader. The engine's switch only handles TypeReg/TypeRegA, so an 'S' file falls into the default branch: it is drained, stored as ArtifactTypeOther, not counted in FilesSeen, never scanned, and no diagnostic is emitted, so the platform is reported `completed` with `coverage.complete=true`. GNU tar writes this format by default for sparse files (`tar --sparse`, format gnu), so layers imported from tar-produced rootfs (docker/podman import, skopeo dir:) can hide files from the scan. README.md:42 promises incomplete coverage is 'never' reported as clean.
evidence: Fixture built with GNU tar 1.35 (`tar --sparse --format=gnu`) containing an 8 MiB sparse file with a GitHub token in the middle. Probe: `fixture header: typeflag='S' name="sparse.log" size=8388608 format=GNU`; `Replay err=<nil> coverage={LayersSeen:1 LayersCompleted:1 FilesSeen:0 FilesScanned:0 ... EntriesSkippedUnsafe:0}`; `final[sparse.log]: type="other" class="" scannable=false`. Code: state.go:367 `case tar.TypeReg, tar.TypeRegA:` ... state.go:395 `default:` builds ArtifactTypeOther.
proposed_fix: Fix as proposed (`case tar.TypeReg, tar.TypeRegA, tar.TypeGNUSparse, tar.TypeCont:`; drop TypeRegA per LAY-16). The test can use the GNU-tar-generated fixture checked into testdata rather than hand-patching, since Go's tar.Writer cannot emit 'S' headers.
verifier_note: Built a fixture with GNU tar 1.35 (`tar --sparse --format=gnu`): header typeflag='S', size=8388608, format=GNU; tar.Reader delivered 8388608 logical bytes containing the planted ghp_ token. Replay returned err=nil with Coverage{FilesSeen:0 FilesScanned:0 EntriesSkippedUnsafe:0 LayersCompleted:1} and the file was absent from FinalFiles, i.e. stored via the default branch (state.go:395-414) as ArtifactTypeOther with no diagnostic. archive/tar reader.go:197 keeps TypeGNUSparse on the header and only rewrites TypeRegA (reader.go:145-151). ExpandedBytes was already 8388608, so logicalLayerBudget already charges the logical size and the proposed one-line fix is budget-safe.

title: A './' (or '.') root directory entry is counted as an unsafe archive entry, forcing a false partial status and exit code 1
description: normalizePath returns an error when path.Clean yields ".", and the caller increments EntriesSkippedUnsafe and later emits the `unsafe_archive_entries_skipped` diagnostic with Complete=false. Tarballs created with `tar -C rootfs -c .` (the common way to build rootfs archives that become layers via docker/podman import or OCI layout tools) begin with a `./` directory entry. Nothing unsafe was skipped, yet the scan becomes `partial` and the CLI exits 1 unless --allow-partial is set.
evidence: Probe layer entries `./`, `./app/`, `./app/safe`: `err=<nil> unsafe=1 files=[app/safe(regular/text)]`. Code: state.go:1104-1107 `cleaned := path.Clean(value); if cleaned == "" || cleaned == "." { return "", fmt.Errorf("path is required") }`; state.go:249-256 `entryPath, err := normalizePath(header.Name); if err != nil { working.coverage.EntriesSkippedUnsafe++ ...`.
proposed_fix: As proposed; a sentinel errRootEntry handled before the EntriesSkippedUnsafe++ at state.go:251 (drain and continue). Keep counting it in entryCount for the entry limits, as runtimes do.
verifier_note: Probe layer with entries `./`, `./app/`, `./app/safe`, `.` produced err=nil, EntriesSkippedUnsafe:2, FinalFiles=[app/safe]. normalizePath (state.go:1104-1107) returns an error for path.Clean results of ".", and applyLayer (state.go:249-251) counts that as unsafe, which scan.go:450-457 turns into `unsafe_archive_entries_skipped` and Complete=false (scan.go:440). Nothing hostile was present. `tar -C rootfs -c .` always emits a leading `./` entry.

title: zstd decoder window cap is derived from MAX_LAYER_BYTES, so a 10-byte hostile frame allocates 513 MiB at production defaults
description: zstdDecoderLimit returns MaxLayerBytes clamped to [1 MiB, zstd.MaxWindowSize=512 MiB] and passes it to both WithDecoderMaxWindow and WithDecoderMaxMemory. With the documented default LAYERLEAK_MAX_LAYER_BYTES=536870912 the cap is exactly 512 MiB, so any frame declaring a 512 MiB window is accepted and klauspost allocates windowSize+1 MiB of history on the first block. A single 10-byte blob (or one such layer per manifest, up to MAX_IMAGE_LAYERS) forces a ~0.5 GiB transient allocation per scan, multiplied by LAYERLEAK_API_MAX_CONCURRENT_SCANS. MAX_LAYER_BYTES is meant to bound stream length, not decoder memory; real zstd layers use 8 MiB windows (zstd CLI refuses >128 MiB by default). CONTRIBUTING.md:103 requires bounding reads before allocation. The existing test only exercises 1 MiB and the 64 MiB fallback, not the shipped default.
evidence: Probe frame `28 b5 2f fd 00 98 09 00 00 78` (window descriptor 0x98 = 2^29): `production default LAYERLEAK_MAX_LAYER_BYTES=512MiB: err=... read tar entry: unexpected EOF allocated=513 MiB for a 10-byte blob`; with 128 MiB or disabled: `window size exceeded allocated=0 MiB`. Code: state.go:990-993 `if maxLayerBytes > zstd.MaxWindowSize { return zstd.MaxWindowSize }; return uint64(maxLayerBytes)`. klauspost framedec.go:262-265 `d.history.allocFrameBuffer = d.history.windowSize + maxBlockSize/2`; history.go:97-98 `h.b = make([]byte, 0, h.allocFrameBuffer)`.
proposed_fix: As proposed. Note the cap must stay independent of MaxLayerBytes in both directions: today MaxLayerBytes=0 already yields the 64 MiB fallback, so a fixed 64-128 MiB bound is consistent with existing behavior, and my probe confirmed a 70 MiB-decompressed zstd frame with known FrameContentSize still decodes under the 64 MiB fallback (streaming does not enforce maxDecodedSize against frame size), so lowering the window cap does not reject legitimate large layers.
verifier_note: Reproduced: frame `28 b5 2f fd 00 98 09 00 00 78` with MaxLayerBytes=512<<20 gave `read tar entry: unexpected EOF` and TotalAlloc delta of 513 MiB; with 128 MiB or 0 it was `window size exceeded`, 0 MiB. zstdDecoderLimit (state.go:990-993) returns zstd.MaxWindowSize (framedec.go:43, 1<<29) at the documented default, so framedec.go:231 `d.WindowSize > d.o.maxWindowSize` is false and history.go:97-98 allocates allocFrameBuffer = windowSize + maxBlockSize/2 (framedec.go:264) on the first block. WithDecoderMaxMemory does not help: in streaming mode it only clamps the window (framedec.go:52-53) and is otherwise a DecodeAll bound.

title: Files larger than MAX_FILE_BYTES (1 MiB default) are not scanned at all; 3.0 should stream-scan them instead of skipping
description: buildRegularArtifact reads MaxFileBytes+1 bytes and, if the file is larger, drops all content (ContentClassOversize, Content=nil). The scanner then emits `files_skipped_oversize` and marks coverage partial. Minified JS bundles, large JSON/YAML dumps, logs, lockfiles and notebooks routinely exceed 1 MiB and are exactly where leaked tokens appear, so today the default configuration neither scans them nor lets the scan complete cleanly. Detector inputs are line/regex based and could be fed in bounded windows without retaining the file.
evidence: state.go:823-826 `scannable := int64(len(content)) <= maxFileBytes; if !scannable { contentClass = ContentClassOversize; content = nil }`; scan.go:440 `Complete = err == nil && layerResult.Coverage.FilesSkippedOversize == 0 && ...`; scan.go:441-448 diagnostic `"%d file(s) exceeded the per-file scan limit"`. README.md:229 describes only buffering.
proposed_fix: Introduce streamed scanning for oversize regular files: read the entry in overlapping windows (e.g. 1 MiB windows with a 4 KiB overlap so tokens spanning a boundary are seen once), run detectors per window with line-offset bookkeeping, dedupe by fingerprint+offset, and never retain oversize content (so deleted-artifact recovery for oversize files is explicitly documented as content-less). Report `files_scanned_streamed` in coverage and keep coverage complete. Consider raising the default MAX_FILE_BYTES to 4-8 MiB in 3.0 and document the change in CHANGELOG.
verifier_note: state.go:823-826 drops all content above MaxFileBytes; scan.go:440-448 makes the platform partial with files_skipped_oversize. Accurate description of an improvement a major release can make.

title: Binary/NUL classification excludes UTF-16 text, nested archives (.jar/.zip/.whl/.tar.gz) and compiled binaries entirely, yet coverage stays 'complete'
description: classifyContent marks any content with a NUL byte or <85% printable as binary and drops it; scanner does not consider FilesExcludedBinary when computing Complete. Consequences: UTF-16LE config files (web.config, PowerShell, Windows-originated .env) contain NULs and are never scanned; secrets inside .jar/.war/.zip/.whl/.egg/.tar.gz/.gz and Go/Rust binaries with embedded credentials are invisible; keystores are silently ignored. Competing scanners extract printable strings from binaries and expand archives one level under the same byte limits.
evidence: state.go:871-879 `if hasNULByte(content) { return ContentClassBinaryNUL } if printableRatio(content) < 0.85 { return ContentClassBinaryLowPrintable }`; state.go:830-832 `if !scannable { content = nil }`; scan.go:440 Complete ignores FilesExcludedBinary.
proposed_fix: Phase 1 (s): detect UTF-16 BOM/alternating-NUL pattern and transcode to UTF-8 before classification. Phase 2 (m): for zip-family magic (PK\x03\x04) and gzip/tar magic, expand one nesting level with the existing per-file/per-layer budgets and provenance `path!inner/path`. Phase 3 (m): for ELF/other binaries, feed runs of ≥16 printable bytes to detectors (strings-style) with a `binary_strings` source flag and lower confidence. Expose counts (`files_nested_scanned`, `files_binary_strings_scanned`) in coverage.
verifier_note: classifyContent (state.go:871-879) excludes any NUL-containing content (UTF-16 text) and all archives/binaries; scan.go:440 does not consider FilesExcludedBinary in Complete. Correct as an improvement; effort xl is realistic.

title: High-risk tar-header and decompression behaviors have no fixtures in state_test.go
description: The suite covers whiteouts, traversal, PAX long names, PAX sparse budgets, zstd window rejection at 1 MiB/fallback, limits and rollback, but not: root `./`/`.` entries; old-GNU sparse 'S' and contiguous '7' typeflags; PAX global headers; device/fifo/char entries alongside a same-path regular file in a later layer; hardlink to symlink/directory; symlinked-directory write-through (`app -> /etc` then `app/secret`); duplicate entries within one layer (same-layer deleted artifact provenance); repeated layer digest in a manifest ([A,B,A]); whiteout of a symlink and `.wh..wh..opq` at the archive root; concatenated gzip members vs trailing padding/garbage; zstd skippable frames and multi-frame streams; zstd window allocation at the production default; cancellation during a sparse hole with limits disabled; MaxFileBytes boundary (size == limit vs limit+1); non-UTF-8/CRLF text classification; a tar truncated at a block boundary (treated as clean EOF).

title: No fuzz test for applyLayer/tar parsing or retained-byte accounting invariants
description: applyLayer is the hostile-input boundary (CONTRIBUTING.md:100-104, SECURITY.md:66) yet there is no Go native fuzz target. Accounting invariants (RetainedBytes never negative, equals the recomputed sum over final+deleted+dirs, restored exactly on rollback, ExpandedBytes monotonic, entries == committed header count) are only pinned by hand-computed constants in a few tests. checkedRetainedAdd treats a negative RetainedBytes as a limit error (state.go:539), which would surface an accounting bug as a confusing `retained_bytes exceeded` rather than a test failure.
evidence: `grep -n 'func Fuzz' internal/layers/*.go internal/scanner/*.go` returns nothing; state.go:538-543 `if left < 0 || right < 0 || left > math.MaxInt64-right { return 0, false }`; state.go:610 and :643 subtract retained bytes without an invariant check.
proposed_fix: Add FuzzApplyLayer seeded with the existing gzipLayer/zstdLayer/gzipSparseLayer corpora that feeds raw (uncompressed media type) bytes to Replay with small limits and asserts: no panic; Coverage.RetainedBytes >= 0 and equal to a recomputed sum over FinalFiles/DeletedArtifacts/dirs; after an error the FinalFiles equal the pre-layer snapshot; LayersCompleted <= LayersSeen; results identical across two runs (determinism). Wire `go test -run=^$ -fuzz=FuzzApplyLayer -fuzztime=60s` into a scheduled CI job.
verifier_note: `grep -rn 'func Fuzz'` finds only manifest/integrity_test.go:122 and manifest/reference_test.go:217; nothing in layers or scanner. checkedRetainedAdd (state.go:538-543) does convert a negative RetainedBytes into a retained_bytes limit error, masking accounting bugs as described.

title: --version behaviour after /v3: module installs report v3.x, container and no-VCS builds report dev; smoke does not depend on it
description: (a) resolveVersion prefers the -X-set Version, then debug.BuildInfo.Main.Version. `go install github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3@v3.0.0` embeds Main.Version=v3.0.0 so `layerleak --version` prints `layerleak version v3.0.0` (cobra template), satisfying the post-release `grep -F "${RELEASE_VERSION}"`. Dockerfile builds use only `-ldflags="-s -w"`, `.dockerignore` excludes `.git`, and cmd/api, cmd/migrate, cmd/purge, cmd/healthcheck do not use cli.Version at all; the image's only version signal is the `org.opencontainers.image.version` label, which registry-smoke checks. A checkout build embeds a VCS pseudo-version. Trap: the `-X` symbol path changes to `github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3/internal/cli.Version`.

proposed_fix: No code change is required for the migration. Documentation: README/web docs should say module-installed binaries print `layerleak version v3.x.y`, checkout builds print a Go VCS pseudo-version (`v3.0.0-<date>-<sha>[+dirty]` once the module is /v3) and non-VCS builds print `dev`. Update the root.go comment to name the new symbol (`-ldflags "-X github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3/internal/cli.Version=..."`). Optional hardening: tighten the smoke to `grep -Fx "layerleak version ${RELEASE_VERSION}"` so `v3.0.0` cannot be satisfied by a `v3.0.0-rc.1` substring. Optional product improvement (3.0 scope): pass `-X` in the Dockerfile via a build arg wired to the release version so container binaries can self-report.

Reproduced in the /v3 scratch module: `go install .` (no .git) -> `layerleak version dev`; `-X github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3/internal/cli.Version=v3.0.0-rc.1` -> `layerleak version v3.0.0-rc.1`; the OLD symbol path `-X github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/internal/cli.Version=v9.9.9` is silently ignored and prints `dev`, so any ldflag outside the repo (none exist in-repo) must be updated. The `grep -F` substring trap is real (`echo 'layerleak version v3.0.0-rc.1' | grep -F v3.0.0` matches) but cannot occur in the workflow because `go install path@v3.0.0` stamps exactly v3.0.0. Correction: checkout builds print `v0.0.0-<date>-<sha>` until a v3 tag is an ancestor (see MIG-13).

title: Root path github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest resolves to v1.0.0 forever after the move
description: (b) Go resolves @latest per module path; the root path will never see v3 tags. Mitigations: (1) Docs wording (README, web docs, CONTRIBUTING, release notes) telling users to include /v3 - cheap, must ship with v3.0.0. (2) pkg.go.dev automatically shows 'The highest tagged major version is v3' on the root-path page once /v3 is indexed - free, no action. (3) A final root-path pointer release (e.g. v1.0.1) whose go.mod carries `// Deprecated: use github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3` above the module line - `go get`/`go install` then print a deprecation warning and pkg.go.dev shows a banner; but it requires a commit with the root module path reachable from main, a workflow that still accepts v1 (or a dedicated pointer-only lane), an RC plus 72-hour soak and a full container build for a documentation-only change, and a v1.* tag ruleset that allows creation. (4) Shipping v1.1.0 first as already prepared, then v3.0.0 - gives v1 users the fixes but doubles the release effort and produces two identical code lines. Note the `retract` directive cannot help (it also requires a new v1 version and only affects the same module).
evidence: README.md:54 `go install github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest`; proxy: `go list -m -f '{{.Version}}' github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest` -> `v1.0.0`; go.mod has no `// Deprecated:` comment (grep empty).
proposed_fix: Recommendation unchanged (docs wording + pkg.go.dev banner now). If a pointer release is wanted later, the dedicated `pointer_release` mode must (a) accept `^v1\.0\.[1-9][0-9]*$`, (b) expect `module github.com/brumbelow/layerleak` plus a `// Deprecated:` comment in go.mod, (c) replace the main-ancestry check with 'commit is a descendant of v1.0.0', (d) skip the RC/soak requirement and image staging, and (e) create the GitHub release with --latest=false.
verifier_note: Proxy probe confirms root @latest = v1.0.0 and the root version list is `v1.0.0-beta v1.0.0-beta.1 v1.0.0`; go.mod has no `// Deprecated:` line. Correction to option (3): a 'documentation-only' v1.0.1 pointer is not achievable under the current workflow. Any commit reachable from main that still has the root module path contains all post-v1.0.0 code (so it is really option 4), while a branch off v1.0.0 carrying only the deprecation comment fails the main-ancestry check (container-release.yml:118-121), the RC-first rule (:180), and after the move also the go.mod check (:111). A pointer lane therefore has to relax three gates, not one.

title: Things that must NOT change with the module major: /api/v1, result_schema_version, record_schema_version, schema 0004
description: (h) The HTTP API path version, the CLI JSON `result_schema_version`, the companion record `record_schema_version`, the migration ledger `0004`, the release-manifest `schema_version` and the demo fixture `version` are independent contracts from the Go module major. A 3.0.0 must not rename `/api/v1` to `/api/v3` nor bump the schema versions merely because the import path changed; doing so would break every existing client and fixture for no behavioural reason. Add one sentence to CONTRIBUTING.md 'API and result compatibility' and to the CHANGELOG v3.0.0 module-path subsection: `The Go module major is independent of the HTTP API path (/api/v1), result_schema_version (1), record_schema_version (1) and database schema version (0004); none of these change in 3.0.0.` Only bump them when their own contracts change.

title: First /v3 publication may need a longer proxy wait than the five-minute loop
description: (d) proxy.golang.org has already served (and can cache) a negative answer for github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3 (`@v/list` 404). The post-release job polls `go install` 30 times at 10 s and then fails; for a brand-new module path the first successful fetch can lag longer than for a new tag on an already-indexed path. A failure here happens after the release is public and only wastes a rerun, but a rerun re-executes the whole workflow.
evidence: container-release.yml:1164-1173 `for attempt in {1..30}; do if ... go install "github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@${RELEASE_VERSION}"; then break; fi; if [[ "${attempt}" -eq 30 ]]; then echo "The Go proxy did not publish ${RELEASE_VERSION} within five minutes."`; probe today: `reading https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3/@v/list: 404 Not Found`.
proposed_fix: Make the @latest wait at least 30 minutes (for example 180 attempts x 10 s or a POST_RELEASE_PROXY_ATTEMPTS env), raise post-release `timeout-minutes` to about 45, treat a 404 'no matching versions' as absent-and-retry rather than a hard failure, and avoid probing `/v3@latest` from local machines between now and the rc.1 dispatch.
verifier_note: proxy.golang.org states: 'explicitly request that version via go get module@version. The new version should be available within one minute. Note that if someone requested the version before the tag was pushed, it may take up to 30 minutes for the mirror's cache to expire'. Nobody has requested `@v/v3.0.0-rc.1.info`, so the exact-version install loop (30x10 s) is probably fine, but `/v3/@v/list` and `@latest` HAVE been requested (by the auditor's probes and this verification), so the @latest answer can lag up to 30 minutes. The post-release job has `timeout-minutes: 15` (container-release.yml:1112), so neither the RC @latest check nor the stable @latest loop (1178-1188, 5 minutes) can wait out the documented window; the first /v3 RC is the most likely victim, and the same cap applies to every later stable promotion.

title: post-release job timeout (15 minutes) is shorter than the Go proxy's documented 30-minute cache window
description: Any fix for MIG-08/MIG-23 that waits for proxy.golang.org to refresh `@latest` for the brand-new /v3 path must fit inside the job timeout. The job is capped at 15 minutes, while the proxy documents up to 30 minutes of staleness for data that was requested before the tag existed (which is the case for /v3 @latest and @v/list). For the first RC the step would be killed before the proxy can answer, failing a release that is already public and forcing a full rerun.
evidence: container-release.yml:1105-1112 `post-release: ... timeout-minutes: 15`; proxy.golang.org: 'if someone requested the version before the tag was pushed, it may take up to 30 minutes for the mirror's cache to expire and fresh data about the version to become available'; probes of `/v3/@v/list` and `/v3@latest` were made on 2026-09-30 during the audit.
proposed_fix: Raise `timeout-minutes` on post-release to about 45 and make the @latest retry budget >= 30 minutes (see MIG-23); keep the exact-version install loop short since the proxy fetches a never-requested version on demand. Document in RELEASING.md that a post-release timeout does not invalidate the published release and may be retried.

title: Replace the nearest-go.mod findings-directory heuristic and the two-file output with one scan-record file, `--no-save`, and `--output`
description: Three awkward defaults compound: (a) when LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR is unset the CLI walks up from cwd looking for a go.mod and writes `findings/` into whatever Go project the user happens to be inside — a heuristic that only makes sense for the layerleak repo itself; (b) files are always written even when `--format json` already streams the full result to stdout, so CI runs leave stray artifacts; (c) two files are written per scan (a legacy findings array plus `scans/<name>.json`) and the code explicitly cannot make them atomic. The legacy array was kept only for v1.x compatibility (plan section 2). A major can end all three.

README.md:161-163: 'The two files are published independently... do not claim the two files form one atomic transaction.' docs/plans/2026-09-09-release-readiness.md:95 '[x] Keep the existing findings-array file format and location compatible.'

Also update README.md:148-166, .env.example:12 (`LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR=findings`), and the record's `persistence` block stays as is.
verifier_note: Premise verified: results.go:210-227 `repoRoot()` walks up to a `go.mod`; :198-207 default `filepath.Join(root, "findings")`; :302-306 writes `findingsPath` and `scans/<name>` with `errors.Join`; scan.go:213 `writeResultArtifacts(...)` runs before the `switch outputFormat` at :249 regardless of `--format json`; README.md:151-154 documents the go.mod heuristic. However the proposed fix has an unstated side effect: the legacy findings array is the ONLY local artifact that carries raw values — results.go:113-116 `if persistRawSecrets { persisted.Value = item.Value; persisted.RawContextSnippet = item.RawSnippet }` — while the scan record is built from `scanservice.RedactedResult` (:298) and README.md:176-180 promises the companion record 'remain[s] redacted'. Deleting the array therefore removes local raw-secret persistence entirely (and the low-confidence group cap at :123-151 that only applied to that file). That is arguably a security improvement, but it must be a deliberate, documented decision. Keep IN 3.0.0.

title: Exit codes: add code 3 for unaccepted incomplete coverage and a `--fail-on` policy so low-confidence entropy hits stop forcing exit 2
description: Two automation pain points. (1) 'registry/network/operational failure' and 'scan completed but coverage was incomplete' both exit 1, yet CI wants to retry the former and investigate the latter. (2) Any actionable finding, including `keyword_entropy` matches that the detector itself labels low confidence, produces exit 2; there is no way to gate CI on confidence (or on a minimum count) without post-processing JSON. Exit-code semantics are a documented stable contract, so this can only change in a major.

README.md:136-142 documents only codes 0/1/2.
proposed_fix: 3.0.0 exit contract: 0 clean; 1 invalid input/operational failure/persistence failure/cancellation; 2 actionable findings at or above the fail threshold; 3 scan finished but coverage incomplete and `--allow-partial` not given (no findings above threshold; findings take precedence and return 2). Add `--fail-on low|medium|high` (default `low`, i.e. today's behavior) and `--fail-on none` (report only). Update README table, OpenAPI is unaffected. Migration note: scripts treating any non-zero as failure keep working; scripts treating `1` as 'retryable' must add `3`.

Effort m (add a `goreleaser`-free matrix build of `.` for linux/darwin × amd64/arm64 and windows/amd64 with `-trimpath -ldflags=-s -w -X .../internal/cli.Version=$VERSION`, checksums, cosign sign-blob, attach to the release).
