title: No layer-digest reuse across targets in `--all-tags` and no parallel layer download — measure before changing; 3.x
description: Checked the code: `--all-tags` dedups only by root manifest digest (tags pointing at the same index share one scan); it does not reuse anything across distinct targets even though adjacent tags of one repository typically share most layers. Every manifest opens every layer from the registry again, sequentially. This is the single largest performance opportunity for sweeps. However, a correct cache is not trivial: `Replay` computes final-state and deleted-artifact semantics across the whole layer stack, so a per-layer cache must store the layer's parsed entry list plus per-file detector matches (bounded by MaxRetainedBytes-style limits) and re-run only the whiteout/final-state merge. Parallel downloads interact with the aggregate byte/retained-state bounds that make the scanner safe. Verdict: 3.x after benchmarks (plan follow-up #3); do not put either in 3.0.0.
evidence: internal/jobs/scan.go:344-350 `group, ok := groups[resolved.Digest]` groups tags by root digest only; :374-396 iterates `groupList` sequentially calling `scanTarget`. internal/layers/state.go:126-140 `for _, descriptor := range descriptors { ... stream, err := opener.OpenLayer(ctx, descriptor)` — sequential, one fetch per layer per manifest. internal/scanner/scan.go:404-425 the `OpenFunc` always calls `request.Registry.OpenBlob(...)`. `grep -rn 'layer.*cache|seenLayer|layerCache|dedup' internal/scanner internal/layers internal/jobs` (non-test) returns nothing.
proposed_fix: 3.x: add a deterministic benchmark (`BenchmarkRepositorySweepSharedLayers`) over a synthetic registry with N tags sharing K layers; then implement an in-memory per-scan `layerScanCache` keyed by layer digest holding `[]layers.Artifact` metadata + detector matches with a byte budget (`LAYERLEAK_MAX_LAYER_CACHE_BYTES`, default 0 = off in the first release), and only then consider bounded parallel prefetch (2 layers) behind a flag. Keep the digest verification per fetch.
verifier_note: jobs/scan.go:344-350 groups only by `resolved.Digest`; :374-396 sequential `scanTarget` loop; layers/state.go:120-141 `for _, descriptor := range descriptors { ... opener.OpenLayer(ctx, descriptor)` sequential; scanner/scan.go:404-410 always `request.Registry.OpenBlob`; grep for layerCache/seenLayer/dedup in non-test scanner/layers/jobs code returns nothing. Measure-first stance and the Replay final-state caveat are correct; 3.x.

title: Developer experience for 3.0.0: check in .golangci.yml (28 default-config issues today) and a Makefile mirroring the 12-command verification list; skip devcontainer, CODEOWNERS and release-please

title: Composite GitHub Action (action.yml) wrapping the CLI — 3.1, immediately after SARIF and binaries
description: The stated integration story for SARIF (PRD-09) is GitHub code scanning, yet the only install path is `go install`, which requires setting up a Go toolchain in every workflow. A composite action that downloads the signed binary for the runner (PRD-11), runs `layerleak scan --format sarif --output results.sarif --no-save`, and optionally calls upload-sarif is the lowest-effort adoption lever for CI users and is how gitleaks/trivy/grype are consumed. Value high, effort s once binaries exist, risk low (a thin shell wrapper with pinned checksum verification).
evidence: `ls action.yml` → No such file. README.md:53-57 the only CLI install is `go install github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest`. verify.yml:64+ 'Install and exercise CLI' installs via `go install` into `${RUNNER_TEMP}` — the same toolchain dependency every downstream user would inherit.
proposed_fix: 3.1: add `action.yml` (composite) with inputs `image`, `format`, `fail-on`, `allow-partial`, `version`; download `layerleak_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz` from the release, verify `checksums.txt` and the cosign signature, run the scan, expose `sarif-file` and `exit-code` outputs; document a 10-line workflow in README. Publish as `brumbelow/layerleak-action@v3` or from this repo with a `v3` floating tag managed by the release workflow.

title: After the /v3 move, `go install github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest` will silently keep installing v1.0.0 forever — mark the v1 module deprecated with a final v1 tag
description: Go resolves `@latest` for the un-suffixed module from v1.x tags only (v2.x tags without /v2 are ignored once a go.mod exists), so existing users and every blog/README copy of the current install line will keep getting v1.0.0 with no signal that v3 exists. Go supports a `// Deprecated: ...` comment on the `module` line, which `go get`/`go list -m -u` print; but it only takes effect from a new version of the un-suffixed module, i.e. a v1.0.1 tag whose go.mod carries the comment. The protected release workflow will by then accept only v3 tags, so this needs an explicit decision and a documented, one-off tag-only path.
evidence: go.mod:1 `module github.com/brumbelow/layerleak` with no deprecation comment. README.md:54 `go install github.com/brumbelow/layerleak@latest` is the only documented install command. Tags per context: v1.0.0 is the highest valid v1 tag; v2.x tags are invalid for the un-suffixed module. container-release.yml:103 will become v3-only under PRD-01.
proposed_fix: Alongside v3.0.0 (not before): cut `v1.0.1` from a `release/v1` branch whose only change is go.mod `// Deprecated: layerleak v1 is unmaintained; use github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3` plus a README pointer; publish it as a Go-module-only tag (no container image) via a documented manual procedure in RELEASING.md with the same signed-tag requirements, or add a narrowly scoped `deprecate-v1` job to the workflow. If the maintainer prefers never to touch v1 again, record that decision and rely on README/CHANGELOG only.

title: Foreign/non-distributable layer media types fail manifest validation as integrity errors, aborting the remaining platforms; layers/state.go foreign-layer branch is unreachable
description: ValidateImageManifest validates every layer with IsLayerMediaType, which excludes MediaTypeDockerSchema2ForeignLayer(Gzip) and the OCI `...layer.nondistributable.v1.tar+gzip` type even though the package defines those constants and layers.Replay has a dedicated `foreign layer media type is not supported` branch (state.go:131) that can never run. Because the failure is an *IntegrityError, scanner.Scan (scan.go:287) treats it as fatal and stops scanning the remaining manifests of the index. Legacy Windows images (anything built on foreign base layers, common before MCR switched to distributable layers) inside a multi-platform index therefore turn a linux scan into a partial/failed run with a misleading `descriptor_media_type_mismatch` diagnostic.
evidence: Probe: `FOREIGN ValidateImageManifest err=descriptor_media_type_mismatch for "layer[0]": expected "supported OCI media type", got "application/vnd.docker.image.rootfs.foreign.diff.tar.gzip"`; `NONDIST ... got "application/vnd.oci.image.layer.nondistributable.v1.tar+gzip"`. Scanner-level probe with linux+windows(foreign) index: `WINDOWS-INDEX status="partial" err=validate image manifest sha256:d35a...: descriptor_media_type_mismatch ... manifests=2 completed=1 failed=1`. integrity.go:136-139: `for index, descriptor := range value.Layers { if err := validateDescriptor(descriptor, IsLayerMediaType, ...) }`; layers/state.go:131-133 `if manifest.IsForeignLayerMediaType(descriptor.MediaType) { return ..., fmt.Errorf("foreign layer media type is not supported...") }`.
proposed_fix: Add MediaTypeOCIImageLayerNonDistributable(+Gzip/+Zstd) constants, let validateDescriptor for layers accept IsLayerMediaType || IsForeignLayerMediaType || nondistributable, and decide the policy in one place: either skip manifests containing foreign layers with a `foreign_layers_unsupported` platform diagnostic (status failed/partial for that platform only, not an IntegrityError so scan.go:287 does not abort the others), or download foreign layers from the registry blob endpoint when available (registries usually serve them) and only fall back to a diagnostic. Remove or make reachable the dead branch in layers/state.go:131 and add a scanner test with a linux+windows(foreign) index asserting the linux platform completes and the windows platform is reported, not aborted.
verifier_note: Probe: ValidateImageManifest on a manifest with a foreign gzip layer returns `descriptor_media_type_mismatch for "layer[0]" ... got "application/vnd.docker.image.rootfs.foreign.diff.tar.gzip"` and IsIntegrityError=true; same for the OCI nondistributable type. layers.Replay is called only from scanner/scan.go:397, after ValidateImageManifest at scan.go:486/506, so state.go:131-133 is unreachable in production. scan.go:287 returns on IsIntegrityError, aborting the remaining platforms. No README/CHANGELOG/SECURITY text documents foreign layers as unsupported (grep -i foreign -> only the code). Severity medium stands: it turns a legacy Windows entry in a multi-arch index into a whole-scan failure with a misleading tampering-class diagnostic.

title: Pinned transport dials only the first resolved address, builds a fresh Transport per request and disables keep-alive (TLS handshake per request, no multi-address fallback)
description: RoundTrip uses addresses[0] only, so a host whose first record (Go sorts IPv6 first under RFC 6724 when a global IPv6 source exists) is unreachable fails outright with no fallback to the other A/AAAA records—unlike net.Dialer's dual-stack fallback that the stock transport would use. Each request also clones the base Transport, sets DisableKeepAlives=true and a new Dialer, so every manifest, HEAD, token and blob request pays a TCP+TLS handshake, and validateOutboundURL plus RoundTrip resolve DNS twice per request. Repository sweeps (one HEAD per tag) and layer-heavy images are the most affected.
evidence: client.go:1070: `request.URL.Host = net.JoinHostPort(addresses[0].IP.String(), port)`; client.go:1072-1074: `transport := t.base.Clone(); transport.DisableKeepAlives = true; transport.DialContext = (&net.Dialer{Timeout: 30 * time.Second, KeepAlive: 30 * time.Second}).DialContext`. TLS probe against an httptest TLS server: `TLS(h2=false) requests=5 connections_opened=5 connections_closed=5` and `TLS(h2=true) requests=5 connections_opened=5 connections_closed=5 protos=map[HTTP/2.0:5]` (no reuse, no leak). TestClientRejectsDNSRebindingBeforeDial asserts `lookups != 2` i.e. two lookups per request.
proposed_fix: Keep one long-lived hardened Transport per Client and implement pinning in a custom DialContext: validate the address set once per request, store it in the request context, and have DialContext iterate the validated addresses (IPv6/IPv4 fallback, per-attempt timeout) instead of rewriting URL.Host. This restores connection reuse (keyed by hostname), removes the double lookup, and fixes REG-01's proxy path naturally. Add tests for fallback to the second address and for connection reuse across requests.
verifier_note: Code confirmed: client.go:1070 dials addresses[0] only; 1072-1074 clones the Transport per request with DisableKeepAlives=true and a fresh Dialer; doRequest->validateOutboundURL (354) and RoundTrip (1054) each call resolveOutbound, so two lookups per request (TestClientRejectsDNSRebindingBeforeDial asserts lookups == 2; my proxy probe also logged lookups=2). The auditor's TLS-reuse probe was not re-run, but the DisableKeepAlives line alone establishes a handshake per request. Fix direction (pin inside DialContext, keep one Transport) is sound and also resolves REG-01 for direct connections.

title: Platform selection has no OS-only selector or variant equivalence, so default scans pull Windows manifests (golang:1.25: two windows/amd64 manifests with 1.5 GB and 918 MB layers)
description: ParsePlatformSelector requires os/arch or os/arch/variant, and SelectDescriptors with an empty selector selects every scannable platform including windows/*. Live check of docker.io/library/golang:1.25 shows 16 entries incl. two windows/amd64 manifests whose layers are 1,523,059,351 and 917,726,084 bytes, so `layerleak scan golang:1.25` without --platform downloads and decompresses gigabytes of Windows base layers or aborts at the 4 GiB aggregate limit after the linux platforms succeeded. There is no way to say 'all linux platforms'. Platform.Matches also treats `linux/arm64/v8` as not matching a bare `linux/arm64` descriptor (and `linux/arm/v7` vs bare `linux/arm`), while containerd/Docker treat those as equivalent, so users copying buildx platform strings get 'platform not found'.
evidence: Live: `golang:1.25` index `count 16 ... windows amd64 10.0.26100.33296 sha256:b9bd6164d464; windows amd64 10.0.20348.5499 sha256:0385ba6437b7`; child manifest layers `application/vnd.docker.image.rootfs.diff.tar.gzip 1523059351`, `917726084`. Probe: `SELECTOR linux -> err=platform selector must be os/arch or os/arch/variant`; `SELECT "linux/arm64/v8" -> [sha256:222/linux/arm64/v8]` (bare linux/arm64 entry excluded); `SELECT "linux/arm" -> [v6 v7 bare]`. document.go:176-178 `parts := strings.Split(raw, "/"); if len(parts) < 2 || len(parts) > 3 {...}`; document.go:284-288 variant comparison.
proposed_fix: Accept `os` and `os/arch` selectors with wildcard semantics (e.g. `--platform linux`), consider defaulting to linux-only unless --platform names another OS (a v3 behaviour change worth a changelog entry), and normalise variants like containerd's platforms.Normalize (arm64→v8, arm→v7, amd64 variant ignored) before matching so `linux/arm64/v8` matches a bare `linux/arm64` descriptor and vice versa. Add tests for os-only selection and variant equivalence.
verifier_note: Live re-check via Docker Hub: library/golang:1.25 index has 16 entries including `windows amd64 10.0.26100.33296 sha256:b9bd6164d464` and `windows amd64 10.0.20348.5499 sha256:0385ba6437b7`. Probe: ParsePlatformSelector("linux") -> `platform selector must be os/arch or os/arch/variant`; SelectDescriptors("") selects windows/amd64; selector `linux/arm64/v8` excludes a bare `linux/arm64` descriptor (document.go:284-288). Additional consequence from code reading (not executed): a Windows base layer decompresses far beyond the default 512 MiB LAYERLEAK_MAX_LAYER_BYTES, so the windows platform fails with a limits error and scan.go:287 aborts the run after the linux platforms, i.e. a default `layerleak scan golang:1.25` cannot finish cleanly.

title: Registry/manifest tests do not cover retryable statuses, Link header shapes, challenge quoting, redirect-to-private/http rejection, the pinned transport against a real TLS server, sha512 through the client, or reference alias normalisation
description: client_test.go exercises timeouts, token refresh, pagination happy path, cycles, byte limits, DNS rebinding (unit level), allowlist kinds and cross-host Authorization stripping, but has no test for: isRetryableStatus (429/5xx) or backoff; nextLinkURL with multiple relations/unquoted rel/param order (REG-02 went unnoticed); parseBearerChallenge with quoted commas, escaped quotes, multiple headers (REG-07); a redirect whose Location resolves to a private address or downgrades to http being rejected end-to-end through doHTTP; pinnedTransport actually dialing (all client tests use roundTripFunc with AllowPrivateHosts=true, so the production transport path is only covered indirectly by cli/scan_test.go over plain http); sha512 digests flowing through ResolveManifest/OpenBlob; ResolveManifest's GET fallback computing the digest from the body; proxy behaviour (REG-01); multi-address selection (REG-05). manifest tests lack ParseReference cases for registry-1.docker.io/DOCKER.IO aliases (REG-08), foreign/nondistributable layers (REG-03), nested index entries (REG-11), variant equivalence (REG-12) and mixed-case media types (REG-13).
evidence: grep of internal/registry/client_test.go for `TooManyRequests|ServiceUnavailable|Retry` → no matches; only Link test shape is `</v2/library/app/tags/list?n=2&last=2.0>; rel="next"` (lines 312, 426, 522); only challenge-parsing test is TestUnsupportedAuthChallengeDoesNotEchoHeader (`Basic`); every client-level test passes `AllowPrivateHosts: true` except the four allowlist/DNS unit tests (784-901); probe TestProbePinnedTransportAgainstTLSServer shows an httptest TLS server with LookupIP→127.0.0.1 and AllowedPrivateRegistryHosts=[host] exercises the real pinned path (`protos=map[HTTP/2.0:5]`).
proposed_fix: Add table tests for each gap listed (they can reuse roundTripFunc/jsonResponse), an httptest-TLS-based test of pinnedTransport (allowlisted 127.0.0.1:port, RootCAs from server.Certificate()) covering success, redirect-to-private rejection, https→http downgrade rejection and multi-address fallback, a Proxy-func test asserting hostname CONNECT (after REG-01), and manifest tests for aliases, foreign layers, nested indexes and variants. Consider a fuzz target for parseBearerChallenge and nextLinkURL alongside the existing FuzzParseReference.
verifier_note: grep of client_test.go confirms: no TooManyRequests/ServiceUnavailable/Retry tests, Link header tested only in the exact `; rel="next"` shape (lines 312, 426, 522), challenge parsing tested only for `Basic`, all client-level tests use roundTripFunc with AllowPrivateHosts=true except lines 784-901. reference_test.go has no bare `registry-1.docker.io/<name>` case. Every gap maps to a confirmed defect above, so medium is justified.

title: A NUL byte in an image config Env/Label key aborts persistence of the entire scan
description: Image config JSON may legally contain "\u0000" inside Env entries or Label keys. scanner/scan.go:693-712 copies the key verbatim into findings.Input.Key (payload.prefix + ".env." + key); findings.sanitizedProvenance only applies strings.ToValidUTF8, which does not remove NUL (NUL is valid UTF-8). The value then reaches finding_occurrences.source_key and the JSON-marshalled result_json. PostgreSQL TEXT rejects 0x00 and JSONB rejects \u0000, so upsertFindingOccurrence / insertScanRun fail and the whole SaveScan transaction rolls back: no scan_run, no findings, no repository update for that image. A hostile image can therefore evade the audit trail while the scan itself appears to run.
evidence: Probe TestProbeNULByteInKeyFailsSaveScan against PG 16.14: `SaveScan with NUL in key -> err = upsert finding occurrence sha256:bbbb.../fingerprint-one: pq: invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8": 0x00 (22021)`; scan_runs count stayed 0. Probe TestProbeNULByteInResultJSONFailsSaveScan: `insert scan run for library/app: pq: unsupported Unicode escape sequence (22P05)`. scanner/scan.go:693-699: `key, _, found := strings.Cut(entry, "=") ... Key: payload.prefix + ".env." + key`; findings.go:581: `redacted := strings.ToValidUTF8(builder.String(), "�")` (no NUL handling). grep for NUL sanitization in internal/scanner, internal/findings, internal/manifest returned nothing.
proposed_fix: Sanitize at the source so fingerprints, live API JSON and stored rows agree: in scanner.scanMetadataWithBudget replace U+0000 (and other C0 controls) in Env/Label keys before building findings.Input.Key, and in findings.sanitizedProvenance/boundedSanitizedProvenance/contextSnippet apply strings.ReplaceAll(value, "\x00", "�") before the length cap. Keep a defensive strip in storage.validateScanRecord for Key/FilePath/SourceLocation/ContextSnippet/RedactedValue/Value/RawSnippet and tag names. For ResultJSON, sanitize the strings of the jobs.Result in BuildScanRecord before json.Marshal (do not regex the encoded JSON). Add the integration test (NUL in Key and in ResultJSON must still produce a scan_run).
verifier_note: Reproduced on a fresh PostgreSQL 16.14 (scratch cluster, scratchpad copy of the repo): SaveScan with Key "config.env.A\x00B" -> `upsert finding occurrence sha256:bbbb.../fp-1: pq: invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8": 0x00 (22021)`, and afterwards scan_runs=0 repositories=0; ResultJSON containing "\u0000" -> `insert scan run for library/probe: pq: unsupported Unicode escape sequence (22P05)`. The JSON path is live: jobs.Result.Findings (internal/jobs/scan.go:143, json:"findings") carries findings.Finding.Key (findings.go:91, json:"key") and RedactedResult only nils DetailedFindings (scanservice/record.go:258); encoding/json decodes \u0000 in an image config into a NUL byte and re-encodes it as \u0000 (probe). Vectors are narrower than stated: layer file paths with NUL are rejected (internal/layers/state.go:1089) and registry tag names are validated (internal/registry/client.go:310 isValidTag), so Env/Label keys (scanner/scan.go:701,718) and detector context around a match are the live inputs. One nuance: the API does not fail silently to the caller (handler.go:725 maps scanservice.IsSaveError), but the scan is not persisted at all.

title: SaveScan performs two serial round trips per finding; large scans can exceed the 2-minute write timeout
description: The findings loop calls upsertFinding then upsertFindingOccurrence once per DetailedFinding, each a separate QueryRow/Exec round trip inside one transaction bounded by writeTimeout (default 2m). LAYERLEAK_MAX_FINDINGS_PER_SCAN defaults to 10,000, so the worst legitimate scan needs ~20,000 sequential round trips plus per-manifest and per-tag statements. Measured locally at 0.70 ms/finding on loopback with fsync=off (7.0 s total); on a managed database with 2-5 ms RTT this becomes 40-100+ s of pure latency and can cross the 2-minute deadline, at which point the whole transaction rolls back and the scan is not persisted at all.
evidence: postgres.go:190-198: `for _, item := range findings.DeduplicateDetailed(record.DetailedFindings) { findingID, err := upsertFinding(...); ... upsertFindingOccurrence(...) }`. Probe TestProbeBulkInsertTiming: `SaveScan(10000 findings, loopback TCP, fsync=off) took 7.013936559s (0.70 ms/finding)`. storage.go:205: `defaultWriteTimeout = 2 * time.Minute`; config.go:201: `LAYERLEAK_MAX_FINDINGS_PER_SCAN` default 10000.
proposed_fix: The unnest/multi-row ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE approach needs one extra step the auditor omitted: PostgreSQL raises `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time` when a single statement contains two rows with the same conflict key. findings.DeduplicateDetailed dedups by a snippet key, so the same (manifest_digest, fingerprint) appears once per occurrence; the findings batch must be collapsed to distinct (manifest_digest, fingerprint) (keeping the newest redacted/raw value) before the multi-row upsert, and the occurrences batch collapsed on the 15-column identity (which excludes raw_snippet). Chunk at ~500-1000 rows, keep the existing sorted order, and keep per-chunk statements inside the one transaction so atomicity is unchanged.
verifier_note: postgres.go:190-198 issues one QueryRow (upsertFinding, RETURNING id) plus one Exec (upsertFindingOccurrence) per deduplicated finding, all serial inside one transaction bounded by withTimeout(ctx, writeTimeout) (postgres.go:152; default 2m at storage.go:205). LAYERLEAK_MAX_FINDINGS_PER_SCAN defaults to 10000 (config.go:201). 20000 round trips at 2-5 ms RTT is 40-100 s, so the arithmetic holds; the full-transaction rollback on deadline is exactly what SaveScan does.

title: Migrations set no lock_timeout/statement_timeout and the migrate binary has no deadline, so 0004 can block all API traffic indefinitely
description: applyMigration runs each file inside a plain transaction with no `SET LOCAL lock_timeout` or `statement_timeout`. Migration 0004 executes `LOCK TABLE finding_occurrences IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE`, several `ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT` (ACCESS EXCLUSIVE) and two `CREATE INDEX` (SHARE). If any session holds even a read transaction on those tables, the ALTER waits in the lock queue and every later reader queues behind it, stalling the running v2.5.0 API replicas that README tells operators may keep serving until the new version is ready. cmd/migrate only cancels on SIGINT/SIGTERM, so a compose `migrate` job hangs forever with no diagnostic.
evidence: Probe TestProbeMigrationBlocksBehindOpenTransaction (0001-0003 applied, one idle-in-transaction reader holding an ACCESS SHARE lock): `0004 behind an idle-in-transaction reader: elapsed=2.002s err=apply migration 0004_storage_hardening: pq: canceling statement due to user request (57014)` — it only returned because the probe's context expired. migrate.go:257-277 has no timeout statements; cmd/migrate/main.go:35 uses only `signal.NotifyContext(...)`; migrations/0004_storage_hardening.up.sql:11 `LOCK TABLE finding_occurrences IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE;` and :174-239 ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT.
proposed_fix: Use `SET LOCAL lock_timeout` (e.g. 15s, configurable) in applyMigration and retry a bounded number of times on SQLSTATE 55P03 (lock_not_available) since the per-migration transaction rolls back cleanly. Be careful with statement_timeout: 0004's dedup/repair UPDATE/DELETE and VALIDATE CONSTRAINT statements scale with table size, so either leave it unset or make it opt-in with a generous default. Add LAYERLEAK_MIGRATION_TIMEOUT to cmd/migrate and a 'waiting for lock' progress line; document quiescing the API before 0004 on populated databases. See also DB-20.
verifier_note: Reproduced: with 0001-0003 applied and one idle-in-transaction session holding ACCESS SHARE on finding_occurrences, RunMigrations under a 2 s context returned `apply migration 0004_storage_hardening: pq: canceling statement due to user request (57014)` after 2.002 s and left 0 advisory locks; without that context it would wait indefinitely. applyMigration (migrate.go:257-277) sets no lock_timeout/statement_timeout and cmd/migrate/main.go:35 has only signal.NotifyContext. 0004 takes LOCK TABLE SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE (:11) then ACCESS EXCLUSIVE via ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT (:174-239), so every later reader queues behind it. README:85-90 does not literally say replicas 'may keep serving' but it does instruct operators to migrate before starting the new API version while the old one remains, so the overlap scenario is the documented one.

title: Every documented connection string uses sslmode=disable and the implicit lib/pq default skips certificate verification
description: README's production `docker run` example, the checkout examples, .env.example, docker-compose.yml, CI and CONTRIBUTING all use `?sslmode=disable`. When sslmode is omitted, lib/pq defaults to `require`, which sets tls.Config.InsecureSkipVerify = true (encryption without authentication, MITM-able). Nothing in storage.PostgresConfig.Validate warns about disable/require/prefer/allow, and no doc mentions verify-full or sslrootcert. For a tool whose database may hold raw secrets (LAYERLEAK_PERSIST_RAW_SECRETS=1) this guidance is a security regression waiting to be copy-pasted.
evidence: README.md:401 `-e LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_URL='postgres://<user>:<password>@<host>:5432/layerleak?sslmode=disable'` (production docker run); README.md:277,320; .env.example:65; docker-compose.yml:44,96,121. lib/pq v1.12.3 ssl.go:84-86: `case mode == "" || mode == SSLModeRequire || mode == SSLModePrefer: // Skip TLS's own verification since it requires full verification. tlsConf.InsecureSkipVerify = true`. Probe with sslmode omitted: `ping postgres: pq: SSL is not enabled on the server` (i.e. default is require). storage.go:220-268 Validate() has no sslmode handling.
proposed_fix: Docs: change the production docker run example to `sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=/path/ca.pem` (or mount the CA), keep `disable` only in the compose/CI examples with an explicit comment that it is acceptable solely on the private compose network, and add a short 'TLS to PostgreSQL' paragraph to README and SECURITY.md. Code (3.0.0 opportunity): in Validate()/NewPostgresStore log a warning when sslmode is disable/allow/prefer/require and the host is not loopback or a unix socket, and optionally add LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_REQUIRE_TLS_VERIFY=1 to refuse those modes.
verifier_note: lib/pq v1.12.3 conn.go:294 sets `mode = SSLModeRequire` when sslmode is absent and ssl.go:84-86 sets `tlsConf.InsecureSkipVerify = true` for "", require and prefer. All documented DSNs use sslmode=disable (README.md:277,320,401; .env.example:65; docker-compose.yml:44,96,121; CONTRIBUTING.md:32) and storage.go:220-268 Validate() has no sslmode handling. The production `docker run` example at README.md:401 is the one that matters.

title: Integration coverage misses concurrency, NUL input, tie-break pagination on scans/findings, newer-ledger rejection, 0004 rollback re-adoption, lock release on cancellation, real-DB API tests and -race
description: The suite covers happy paths, drift detection and legacy adoption well, but the following behaviours are untested in-repo (I verified each with probes in a scratchpad copy): concurrent SaveScan across repositories sharing a manifest (advisory-lock/ordering deadlock freedom); NUL bytes in provenance (DB-01 fails today); pagination stability with equal last_seen_at for ListRepositoryScans, ListRepositoryFindings and GetFinding occurrences (only ListRepositories has a tie test); checkSchemaVersion/RunMigrations rejecting a 0005 ledger row; 0004 down migration followed by RunMigrations re-adopting 0001-0003 and re-applying 0004; RunMigrations honouring context cancellation while waiting on the advisory lock and leaving no lock behind; partial-0004 marker detection error path. internal/api tests use stubReadStore exclusively, so no HTTP handler is ever exercised against a real PostgreSQL; cmd/healthcheck has no httptest-based success/failure test. CI runs -race only with -short, so integration code never runs under the race detector, and integration tests skip silently (t.Skip) when LAYERLEAK_TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset even without -short.
evidence: grep 'sync\.|go func' internal/storage/*_test.go -> none; the only tie test is TestPostgresStoreListRepositoriesPaginatesTiedRegistries (storage_integration_test.go:826); grep '0005' internal/storage -> none; TestMigrationFilesApplyAndRollback (line 21) applies all downs then only checks `tableExists("repositories")`; internal/api/handler_test.go:587 `type stubReadStore struct`; cmd/healthcheck/main_test.go has only argument/address tests; .github/workflows/verify.yml:63 `go test -short -race ./... -count=1` vs :236 `go test ./... -count=1` (no -race); storage_integration_test.go:1111-1114 `if baseURL == "" { t.Skip(...) }`. Probe results: TestProbeConcurrentSaveScan `concurrent failures = 0` (24 goroutines, 2 repos, 1 finding, 2 occurrences, 24 scan_runs), TestProbeFindingsPaginationTies `pagination stable for 7 tied findings`, TestProbeSchemaVersionRejectsNewerLedgerRow, TestProbeDownFourThenMigrateUpReadopts `Applied:[0004_storage_hardening]`, TestProbeMigrationLockContentionHonorsContext `advisory locks still held for migration key: 0`.
proposed_fix: Port the probe tests into storage_integration_test.go (concurrency, NUL, ties for scans/findings/occurrences, newer ledger, 0004 down->up, lock release, partial-0004 marker), add an internal/api integration test that wires NewHandler to a real PostgresStore (behind the same LAYERLEAK_TEST_DATABASE_URL gate) covering /readyz, repositories, scans, findings, and add an httptest-based cmd/healthcheck test. Run the postgres CI job with `-race`, and make the postgres job fail (not skip) when the env var is missing, e.g. a guard test that asserts LAYERLEAK_TEST_DATABASE_URL is set when CI=true.
verifier_note: All evidence checks: no goroutines or sync in storage tests; only ListRepositories has a tie test (storage_integration_test.go:826); no '0005' anywhere in internal/storage; TestMigrationFilesApplyAndRollback (:21) only checks tableExists("repositories") after the downs; handler_test.go:587 stubReadStore is the only API store; cmd/healthcheck/main_test.go has two argument/address tests; verify.yml:63 `go test -short -race` vs :236 `go test ./... -count=1`; integrationDatabaseURL skips at :1113 when the env var is unset. I ran the full storage suite against PostgreSQL 16.14 both normally (all 60 tests pass, 1.98 s) and with -race (passes), so there is no latent race today, but the gap in CI is real.

title: Shipped migration files are byte-frozen by the ledger but nothing guards them against edits or line-ending drift
description: The ledger stores SHA-256 over the raw bytes of each 000N.up.sql (migrate.go:181-186) and validateAppliedMigrations rejects any mismatch with `migration %s checksum changed` (migrate.go:238-240) with no override. Any byte change to the four shipped files, such as a trailing-newline or whitespace cleanup, a license header, a formatter pass, or a CRLF checkout (there is no .gitattributes or .editorconfig in the repository) used to build a local image, makes RunMigrations and therefore every API startup fail against every existing database. Nothing pins the current checksums in a test and no document states that migrations/*.sql are immutable once released. GitHub confirms 0001-0003 are blob-identical from v1.0.0 through HEAD today, so the contract has held by luck rather than by a guard.
evidence: migrate.go:181 `digest := sha256.Sum256(body)` over os.ReadFile bytes; :238 `if row.Checksum != migration.Checksum { return fmt.Errorf("migration %s checksum changed", version) }`; `ls .gitattributes .editorconfig` -> neither exists; grep for the current digests (cefae744..., 53721c24..., 05bdabd5..., 16e385fd...) or `Checksum ==` in internal/storage/*_test.go, cmd/, scripts/ -> no pin; CONTRIBUTING.md/RELEASING.md contain no immutability rule for migrations/.
proposed_fix: Add TestShippedMigrationChecksumsAreFrozen in internal/storage that asserts the SHA-256 of each committed migrations/000N.up.sql equals a hard-coded golden value (cefae744e62b9b052f0207507067d95e85a273dd4a4e3ab565b48ac7fdcd5f43, 53721c24c993d360b88b3cf3891e0f9aca8083c403d9d8f67ecef484775007d5, 05bdabd562a6aa6b01c8ae52422903e035f0322d71b46052b3f6b5e2bc46cd0c, 16e385fdff86018a6a69759a76753531ad55c0210df1e2c23bb9e6ddde426f65) so an accidental edit fails CI with an explanatory message; add `.gitattributes` with `migrations/*.sql text eol=lf`; optionally normalize CRLF to LF in loadMigrationFiles before hashing (backward compatible for LF files); state in CONTRIBUTING.md and RELEASING.md that released migration files are immutable and new behaviour goes in a new numbered file.

title: No golangci-lint in CI and no .golangci config; default run reports 28 issues
description: `golangci-lint run ./...` (v2.5.0, default linters) exits 1 with 28 issues: errcheck 22, staticcheck 5, ineffassign 1. verify.yml runs only `go vet`, tests and govulncheck; `grep -rn golangci .github` finds nothing. revive.toml exists but is only consumed by .codacy.yml. A release branch with a green CI therefore still carries lint debt that any contributor running the standard tool will see.
evidence: `golangci-lint run ./...` -> `28 issues: * errcheck: 22 * ineffassign: 1 * staticcheck: 5`; verify.yml:57 `run: go vet ./...`, no lint step; `.codacy.yml:8:  revive:` is the only revive reference.
proposed_fix: Add a `.golangci.yml` (version 2) enabling errcheck/govet/staticcheck/unused/ineffassign plus revive with the rules from revive.toml (exported and package-comments disabled), exclude the deferred-Close errcheck pattern or fix them, and add a `golangci-lint run` step to verify.yml pinned to v2.5.0.

title: Five packages under 30% coverage; cmd/api and cmd/scanner have no tests at all
description: `go test -short -cover` per package sorted ascending: cmd/api 0.0% (no test files), cmd/scanner 0.0% (no test files), internal/limits 13.6%, cmd/healthcheck 24.1%, cmd/migrate 25.0%, internal/storage 30.8% (integration tests gated behind testing.Short so storage is effectively untested in the default CI job), cmd/purge 39.3%. Everything else is 67-99%. internal/limits is the budget/overflow logic that guards the untrusted-input paths and is the least covered library package.
evidence: coverage output: `0.0 cmd/api`, `0.0 cmd/scanner`, `13.6 internal/limits`, `24.1 cmd/healthcheck`, `25.0 cmd/migrate`, `30.8 internal/storage`; `grep -rln testing.Short()` -> only internal/storage/storage_integration_test.go
proposed_fix: Add table tests for internal/limits (OverflowProbeLimit, budget add/overflow paths); add a config/flag parsing test for cmd/api and cmd/scanner main (extract run(args, env) like cmd/migrate does); ensure the Postgres integration job in verify.yml actually runs storage tests (it does run `go test ./... -count=1` at line 236, so also publish that coverage rather than only the -short profile at codacy.yml:116).

title: OpenAPI ScanSummary documents 8 of 22 emitted fields and hides the rest behind additionalProperties:true; status/mode enums and constant error_message undocumented
description: scanSummaryItem emits id, requested_reference, resolved_reference, requested_digest, mode, status, error_message, scanned_at, tags_enumerated, tags_resolved, tags_failed, target_count, completed_target_count, failed_target_count, partial_target_count, manifest_count, completed_manifest_count, failed_manifest_count, total_findings, unique_fingerprints, suppressed_findings_count, suppressed_unique_fingerprints. The spec lists only the first eight, declares `status`/`mode` as free strings (they are the enums completed|partial|failed and reference|repository), and does not say that `error_message` is never the stored message but the constant "scan did not complete successfully" whenever any error was recorded. Clients generated from the spec lose 14 fields.
evidence:
internal/api/handler.go:127-150 (22 json fields) vs web/docs/openapi.yaml:909-931:
    ScanSummary:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: true
      required: [id, requested_reference, mode, status, scanned_at]
      properties: id, requested_reference, resolved_reference, requested_digest, mode, status, error_message, scanned_at
internal/api/handler.go:596-599:
  if strings.TrimSpace(item.ErrorMessage) != "" { errorMessage = "scan did not complete successfully" }
proposed_fix: Document all 22 fields, set additionalProperties:false, `status: $ref ResultStatus`, `mode: enum [reference, repository]`, describe error_message as the fixed marker string. Add GET /api/v1/scans/{id} and list fixtures to web/testdata/api-contract.json so validate_docs.py checks them like the POST fixtures.
verifier_note: Field count verified: handler.go:127-150 emits 22 fields; openapi.yaml:909-931 documents 8 under additionalProperties:true; status/mode have no enums; handler.go:596-599 makes error_message a constant marker. The spec is therefore permissive and incomplete rather than false (fixtures would still validate), so this is a completeness gap that costs generated clients 14 fields, not a contract contradiction — low rather than medium.

title: TagResult.status enum and sanitised error/message strings undocumented in OpenAPI
description: jobs emits TagResult.status values `scanned`, `resolved`, `failed` (spec: plain string). sanitizeResultErrors rewrites every `error`/`error_message` value to "scan step failed" and every diagnostic `message` to one of four fixed strings, so TagResult.error, TargetResult.error, PlatformResult.error and Diagnostic.message are effectively enums in API output, while the spec (and the shared CLI result schema description) presents them as free text. Consumers cannot know that the API deliberately strips operational detail that the CLI keeps.
evidence:
internal/jobs/scan.go:244,316,329,341: Status: "scanned" / "failed" / "resolved"
internal/api/handler.go:929-963 (sanitizeResultErrors / safeDiagnosticMessage): item[key] = "scan step failed"; fixed messages for files_skipped_oversize, max_findings_exceeded, max_raw_finding_bytes_exceeded.
web/docs/openapi.yaml:650-653: status: type: string / error: type: string (no enum, no description).
proposed_fix: Add `enum: [scanned, resolved, failed]` to TagResult.status; add descriptions to TagResult.error, TargetResult.error, PlatformResult.error and Diagnostic.message stating that the API replaces detail with neutral fixed strings (list them). Consider keeping the diagnostic `code` as the machine-readable signal and say so.
verifier_note: jobs/scan.go:244,316,329,341 emit exactly scanned/failed/resolved; handler.go:929-963 rewrites every error/error_message value to 'scan step failed' and diagnostic messages to one of four fixed strings; openapi.yaml:650-653 types them as plain strings with no description.

title: Parameter docs disagree with handler: Repository says %2F is required, Limit says max 200 but server clamps
description: The Repository path parameter instructs clients to percent-encode `/` as `%2F`, but the handler is a subtree route that accepts literal slashes (`/api/v1/repositories/library/app/scans`, which is what all tests and README examples use) and percent-encoded ones alike. Limit declares `maximum: 200`, implying 400 for larger values, while the server silently clamps (probe: `limit=500` -> 200 with `"limit": 200`). README says "capped at 200" so README and spec disagree with each other.
evidence:
web/docs/openapi.yaml:284: description: Repository path, for example `library/alpine`. Percent-encode path separators as `%2F` in request URLs.
web/docs/openapi.yaml:301-304: minimum: 1 / maximum: 200 / default: 50
internal/api/handler.go:671-673: if parsed > maxPageLimit { parsed = maxPageLimit }
handler_test.go:360: "/api/v1/repositories/library/app/findings?disposition=suppressed&limit=500&offset=2" expects store.limit == 200.
proposed_fix: Reword Repository: "Repository path such as `library/alpine`; literal `/` and `%2F` are both accepted." For Limit either drop `maximum` and describe clamping, or make the server return 400 for >200 (a v2-style change). Keep README/spec/handler saying the same thing.
verifier_note: Probe: GET /api/v1/repositories/library%2Fapp/scans and the literal-slash form both reach the store as `library/app`, so the %2F instruction at openapi.yaml:284 is unnecessary rather than wrong. handler.go:671-673 clamps limit>200 while openapi.yaml:303 declares maximum:200 (implying 400); README.md:362-363 says 'capped at 200', matching the handler and contradicting the spec.

title: OpenAPI omits 405 (Allow header), unknown-route 404 and the always-present Cache-Control/X-Content-Type-Options headers
description: Every path answers wrong methods with 405 JSON `method_not_allowed` plus `Allow`, unknown routes get 404 JSON `not_found`, and the middleware sets `Cache-Control: no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on every response. None of this is in the spec, which only documents X-Request-ID.
evidence:
internal/api/handler.go:813-815: Set("X-Request-ID"...), Set("Cache-Control", "no-store"), Set("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
internal/api/handler.go:829-834: writer.Header().Set("Allow", allowed); 405 method_not_allowed
Probe: OPTIONS /api/v1/scans -> 405 Allow="POST"; GET /api/v2/scans/1 -> 404 not_found.
proposed_fix: Add `components.responses.MethodNotAllowed` (with `Allow` header) and reference it via a `default` response on each operation; add a top-level note or per-response headers for Cache-Control and X-Content-Type-Options.
verifier_note: handler.go:813-815 sets X-Request-ID, Cache-Control: no-store, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on every response; handler.go:829-834 writes Allow + 405 JSON; probe: OPTIONS /api/v1/scans -> 405 Allow=POST JSON. None appear in openapi.yaml. Also add the 301 path-cleaning redirect found in API-24 to this documentation work.

title: Repository subtree routing double-decodes, accepts non-OCI names, and treats /api/v1/repositories/scans as repository "scans"
description: repositoryPathValue trims the prefix/suffix from `request.URL.Path` (already percent-decoded by net/url) and then calls `url.PathUnescape` again, so `library%252Fapp` becomes `library/app` (probe confirmed). It performs no OCI repository-name validation, so `UPPER/Case Name` is forwarded to Postgres and returns an always-empty 200 instead of 400. Because the suffix match runs before the prefix strip, `/api/v1/repositories/scans` is interpreted as repository `scans` (probe: 200 `"repository": "scans"`), although a repository named scans lives at `/repositories/scans/scans`. None of these are exploitable (the value only reaches a parameterised query) but they are sloppy contract edges to fix before a major.
evidence:
internal/api/handler.go:647-648:
  rawRepository := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(path, prefix), suffix)
  repository, err := url.PathUnescape(strings.Trim(rawRepository, "/"))
Probe output: GET /api/v1/repositories/library%252Fapp/scans -> store.repository="library/app"; GET /api/v1/repositories/UPPER/Case%20Name/scans -> 200 repository "UPPER/Case Name"; GET /api/v1/repositories/scans -> 200 repository "scans".
proposed_fix: As proposed; note that removing the second PathUnescape changes behaviour for clients that today send `%252F` (acceptable in a major, mention in CHANGELOG). Validate against the distribution path grammar and return 400 invalid_request; require the suffix to be a separate segment so `/repositories/scans` and `/repositories/findings` return 404. Add tests for all three.
verifier_note: All three behaviours reproduced against the real handler: `library%252Fapp` -> store.repository `library/app` (double decode at handler.go:648); `/api/v1/repositories/scans` -> 200 repository 'scans' and `/api/v1/repositories/findings` -> 200 repository 'findings' (suffix test at handler.go:407-410 runs before the prefix strip); `UPPER/Case%20Name` -> 200 forwarded verbatim. Values only reach parameterised queries (read_postgres.go), so not exploitable.

title: /readyz runs full pg_catalog schema-contract validation on every probe with no caching
description: Each readiness probe does Ping + to_regclass + SELECT schema_migrations + three catalog queries (columns, constraints, indexes) against pg_attribute/pg_constraint/pg_index. The Docker HEALTHCHECK fires every 10 s, Kubernetes typically every 5-10 s per probe type, and load balancers add their own; this is constant catalog load for a check whose answer changes only on migration. There is no cache and no way to make the hot path cheaper.
evidence:
internal/storage/migrate.go:1029-1038: Ready -> PingContext -> checkSchemaVersion
migrate.go:988-1026: tableExistsContext + SELECT version FROM schema_migrations + validateSchemaContract
migrate.go:664-672: requireSchemaColumns, requireSchemaConstraints, requireSchemaIndexes (each a pg_catalog query)
Dockerfile:45: HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s ...
proposed_fix: Cache the readiness result in the Handler for a short TTL (e.g. 5 s, configurable LAYERLEAK_API_READINESS_CACHE) or run the full contract validation at startup and every N minutes in the background while the probe path does only Ping + ledger check. Keep the exact-schema semantics documented in README.
verifier_note: migrate.go:1029-1038 Ready -> PingContext -> checkSchemaVersion; :988-1026 does to_regclass, SELECT version FROM schema_migrations, then validateSchemaContract (migrate.go:664-672: three pg_catalog queries). Dockerfile:45 HEALTHCHECK every 10 s; compose every 10 s. Unauthenticated /readyz hammering is also a cheap way to load the catalog, which argues for the cache.

title: Contract choices worth batching into a future /api/v2 (do not silently change in /api/v1)
description: Several current behaviours are defensible but awkward and can only change with a path-version bump: (a) 429 `scan_capacity_exceeded` for server-side saturation; 429 signals per-client rate limiting, 503 + Retry-After is the semantic for capacity; (b) 408 for cancellation (see API-03); (c) findings always carry `"platform": {}` because `omitempty` on a struct is a no-op; Go 1.24+ `omitzero` fixes it but changes ScanResult and requires result_schema_version 2; (d) `error_message` in ScanSummary is always a constant; (e) limit>200 clamps instead of 400; (f) `repository` in list responses echoes the raw client string rather than the normalised one, and `registry` is not echoed. The module major (/v3) does not require any of these; /api/v1 should remain frozen for 3.0.0.
evidence:
handler.go:324-325: Retry-After 5 + StatusTooManyRequests
handler.go:743: StatusRequestTimeout for context.Canceled
internal/findings/findings.go:88: Platform manifest.Platform `json:"platform,omitempty"`; fixtures web/testdata/api/scan-completed.json:31: "platform": {}
handler.go:596-599 constant error_message
handler.go:671-673 clamp
proposed_fix: Record these in a docs/api-v2.md backlog (or CHANGELOG 'Compatibility' notes) and ship 3.0.0 with /api/v1 unchanged except bug fixes and additive fields. If you do decide to open /api/v2 now, mount both prefixes on the same mux with the v1 handlers delegating, and bump result_schema_version to 2 for the platform/omitzero change.
verifier_note: handler.go:324-325 (429), :743 (408), :596-599 (constant error_message), :671-673 (clamp) verified; findings.go:88 `Platform manifest.Platform json:"platform,omitempty"` is a no-op on a struct and web/testdata/api/scan-*.json lines 31/44/36 show `"platform": {}`. The same no-op exists on findingOccurrenceItem.Platform (handler.go:174), so GET /api/v1/findings/{id} occurrences also emit `platform: {}`; include it in the omitzero/result_schema_version-2 change.

title: Container smoke in CI/release only probes /readyz and /health; no scan or read endpoint is exercised against real Postgres
description: The post-build container test waits for /readyz, curls /health, and checks that scan_runs exists. It never POSTs to /api/v1/scans (even an invalid body to get a 400 JSON envelope), never hits /api/v1/repositories, and never checks 404/405 JSON shape, so a routing or JSON regression in the shipped image would pass the release gate. container-release.yml line 891 does the same.
evidence:
.github/workflows/verify.yml:347-357:
  if curl --fail --silent http://127.0.0.1:18080/readyz >/dev/null; then break; fi ...
  curl --fail --silent http://127.0.0.1:18080/health
  test "$(docker exec ... "SELECT to_regclass('public.scan_runs') IS NOT NULL")" = "t"
.github/workflows/container-release.yml:891: same readyz loop.
proposed_fix: Extend the smoke: `curl -sS -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"reference":"https://bad"}' .../api/v1/scans` expecting 400 and `"code": "invalid_request"`; `GET /api/v1/repositories` expecting 200 `{"repositories": []`; `GET /nope` expecting 404 JSON; `PUT /api/v1/scans` expecting 405 with `Allow: POST`. Optionally run a real scan against a tiny registry:2 container seeded with a one-layer image to cover the full persist path.
verifier_note: verify.yml:347-357 and container-release.yml:884-899 only loop on /readyz, curl /health and check to_regclass('public.scan_runs'). No API route beyond the health endpoints is exercised in the shipped image.

title: Panic recovery swallows http.ErrAbortHandler and turns it into a 500 JSON body
description: net/http's convention is that a handler panicking with http.ErrAbortHandler aborts the response silently (no log, connection closed). The middleware recovers every value, logs it at Error, and writes a 500 envelope. Probe confirmed the sentinel is not re-panicked. Also the panic value/stack is not logged (only `%T`), which makes real panics hard to debug.
proposed_fix: `if recovered == http.ErrAbortHandler { panic(recovered) }` before logging. Log `debug.Stack()` (stack frames contain no secrets) alongside panic_type; keep the value itself out of the log if you fear secret material in error strings.
verifier_note: Reproduced: a handler panicking with http.ErrAbortHandler yields 500 JSON `internal_error` and an ERROR log line (handler.go:817-824 recovers every value, logs only %T, never re-panics). The server also then finishes the chunked response, so a mid-body panic looks like a complete response to the client.

title: http.Server has no ErrorLog and cmd/api prints startup errors as plain text, breaking JSON-only logging
description: slog is configured with a JSON handler on stderr, but net/http's internal logger (TLS/handshake/`http: Accept error`, `http: panic serving` for panics outside the middleware) falls back to the `log` package in plain text, and cmd/api/main.go writes the fatal startup error with fmt.Fprintln. Log shippers expecting one JSON object per line will choke on these lines.
proposed_fix: Set `ErrorLog: slog.NewLogLogger(logger.Handler(), slog.LevelError)` on the server; in Run() log the fatal error via slog.Error before returning (main can still exit 1). Consider a `--version` flag on cmd/api mirroring the CLI.
verifier_note: run.go:63-76 constructs http.Server without ErrorLog; cmd/api/main.go:11-13 prints the fatal error with fmt.Fprintln while run.go:111 configures a JSON slog handler on the same stderr.

title: List responses do not echo the effective registry filter and the registry query is not validated
description: `?registry=` is forwarded verbatim (probe: `" GHCR.IO "` reaches the store, which trims/lowercases and maps docker.io aliases). The response contains `repository`, `limit`, `offset` but not the registry actually used, so a client cannot confirm which registry its page came from, and an invalid host string yields a silently empty 200.
evidence:
internal/api/handler.go:433: registry := request.URL.Query().Get("registry")
internal/api/handler.go:88-93: repositoryScansResponse{Repository, Scans, Limit, Offset} (no Registry)
internal/storage/read_postgres.go:16-27: normalizeRegistryFilter trims/lowercases and defaults to docker.io.
proposed_fix: Validate `registry` as a hostname[:port] (reuse manifest's registry validation) and return 400 otherwise; add an additive `registry` field (the normalised value) to RepositoryScansResponse and RepositoryFindingsResponse and document it in openapi.yaml.
verifier_note: handler.go:433/477 forward the raw query value; repositoryScansResponse (handler.go:88-93) and repositoryFindingsResponse (:102-108) have no registry field; read_postgres.go:16-27 normalises/lowercases and maps Docker Hub aliases server-side so the client cannot see the effective value.

title: No version/build information is exposed by the API
description: /health returns `{"status":"ok"}` only. Operators running several tags (3.0.0-rc.1 soak next to 2.5.0) cannot ask a running instance which build it is; the CLI has a version flag but the API binary does not.
evidence:
internal/api/handler.go:252-254:
  func (h *Handler) handleHealth(...) { writeJSON(writer, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "ok"}) }
proposed_fix: Add `GET /version` (or `version`/`commit` fields on /health, additive) populated from `debug.ReadBuildInfo()` / `-ldflags -X` in the Dockerfile build; document in openapi.yaml and RELEASING.md smoke steps (assert the version equals the tag).
verifier_note: handler.go:252-254 returns only {status: ok}; Dockerfile:20-23 builds with -ldflags='-s -w' and no -X version injection; nothing exposes build info.

title: Startup raw-secret inventory uses the 2 s readiness timeout and can spuriously warn on large databases
description: CountRawSecrets counts rows in findings/occurrences with a context bounded by LAYERLEAK_API_READINESS_TIMEOUT (default 2 s), a knob meant for probes. On a large history table the count exceeds 2 s and the API logs "could not inspect historical raw secret storage", masking the real answer.
evidence:
internal/api/run.go:49-53:
  warningCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), cfg.APIReadinessTimeout)
  counts, countErr := store.CountRawSecrets(warningCtx)
  ... slog.Warn("could not inspect historical raw secret storage", ...)
proposed_fix: Use cfg.DatabaseQueryTimeout (10 s) or a dedicated startup timeout, or use an EXISTS query instead of a count so it is O(1) with the right index.
verifier_note: run.go:49 uses cfg.APIReadinessTimeout (2 s default, config.go:101) and storage/admin.go:25 applies withTimeout(ctx, queryTimeout) so the effective bound is min(2 s, 10 s) = 2 s for two COUNT(*) scans over findings and finding_occurrences (admin.go:29-33).

title: Completed scans are discarded (503/408/504) when the request context ends between scan completion and the SaveScan write
description: ScanAndSave reuses the handler's scanCtx (request.Context() + ScanTimeout) for persistence. If the scan finishes successfully but the context is already cancelled or expires before SaveScan returns — client disconnected after 29 minutes, or the scan completed at 29m59s — the result is thrown away: service.go:124-130 returns ctx.Err() (mapped to 408/504 by the handler) and service.go:149 / postgres.go:152 run the INSERT under min(remaining scanCtx, DatabaseWriteTimeout), turning a healthy database into 503 storage_unavailable. The refusal to persist is only justified when the scan itself was aborted mid-way (scanErr is a context error), not when scanErr == nil.
proposed_fix: When scanErr == nil (or is a non-context error with a usable result), persist with `saveCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), s.config.DatabaseWriteTimeout)` so a finished scan is stored regardless of the HTTP connection's fate; keep refusing to save only when the scan was interrupted by ctx (errors.Is(scanErr, context.Canceled/DeadlineExceeded)). Add a scanservice test with a context cancelled after the stub scan returns, asserting SaveScan is still called. This is the cheap half of API-12.

title: ServeMux path cleaning returns 301 text/html redirects, breaking the 'every response is JSON' contract
description: net/http.ServeMux canonicalises paths containing repeated slashes or dot segments and answers with a 301 whose body is HTML. Probe against the real handler: GET /api/v1/repositories//library/app/scans -> 301 Location=/api/v1/repositories/library/app/scans, Content-Type text/html; GET /api/v1/repositories/library/../app/scans -> 301 to /api/v1/repositories/app/scans. The middleware still sets the security headers, but README.md:365 ('Error bodies use this shape') and the checked_ok claim 'unknown paths return JSON 404' do not hold for these inputs, and the behaviour is undocumented in openapi.yaml.
evidence: Probe output: GET /api/v1/repositories//library/app/scans -> 301 ct="text/html; charset=utf-8" loc="/api/v1/repositories/library/app/scans" body="Moved Permanently." handler.go:206: mux := http.NewServeMux() (default cleaning/redirect behaviour, no pre-check in middleware at handler.go:802-827).
proposed_fix: In middleware, before calling the mux, compare `path.Clean(request.URL.Path)` (preserving a trailing slash) with request.URL.Path and return JSON 404 not_found (or 400 invalid_request) on mismatch, so no HTML ever leaves the API; alternatively document the 301 in openapi.yaml under a `default` response. Add a test for `//` and `..` paths.

title: scan_limit_exceeded is the only API error whose message is the raw err.Error() chain, contradicting the neutral-message policy
description: classifyScanError returns `err.Error()` verbatim for limits.IsExceeded errors. Every other failure string in API output is neutralised (sanitizeResultErrors rewrites result error fields to 'scan step failed'; storage and upstream errors use fixed messages). The limits chain includes scanner wrap prefixes and subjects such as 'read config blob: config blob sha256:... exceeded max config bytes limit of N', 'manifest <identifier>', 'tag response for repository X' — operational detail, not secrets, but unspecified in openapi.yaml and inconsistent with the stated policy; its wording also changes whenever an internal wrap message changes.
evidence:
internal/api/handler.go:738-739:
  case limits.IsExceeded(err):
      return http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, "scan_limit_exceeded", err.Error()
internal/limits/limits.go:28-38 (Error() embeds Subject); internal/scanner/scan.go:935-983 wraps with fmt.Errorf("read config blob: %w", ...), "fetch config blob: %w"; internal/registry/client.go:732,753 subjects include manifest identifier and repository.
proposed_fix: Extract the *limits.ExceededError with errors.As and build a fixed-format message from Kind and Limit ('the scan exceeded the configured <kind> limit of <limit>'), optionally adding additive `limit_kind`/`limit` fields to the error object; document the format in openapi.yaml's IncompleteScan response and add a unit test asserting the wrap chain does not appear.

title: Only refs/tags/v1.* is protected by a tag ruleset; v2.x tags today and v3.x tags at release are unprotected
description: The live repository ruleset 'Protect v1 release tags' includes only `refs/tags/v1.*` (update, deletion, non_fast_forward blocked). The historical v2.0.0-v2.5.0 tags that the docs promise are 'preserved' can be moved or deleted by anyone with write access, and a v3.0.0 tag pushed by the workflow would have no protection at all, contradicting 'Never move or reuse a version tag'. RELEASING step 5 instructs creating a v1.* ruleset only.
evidence: `gh api repos/Brumbelow/layerleak/rulesets/<id>` -> `{"name":"Protect v1 release tags","target":"tag","conditions":{"ref_name":{"include":["refs/tags/v1.*"]}},"rules":["update","deletion","non_fast_forward"],"bypass":[]}`; RELEASING.md:146 'Add a tag ruleset for `v1.*` that blocks updates, deletion, and non-fast-forward changes'.
proposed_fix: Before the first v3 RC, widen the ruleset include pattern to `refs/tags/v*` (covers v1, v2 history and v3+) while keeping creation allowed for the workflow, and update RELEASING.md step 5 to say `v*`. Optionally add a read-only pre-dispatch check in RELEASING (`gh api repos/.../rulesets`) confirming the v3 pattern is active.
verifier_note: Live ruleset 20827054 confirmed: include `refs/tags/v1.*`, rules update/deletion/non_fast_forward, no bypass. But the impact is overstated: `gh api repos/Brumbelow/layerleak/releases` shows v1.0.0, v2.0.0, v2.1.0, v2.1.1 and v2.5.0 all have `immutable: true`, and GitHub immutable releases lock the release's tag against update and deletion independently of rulesets. The v2.x history is therefore already protected, and a v3.0.0 tag is exposed only for the seconds between the tag push (line 985) and `gh release create` (line 1080). Only v1.0.0-beta.1 and v2.0.0-beta (non-immutable prereleases) are unprotected. Still worth doing as defence in depth and for RELEASING.md step 5 accuracy, but not release-blocking.

description: Verified with git ls-remote that every SHA pin matches its comment tag. Behind: docker/setup-buildx-action v4.3.0 (current v4.4.1), docker/setup-qemu-action v4.3.0 (v4.4.0), docker/build-push-action v7.3.0 (v7.4.0), actions/setup-python v6.1.0 (v7.0.0), github/codeql-action v4.37.9 (v4.38.2). Last Dependabot actions bump merged 2026-09-04.
