title: Dependabot ignores the pip lock, the npm lock and the digest-pinned images/tool versions embedded in workflows
description: Only gomod, github-actions and docker (root directory) are configured. requirements-docs.lock (openapi validators, PyYAML) and scripts/tests/package-lock.json (Playwright) are never updated automatically, and the `postgres:16.13-alpine@sha256` references inside verify.yml/container-release.yml and the `BUILDKIT_IMAGE` env are outside Dependabot's docker ecosystem scope.
evidence: dependabot.yml lists `package-ecosystem: "gomod"`, `"github-actions"`, `"docker"` only; verify.yml:183 and container-release.yml:864 `postgres:16.13-alpine@sha256:4e6e670b...`; container-release.yml:37 `BUILDKIT_IMAGE: moby/buildkit:v0.33.0@sha256:6c2fa84a...`.
proposed_fix: Rename requirements-docs.lock to requirements-docs.txt (update verify.yml:98,101, the pip-compile comment in the file, RELEASING/readiness references) so the pip ecosystem with pip-compile can update it from requirements-docs.in; add `package-ecosystem: npm` for /scripts/tests; add `package-ecosystem: docker-compose` for / to cover docker-compose.yml; keep a RELEASING checklist item for the postgres and BuildKit digests embedded in workflow YAML, which no ecosystem parses.
verifier_note: .github/dependabot.yml has only gomod, github-actions and docker. The fix needs two corrections: Dependabot's pip ecosystem discovers `requirements*.txt`/`*.in` files, not a `.lock` file, so adding `package-ecosystem: pip` alone would update nothing for requirements-docs.lock; and docker-compose.yml:6 pins `postgres:16.13-alpine@sha256:...`, which the `docker` ecosystem (Dockerfile only) does not cover.

title: Recovery gaps: a leftover draft release blocks every retry, and an RC whose image exists without attestations has no documented way forward
description: gh 2.100.0 creates the release as a draft, uploads assets, then publishes, deleting the draft on failure; if that cleanup itself fails (network), the draft remains. validate then sees `gh release view` succeed with isDraft=true and exits 'incompatible GitHub release state', so every retry fails until someone deletes the draft manually, and RELEASING.md's Failure and recovery section never mentions drafts. Likewise the recovery step in supply-chain hard-fails when `${IMAGE_NAME}:${RELEASE_VERSION}` exists but source-bound attestations are missing (manual push, registry loss); the correct outcome (burn the version, publish the next RC) is implied but not written down.
evidence: :144-151 `if gh release view ...; then release_state=...; if [[ "${release_state}" != $'false\ttrue\t'"${prerelease}" ]]; then echo "... has incompatible GitHub release state."; exit 1`; cli/cli v2.100.0 create.go:509-511 'Save the release initially as draft and publish it after all assets have finished uploading ... params["draft"] = true', :534 `cleanupDraftRelease`; :641-644 `gh attestation verify "oci://${IMAGE_NAME}@${IMAGE_DIGEST}" ... > recovered-index-attestations.json; jq -e 'length > 0 ...'`.
proposed_fix: In validate, when the release exists and `isDraft` is true, print an explicit message ('a draft from an interrupted publication exists; delete it with `gh release delete <tag> --yes` (drafts are not immutable) and re-run') instead of the generic state error, or delete it automatically in the publish job when `isDraft=true && isImmutable=false` and no assets are needed. Add both scenarios (draft left behind; version image present without attestations -> publish next RC, never repush) to RELEASING.md 'Failure and recovery'.
verifier_note: Fetched cli/cli v2.100.0 sources: pkg/cmd/release/create/create.go:509-511 `// Save the release initially as draft and publish it after all assets have finished uploading ... params["draft"] = true`, :534 `cleanupDraftRelease`; pkg/cmd/release/shared/fetch.go:183-230 runs a parallel `fetchDraftRelease` lookup (GraphQL by pending tag) so `gh release view <tag>` with the authenticated GITHUB_TOKEN does find a leftover draft, and validate line 148 then fails with the generic state error. Recovery gap in RELEASING.md confirmed.

title: CodeQL runs only on push/PR with no schedule, uses deprecated Go autobuild, default query suite and no timeout
description: Without a cron schedule, newly published CodeQL queries never re-analyze a quiet main branch; the `github.event_name != 'schedule'` condition is vestigial. Go analysis no longer needs autobuild (build-mode: none); the default suite omits security-extended queries; the job has no timeout-minutes.
evidence: codeql-analysis.yml:3-7 `on: push: branches: [main] pull_request: branches: [main]` (no `schedule`); :17 `if: github.event_name != 'schedule' || github.repository == 'brumbelow/layerleak'`; :35-36 `- name: Autobuild uses: github/codeql-action/autobuild@...`; no `queries:` input; no `timeout-minutes`.
proposed_fix: Add `schedule: - cron: '23 6 * * 1'`, set `build-mode: none` in the init step and drop the Autobuild step, add `queries: security-extended`, `timeout-minutes: 30`, and keep the repository guard only for the scheduled event.
verifier_note: codeql-analysis.yml:3-7 has no schedule, :17 vestigial schedule guard, :35-36 autobuild, no queries/timeout. Fix is correct (Go supports build-mode: none).

title: Codacy workflow can never fail on findings, lacks a timeout, and re-runs the unit suite for coverage
description: `max-allowed-issues: 2147483647` turns the security scan into upload-only (acceptable if intentional, but undocumented); the scan job has no timeout-minutes; the coverage job re-runs `go test -short ./...` that the CI workflow already ran on the same commit; `.codacy.yml` configures the deprecated tslint engine and excludes `.github/**` so Codacy performs no workflow analysis.
evidence: codacy.yml:50 `max-allowed-issues: 2147483647`; :46 `verbose: true`; job `codacy-security-scan` has no `timeout-minutes`; :116 `go test -short ./... -count=1 -covermode=atomic -coverprofile=unit.coverage.out`; .codacy.yml:3 `tslint:` and :12 `- ".github/**"`.
proposed_fix: Add `timeout-minutes: 30` to the scan job; add a comment stating the upload-only intent (or lower to a real budget once the SARIF baseline is clean); produce the coverage profile in verify.yml's quality job and upload it as an artifact that codacy.yml downloads (or run coverage only on push); remove the obsolete `tslint` block and consider not excluding `.github/**` if you want Codacy's actionlint-style checks.
verifier_note: codacy.yml:50 max-allowed-issues 2147483647, no timeout on the scan job, :116 duplicate `go test -short`; .codacy.yml:3 tslint block and :12 `.github/**` exclusion confirmed.

title: No macOS or Windows build/test job for the CLI, and the preflight test suite fails on non-x86_64 Linux hosts
description: All jobs use ubuntu-24.04, so darwin/windows path handling, TTY progress and the findings directory are never exercised even though those platforms are advertised install targets via `go install`. Separately, `test_installer_rejects_corrupt_cached_archive_without_installation` asserts the checksum message, but on arm64/macOS the installer exits earlier with 'supports Linux x86_64 only', so `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests` fails for contributors on Apple silicon.
evidence: verify.yml uses `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` in every job; scripts/tests/test_release_preflight.py:153-156 `[bash, str(SCRIPT.with_name('release-tools.sh')), directory] ... self.assertIn('Checksum verification failed', result.stderr)`; scripts/release-tools.sh:14-16 `if [[ "$(uname -s)" != Linux || "$(uname -m)" != x86_64 ]]; then echo 'The reviewed release tool bundle supports Linux x86_64 only.'`.
proposed_fix: Add a lightweight `cli-cross` job: matrix `[macos-15, windows-2025]` running `go build ./...` and `go test -short ./internal/cli/... ./internal/output/...` (or the full short suite if it is portable). Guard the installer test with `@unittest.skipUnless(platform.system()=='Linux' and platform.machine()=='x86_64', ...)` or inject `uname` overrides via env.
verifier_note: release-tools.sh:14-16 exits with 'supports Linux x86_64 only' before the checksum step, while test_release_preflight.py:153-156 asserts 'Checksum verification failed' in stderr; on arm64/macOS the assertion fails. All verify.yml jobs are ubuntu-24.04.

title: scripts/layerleak-migrate-up.sh only works when invoked from inside the module directory
description: The script resolves the repository directory but then runs `go run <absolute path>` from the caller's cwd; Go requires the current directory to be inside a module, so calling the helper from anywhere else fails. The script is not referenced by any documentation, so it is either dead or an undocumented operator helper.
evidence: `cd /tmp && /home/user/layerleak/scripts/layerleak-migrate-up.sh` -> `go: go.mod file not found in current directory or any parent directory; see 'go help modules'` rc=1; scripts/layerleak-migrate-up.sh:11 `exec go run "${repository_dir}/cmd/migrate"`; `grep -rn layerleak-migrate-up.sh *.md docs` -> no references.
proposed_fix: Change line 11 to `cd "${repository_dir}" && exec go run ./cmd/migrate "$@"`, add it to README/database docs (or delete it if the native `layerleak-migrate-up` binary supersedes it), and cover it with shellcheck in the new tooling job (REL-15).
verifier_note: Ran the script from the scratchpad directory: `go: go.mod file not found in current directory or any parent directory` rc=1. Line 11 `exec go run "${repository_dir}/cmd/migrate"` never changes directory. Fix is correct.

title: release-manifest.json hard-codes cosign v3.0.2 instead of recording the tool that actually signed
description: The manifest's `tools.cosign` is a literal string duplicated from scripts/release-tools.sh, while `tools.grype` comes from the env. If the installer pin changes without this line (REL-09), the evidence file misreports the signing tool.
evidence: :754-755 `--arg grype_version "${GRYPE_VERSION}" --arg cosign_version "v3.0.2"`; scripts/release-tools.sh:43 pins `cosign ... v3.0.2`.
proposed_fix: Derive it at runtime: `cosign_version="$(cosign version 2>&1 | awk '/^GitVersion:/{print $2}')"` (the preflight already asserts this format) and pass `--arg cosign_version "${cosign_version}"`; do the same for `gh --version` and `docker buildx version` so the manifest records the full reviewed toolset.
verifier_note: container-release.yml:755 `--arg cosign_version "v3.0.2"` literal while grype comes from env (754). The preflight already parses `GitVersion:` from `cosign version` (release-preflight.py:66) so the proposed awk is consistent.

title: Minor permission over-grants: stage-image requests attestations:read it never uses
description: stage-image only builds/pushes and inspects images; `attestations: read` is unused there (gh attestation verify runs in supply-chain and post-release). Everything else is minimal: publish needs contents:write+packages:write, supply-chain needs id-token/attestations/packages write, validate/scan/smoke are read-only, persist-credentials is false on every checkout.
evidence: :253-256 `permissions: contents: read / packages: write / attestations: read` on stage-image; no `gh attestation` call in that job.
proposed_fix: Remove `attestations: read` from stage-image. Optionally add a comment above each job's permissions block naming the step that needs each write scope, which makes future review of GITHUB_TOKEN scopes faster.
verifier_note: stage-image permissions (lines 253-256) include attestations:read; no `gh attestation` or actions/attest usage in that job (lines 262-430).

title: Repository templates: FUNDING.yml is mostly boilerplate, issue templates are legacy Markdown, PR checklist omits lint and changelog
description: FUNDING.yml keeps twelve commented placeholder lines around the single `ko_fi: brumbelow` entry. Issue templates use the legacy Markdown front-matter format rather than YAML issue forms (no required fields, no dropdowns for install method/platform, the security warning is an HTML comment users often delete). The PR template checklist has no golangci-lint/actionlint item and no CHANGELOG.md entry item even though RELEASING requires the changelog to be frozen before an RC.
evidence: FUNDING.yml:1 `github: # Replace with up to 4 GitHub Sponsors-enabled usernames ...` (lines 1-3, 5-13 are placeholders); ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md:1-7 Markdown front matter `name: Bug report ... labels: bug`; PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:14-21 checklist lists git diff --check, gofmt, vet, tests, container checks, docs, notices but no lint or CHANGELOG item.
proposed_fix: Trim FUNDING.yml to `ko_fi: brumbelow`. Convert the three templates to `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml` issue forms with required version/install-method/platform fields and a visible 'no secrets' checkbox. Add `- [ ] golangci-lint / actionlint / shellcheck` and `- [ ] CHANGELOG.md updated under [Unreleased]` to the PR template.
verifier_note: FUNDING.yml has 12 placeholder lines around `ko_fi: brumbelow`; ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md uses Markdown front matter with the secrets warning in an HTML comment; PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md checklist (lines 14-21) has no lint or CHANGELOG item.

title: Dockerfile `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7` pulls an unpinned frontend image at every release build
description: The release build pins BuildKit by digest (BUILDKIT_IMAGE) and the base image by digest, but the `# syntax=` directive makes BuildKit fetch `docker/dockerfile:1.7` (a floating tag) from Docker Hub at build time and execute it as the Dockerfile frontend. That is a remote, unreviewed component in a pipeline whose policy is reviewed, checksum-pinned tools, and Dependabot's docker ecosystem does not update syntax directives. The pinned BuildKit v0.33.0 built-in frontend already supports every feature used (`--mount=type=cache`, `$BUILDPLATFORM`, TARGETOS/TARGETARCH).
evidence: Dockerfile:1 `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7`; container-release.yml:37 `BUILDKIT_IMAGE: moby/buildkit:v0.33.0@sha256:6c2fa84a...` (digest-pinned) and Dockerfile:5 `golang:1.27.1-bookworm@sha256:648f44...` (digest-pinned) show the pinning policy the directive escapes.
proposed_fix: Remove line 1 so the digest-pinned BuildKit's built-in frontend is used, or pin it as `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7@sha256:<digest>` and add it to the RELEASING tool table. Verify with the existing CI container job that the build still succeeds.

title: The Grype binary that gates the release is installed by anchore/scan-action, not the repository-checksum-pinned bundle the preflight verifies
description: validate installs Grype 0.99.1 from scripts/release-tools.sh with a repository-pinned SHA-256 and runs `release-preflight.py tools --full` against it, but that binary never scans anything. scan-image runs anchore/scan-action, which downloads its own Grype (version-pinned by `grype-version`, checksum taken from the upstream release, not from this repository). RELEASING.md's tool table claims Grype is 'Official archive and repository-pinned SHA-256; scan action selects the same version', which conflates the two installations.
evidence: container-release.yml:458-472 `uses: anchore/scan-action@27805bf3...` with `grype-version: ${{ env.GRYPE_VERSION }}` and no checkout or release-tools.sh in the scan-image job (lines 450-510); release-tools.sh:47-51 installs grype only in `all` mode for validate/supply-chain/post-release; RELEASING.md:40 'Official archive and repository-pinned SHA-256; scan action selects the same version'.
proposed_fix: Either run the reviewed binary directly in scan-image (checkout control plane, `scripts/release-tools.sh ... all`, then `grype "${IMAGE_NAME}@${DIGEST}" --platform "${platform}" --fail-on critical --output sarif --file ...` and a second `--only-fixed --fail-on high` run, keeping the always() enforcement step), or reword RELEASING.md:40 to say the scanning job uses anchore/scan-action's version-pinned download and the repository checksum covers only the preflight copy.

title: README's global "0 disables a MAX_* bound" rule is contradicted by four MAX_* variables that reject 0
description: README.md:197-199 says "A value of `0` disables a `MAX_*` bound unless the description says otherwise." Only LAYERLEAK_MAX_FILE_BYTES (line 229) says "must be positive". But config.go parses LAYERLEAK_MAX_AUTH_RESPONSE_BYTES (line 129) and LAYERLEAK_API_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES (line 69) with int64FromEnv, and LAYERLEAK_API_MAX_CONCURRENT_SCANS (line 77) and LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_MAX_OPEN_CONNS (line 205) with intFromEnv; all four return "%s must be greater than zero" for 0. .env.example scopes the same sentence to the scan-bounds block (line 44) but README applies it globally.
evidence: config.go:446-448 `if parsed <= 0 { return 0, fmt.Errorf("%s must be greater than zero", key) }` (int64FromEnv) used at 69 (API_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES) and 129 (MAX_AUTH_RESPONSE_BYTES); config.go:463-465 same for intFromEnv used at 77 and 205; README.md:198-199 `A value of `0` disables a\n`MAX_*` bound unless the description says otherwise.`; README.md:213 `| LAYERLEAK_MAX_AUTH_RESPONSE_BYTES | 1048576 | Maximum registry token response size. |` (no exception noted)
proposed_fix: Fix as proposed. Since the four variables live in different tables (core/registry, API and PostgreSQL), the least error-prone edit is to move the sentence under '### Resource bounds' (where every MAX_* row except MAX_FILE_BYTES accepts 0, which is already annotated) and add 'must be positive' to the four rows. Add `TestLoadRejectsZeroForPositiveOnlyBounds` covering LAYERLEAK_API_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES, LAYERLEAK_MAX_AUTH_RESPONSE_BYTES, LAYERLEAK_API_MAX_CONCURRENT_SCANS, LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_MAX_OPEN_CONNS, LAYERLEAK_TAG_PAGE_SIZE, LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_MAX_REDIRECTS, LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_REQUEST_ATTEMPTS.
verifier_note: Confirmed: README.md:198-199 states the global rule; config.go:69 (API_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES) and :129 (MAX_AUTH_RESPONSE_BYTES) use int64FromEnv whose :446-448 rejects `parsed <= 0`; config.go:77 (API_MAX_CONCURRENT_SCANS) and :205 (DATABASE_MAX_OPEN_CONNS) use intFromEnv with the same rejection at :463-465. Only README.md:229 (MAX_FILE_BYTES) carries 'must be positive'; rows at :213, :251, :253, :261 do not. .env.example:44 correctly scopes the rule to the scan bounds. Impact is low because a user who sets 0 gets a clear `<VAR> must be greater than zero` error at startup rather than silent misbehaviour; still a documentation statement that is false and cheap to fix before release.

title: Dependabot ignores the npm (Playwright) and pip (OpenAPI validators) toolchains; the pip lock uses a filename Dependabot will not detect
description: scripts/tests/package.json pins `playwright 1.62.1` and requirements-docs.lock pins openapi-spec-validator 0.9.0, pydantic 2.13.5, rpds-py etc. with hashes. Neither ecosystem is in dependabot.yml, so these test-time dependencies (which download and execute Chromium and run pip with `--require-hashes` in the documentation job) are never updated or alerted on. Dependabot's pip updater detects requirements*.txt / *.in files; `requirements-docs.lock` is not a recognized manifest name, so adding the ecosystem alone would not pick it up.
evidence: dependabot.yml lists only gomod, github-actions, docker; scripts/tests/package.json:8 `"playwright": "1.62.1"`; requirements-docs.lock:3 `# pip-compile --generate-hashes --strip-extras --output-file=requirements-docs.lock requirements-docs.in`; verify.yml:98 `cache-dependency-path: requirements-docs.lock`, :101 `pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-docs.lock`
proposed_fix: Add `- package-ecosystem: "npm" directory: "/scripts/tests"` and `- package-ecosystem: "pip" directory: "/"` entries (weekly, grouped). Rename requirements-docs.lock to requirements-docs.txt (update its header, verify.yml:98 and :101, and any scripts referencing it) so Dependabot's pip updater sees it, or point the pip entry at requirements-docs.in and regenerate hashes in the PR.
verifier_note: scripts/tests/package.json:8 pins `"playwright": "1.62.1"`; requirements-docs.lock header prescribes pip-compile with `--output-file=requirements-docs.lock`; verify.yml:96-101 installs it with Python 3.13 and `--require-hashes`; dependabot.yml has no npm or pip entry. Dependabot's pip detection of only *.txt/*.in requirement files cannot be executed here, so that part keeps medium confidence, but the fix (rename to requirements-docs.txt and reference it in verify.yml:98/101) is safe either way.

title: Direct and indirect Go dependencies have newer releases; refresh before rc.1 so notices and SBOMs match
description: `go list -m -u all` reports klauspost/compress v1.19.2 -> v1.20.1 (2026-09-25), golang.org/x/term v0.45.0 -> v0.46.0, golang.org/x/sys v0.47.0 -> v0.48.0, spf13/pflag v1.0.9 -> v1.0.10, plus go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 and go-md2man test-only bumps. govulncheck reports no vulnerabilities today, so this is hygiene, but THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md hard-codes these versions (lines 9-16) and the rc must be cut from the final dependency set because the release workflow reuses the RC digest for the stable tag.

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:10/14/15/16 hard-code the current versions.

title: `docker compose up -d api` on a fresh volume yields an API that is never ready because migrate is profile-gated and not a dependency
description: The api service depends only on `db: condition: service_healthy`; the migrate service lives in the `tools` profile and must be run manually first (README:413). NewPostgresStore is created with RequireSchema: true, so an API started against an empty database fails schema validation, exits, and is restarted forever by `restart: unless-stopped`, while the healthcheck shows unhealthy. Compose supports `service_completed_successfully`, which would make the documented ordering automatic and idempotent (the migration command is a no-op when current).
evidence: docker-compose.yml:72-74 `depends_on: db: condition: service_healthy`; docker-compose.yml:108-109 `profiles: - tools` on migrate; internal/api/run.go:42 `RequireSchema: true,`; README.md:88-89 `the API will remain unready on an older schema.`
proposed_fix: Remove `profiles: [tools]` from migrate (keep `restart: "no"`) and add to api: `depends_on: { db: {condition: service_healthy}, migrate: {condition: service_completed_successfully} }`. Keep purge-raw-secrets in the tools profile. Update README:413-414 to a single `docker compose up -d`.
verifier_note: docker-compose.yml:72-74 api depends only on db health; :108-109 migrate is in profile `tools`; internal/api/run.go:42 `RequireSchema: true` and postgres.go:60-65 fail construction on schema mismatch; README.md:413-414 documents the manual ordering. `service_completed_successfully` is supported by Compose v2, which the README already requires (`docker compose`). Removing the profile from migrate makes `docker compose up -d` run it every start; RunMigrations is documented as a no-op when current (README:283), so this is safe.

title: Compose hardening gaps: db service unhardened, no resource limits, unbounded tmpfs, floating :latest image default
description: The api/migrate/purge services are well hardened (read_only, tmpfs, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges) but: the db service has only no-new-privileges (no cap_drop, no read_only, no tmpfs); no service sets memory/CPU/pids limits although the API decompresses untrusted layers up to 512 MiB per layer and retains up to 1 GiB; `tmpfs: - /tmp:mode=1777` has no `size=` so it can consume half of host RAM; `LAYERLEAK_IMAGE` defaults to `ghcr.io/brumbelow/layerleak:latest` (.env.example:2, compose:24) which contradicts the digest-pinning discipline applied to postgres and the release verification section (README:432-440).
evidence: docker-compose.yml:19-21 db has only `restart` and `security_opt: - no-new-privileges:true`; docker-compose.yml:84-85 `tmpfs: - /tmp:mode=1777`; docker-compose.yml:24 `image: ${LAYERLEAK_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/brumbelow/layerleak:latest}`; no `deploy:`/`mem_limit`/`pids_limit` keys anywhere in the file
proposed_fix: db: add `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `cap_add: [CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE, FOWNER, SETGID, SETUID]`, `tmpfs: [/run/postgresql, /tmp]`, `shm_size: 256m`. api: `tmpfs: - /tmp:mode=1777,size=256m`, `pids_limit: 256`, `mem_limit: 2g` (or `deploy.resources.limits`). Default LAYERLEAK_IMAGE in .env.example to the released version tag (`ghcr.io/brumbelow/layerleak:v3.0.0`) and show the digest form in README.
verifier_note: docker-compose.yml:19-21 db has only restart and no-new-privileges; :84-85 `tmpfs: - /tmp:mode=1777` has no size; :24 defaults LAYERLEAK_IMAGE to `:latest`; grep for shm_size/mem_limit/pids_limit/deploy: returns nothing. The cap_add list proposed for the official postgres image (CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE, FOWNER, SETGID, SETUID) matches what its entrypoint needs; keep medium confidence until tested.

title: .dockerignore excludes almost nothing, so docs/web/scripts changes invalidate the Go build cache and bloat the context
description: .dockerignore contains only `.git`, `.github`, `findings`. Dockerfile:13 `COPY . .` therefore ships web/, docs/, scripts/ (including scripts/tests/node_modules if present locally), *.md, .env.example, docker-compose.yml, CHANGELOG etc. into the build stage; any edit to those files changes the COPY layer digest and forces `go build` to re-run despite the cache mounts. The build also relies on -buildvcs=auto silently doing nothing because .git is excluded; making it explicit avoids a surprise if the ignore list changes.
evidence: .dockerignore (entire file): `.git\n.github\nfindings`; Dockerfile:13 `COPY . .`; Dockerfile:20 `go build -mod=readonly -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o /out/layerleak-api ./cmd/api` (no -buildvcs flag)
proposed_fix: As proposed; the allowlist form (`*` then `!go.mod !go.sum !**/*.go !cmd/ !internal/ !migrations/`) is the most robust. `-buildvcs=false` is correct and harmless since .git is excluded today.
verifier_note: .dockerignore is exactly `.git`, `.github`, `findings`; Dockerfile:13 `COPY . .`; Dockerfile:20-23 has no -buildvcs flag. Nuance: because the RUN uses a go-build cache mount, the re-executed `go build` is nearly a no-op, so the cost is layer invalidation and context size rather than a full rebuild. An additional reason to add `.env*`: a developer's local .env (real DB password) is otherwise copied into the build stage cache, though it never reaches the scratch image.

title: Dead configuration: LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR is baked into the image/compose but never used by the API; Config.MigrationsDir is read but unused
description: cfg.FindingsDir is consumed only by internal/cli/scan.go:213 (CLI result artifacts). The container has no CLI binary, yet Dockerfile:39 sets `ENV LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR=/tmp/layerleak/findings` and docker-compose.yml:46 passes `LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR` to the api service, suggesting the API writes findings to disk (it does not). Conversely config.Load populates MigrationsDir (config.go:280) but nothing reads it: cmd/migrate/main.go:30-33 reads LAYERLEAK_MIGRATIONS_DIR and applies the `/app/migrations` default itself, duplicating the default in two places. A major release can delete both without compatibility cost.

proposed_fix: Remove Dockerfile:39 and compose:46 (or ship the CLI in the image per CFG-14 and keep them). Either delete Config.MigrationsDir and its README row from the general table (documenting it under the migration command instead), or make cmd/migrate use config.Load()/a shared constant so the default lives in one place.

Dockerfile:39 `ENV LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR=/tmp/layerleak/findings` and compose:46 pass it to an image that contains no CLI. grep MigrationsDir -> only config.go:61/280 and config_test.go:143; cmd/migrate/main.go:30-33 reads LAYERLEAK_MIGRATIONS_DIR itself with its own `/app/migrations` default.

title: The container image has no `layerleak` CLI and compose has no scan profile
description: The scratch image contains only layerleak-api, layerleak-migrate-up, layerleak-purge-raw-secrets and layerleak-healthcheck. Users who want to scan from CI or a workstation without a Go toolchain have no supported image (README:83-86 says the CLI is go-install only). Adding the root CLI to the same image (it is the same module and already static) and a `scan` compose profile (`profiles: [scan]`, `entrypoint: /usr/local/bin/layerleak`, volume for findings, optional LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_URL) would make the compose stack usable end-to-end and is a natural 3.0 feature.

Extend scripts/verify-container-platform.py's expected binary list and README's distribution paragraph.

title: No test pins .env.example/compose defaults to config.Load, and several parser edge cases are untested
description: TestLoadDefaults hand-copies expected values, so a drift between .env.example, docker-compose.yml defaults and config.go would not be caught (today they match only by discipline). Untested behaviours verified by probing the stdlib: `LAYERLEAK_MAX_AUTH_RESPONSE_BYTES=0`, `LAYERLEAK_API_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES=0`, `LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_MAX_OPEN_CONNS=0` rejection; `LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_MAX_IDLE_CONNS=0` acceptance; whitespace-padded numerics (` 5 `), `+5`, out-of-range (`9223372036854775808` -> value out of range), unitless durations (`30` -> missing unit), fractional durations (`1.5h`), LOG_LEVEL offsets (`INFO+2` accepted, `warning` rejected), and PERSIST_RAW_SECRETS forms (`t`, `TRUE` accepted; `yes`, `on` rejected). Only the log-level test asserts error text.
evidence: config_test.go has no test referencing LAYERLEAK_MAX_AUTH_RESPONSE_BYTES, LAYERLEAK_API_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES or LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_MAX_OPEN_CONNS with "0"; probe: `ParseBool("yes") = false, strconv.ParseBool: parsing "yes": invalid syntax`; `ParseDuration("30") = 0s, time: missing unit in duration "30"`; `Level("INFO+2") = INFO+2, <nil>`; `ParseInt("9223372036854775808") ... value out of range`
proposed_fix: Add `TestEnvExampleMatchesDefaults` that parses ../../.env.example (skipping LAYERLEAK_IMAGE/API_HOST/API_PORT/DB_*), sets every key with t.Setenv, calls Load(), and compares to a Load() with all keys empty (FINDINGS_DIR/DATABASE_URL excepted after CFG-03). Add a similar test that extracts `${VAR:-default}` pairs from docker-compose.yml. Add a table-driven `TestLoadRejectsZeroForPositiveOnlyBounds` and `TestLoadParsesEdgeCases` covering the inputs above and asserting error text names the variable.
verifier_note: config_test.go has TestLoadInvalidMaxFileBytes ("0") and TestLoadInvalidTagPageSize ("0") but no zero-rejection test for LAYERLEAK_MAX_AUTH_RESPONSE_BYTES, LAYERLEAK_API_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES, LAYERLEAK_API_MAX_CONCURRENT_SCANS or LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_MAX_OPEN_CONNS; TestLoadDefaults (lines 9-146) hand-codes every expected value; only TestLoadRejectsInvalidLogLevel (:345-351) asserts error text. No test reads .env.example or docker-compose.yml. `go test ./internal/config` passes today.

title: LOG_LEVEL and PERSIST_RAW_SECRETS accept more (and less) than the README states
description: README:205 documents `debug, info, warn, or error`, but logLevelFromEnv lower-cases and hands the string to slog.Level.UnmarshalText, which also accepts `INFO+2`, `warn-1` (= INFO+3), and rejects `warning`. The accepted value is stored as a string and re-parsed in api/run.go:108, so offsets propagate to the handler. README:177/207 shows only `1` for LAYERLEAK_PERSIST_RAW_SECRETS; strconv.ParseBool also takes `t/T/TRUE/true/True` but not `yes`/`on`, which is a common operator expectation for a boolean env var.
evidence: config.go:285-290 `value := strings.ToLower(envOrDefault(key, fallback)); var level slog.Level; if err := level.UnmarshalText([]byte(value))`; probe: `Level("INFO+2") = INFO+2, <nil>`, `Level("warn-1") = INFO+3, <nil>`, `Level("warning") ... unknown name`; config.go:428 `parsed, err := strconv.ParseBool(value)`; probe: `ParseBool("yes") ... invalid syntax`
proposed_fix: Either restrict LOG_LEVEL to the four documented names (switch statement) so misconfigurations fail loudly, or document "slog level names, optionally with +N/-N offsets". For PERSIST_RAW_SECRETS document "`1`/`true` enable; `0`/`false` disable" and, if desired, accept `yes/no/on/off` explicitly with an error message listing accepted forms.

README.md:205 lists only four names and :177/:207 only `1`.

title: Config validation gaps: API_ADDR unchecked at load time, no cross-checks between related bounds, 51 hand-rolled env reads
description: LAYERLEAK_API_ADDR is taken verbatim (envOrDefault) so a malformed value like `8080` or `localhost` only fails at ListenAndServe, after the database has been opened and raw-secret counts queried. Interdependent values are not cross-checked: LAYERLEAK_TAG_PAGE_SIZE larger than a non-zero LAYERLEAK_MAX_REPOSITORY_TAGS requests more tags than will ever be used; LAYERLEAK_MAX_FILE_BYTES larger than a non-zero LAYERLEAK_MAX_LAYER_BYTES can never be satisfied; LAYERLEAK_API_MAX_CONCURRENT_SCANS is not compared with LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_MAX_OPEN_CONNS. Load() is 220 lines of repeated `x, err := fooFromEnv(...); if err != nil { return Config{}, err }` blocks, which is how MigrationsDir became dead and why no test can enumerate the variable set.
evidence: config.go:235 `APIAddr: envOrDefault("LAYERLEAK_API_ADDR", "127.0.0.1:8080")` with no net.SplitHostPort; config.go:213-215 is the only cross-field check (`if databaseMaxIdleConns > databaseMaxOpenConns`); internal/registry/client.go:266-271 sends `n=<pageSize>` regardless of maxTags
proposed_fix: Validate APIAddr with net.SplitHostPort (host may be empty) and validatePort. Add warnings or errors for TagPageSize > MaxRepositoryTags (>0) and MaxFileBytes > MaxLayerBytes (>0), or clamp pageSize to remaining tags in ListTags. For 3.0 refactor Load() around a declarative spec slice (name, kind, default, min) so a single loop parses, a generated table feeds README/.env.example, and tests can iterate the spec.
verifier_note: config.go:235 takes LAYERLEAK_API_ADDR verbatim via envOrDefault; internal/api/run.go opens the store at :33-45 and queries raw-secret counts at :49-51 before ListenAndServe at :83, so a malformed address fails late. config.go:213-215 is the only cross-field check. internal/registry/client.go:265-271 sends `n=<pageSize>` without regard to maxTags (it only clamps pageSize <= 0 to 100). Load() is ~220 lines of repeated parse/return blocks.

title: Dockerfile `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7` is a floating, digest-less, 2.5-year-old frontend pin that contradicts the repository's digest-pinning discipline
description: Every other image reference in the repo (golang builder, postgres) is pinned tag@digest and bumped by Dependabot, but the BuildKit frontend pulled at build time by the release workflow is `docker/dockerfile:1.7` with no digest. Docker Hub currently lists 1.27.1 as the newest frontend; 1.7 dates from early 2024. The directive was introduced at 84d53fd (2026-04-30) and has never changed although the golang image on line 5 was bumped four times since, so Dependabot is not maintaining it. A floating frontend tag means two release builds of the same source can use different frontend code.
evidence: Dockerfile:1 `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7`; Docker Hub docker/dockerfile tags -> ['latest','1','1.27','1.27.1',...]; `git log -S'syntax=docker/dockerfile' -- Dockerfile` -> only 84d53fd; `git log -- Dockerfile` -> a84503d, 8ee7d86, f8622df, bd7a38b dependabot golang bumps after it
proposed_fix: Pin the frontend like the other images: `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.27@sha256:<current multi-platform digest>` (or drop the directive entirely, since the Dockerfile uses only cache mounts that the default frontend shipped with every supported Docker/BuildKit already supports). If kept, add a line to scripts/release-preflight.py or verify.yml that fails when the syntax directive lacks `@sha256:`.

title: .env.example ships LAYERLEAK_DB_PASSWORD=change-me, which defeats the compose `${LAYERLEAK_DB_PASSWORD:?}` required-variable guard
description: docker-compose.yml deliberately uses `${LAYERLEAK_DB_PASSWORD:?set LAYERLEAK_DB_PASSWORD in .env}` on four lines so a missing password aborts `docker compose config/up`. README:410-411 tells users to `cp .env.example .env` and edit the password, but because the example file already carries the non-empty placeholder `change-me`, Compose's `:?` check is satisfied and a user who forgets step two gets a fully running PostgreSQL + API with a publicly known password. Exposure is limited by the default 127.0.0.1 host binding, but the guard the compose file was written to provide never fires. The auditor's checked_ok entry '.env.example marks LAYERLEAK_DB_PASSWORD as required' overlooks that the value, not the comment, is what Compose evaluates.
evidence: .env.example:7-8 `# Required by docker-compose.yml. Replace before deployment.\nLAYERLEAK_DB_PASSWORD=change-me`; docker-compose.yml:10 `POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${LAYERLEAK_DB_PASSWORD:?set LAYERLEAK_DB_PASSWORD in .env}` (also :44, :96, :121); README.md:410-411 `cp .env.example .env\n# Edit LAYERLEAK_DB_PASSWORD in .env.`
proposed_fix: Ship `LAYERLEAK_DB_PASSWORD=` (empty) in .env.example with the existing comment, so `docker compose config` fails with the intended 'set LAYERLEAK_DB_PASSWORD in .env' message until the operator supplies one. Optionally pair with CFG-09 (compose secrets / POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE). Update README:410-411 wording accordingly.

title: .dockerignore does not exclude .env, so a developer's database password is copied into the builder stage and BuildKit cache by `COPY . .`
description: The Dockerfile runs `COPY . .` into the build stage (Dockerfile:12). .dockerignore excludes only .git, .github and findings. The documented quickstart tells users to `cp .env.example .env` and fill in LAYERLEAK_DB_PASSWORD; .env is gitignored but not dockerignored, so any local `docker build`/`docker compose build` sends it in the build context and stores it in the builder layer and BuildKit cache. The final scratch image only copies /out and migrations so the published image is unaffected, and release builds run in CI where no .env exists, hence low severity. CFG-12 covered context bloat/cache invalidation but not the secret-file aspect.
evidence: .dockerignore (entire file): `.git`, `.github`, `findings`. Dockerfile:12 `COPY . .`. .gitignore:36 `.env`.
proposed_fix: Extend .dockerignore to at least `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `node_modules`, `web/`, `docs/`, `scripts/`, `*.md`, `.venv*`, `__pycache__/`; or invert to an allowlist (go.mod, go.sum, *.go dirs, migrations/). Optionally replace `COPY . .` with explicit `COPY cmd internal migrations main.go ./`.

title: TTY progress mode writes raw ANSI cursor sequences and a box-drawing logo without enabling Windows VT processing; Windows support is implied but never tested
description: The CLI cross-compiles cleanly for windows/amd64 and darwin/arm64 (`GOOS=windows go build ./...` and `go vet` both pass), and the Go install path makes Windows users possible. In TTY mode the renderer emits `\x1b[%dA` and `\r\x1b[2K` and prints a box-drawing-character logo (progress.go:15-29, 131, 208, 214). No code enables ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_PROCESSING (no golang.org/x/sys/windows import, no SetConsoleMode), so on legacy conhost (cmd.exe/PowerShell on Windows 10 without Windows Terminal) the escape sequences are printed literally and the eight-line block never redraws; the logo also depends on a UTF-8 code page. There is no NO_COLOR concern (no colour codes are emitted), but there is no documented platform-support statement, no Windows/macOS CI job (REL-19), and no per-OS fallback. CLI-01 (chmod) and CLI-26 (hard links) also behave differently on Windows filesystems.
evidence: `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` -> exit 0; `grep -rn "SetConsoleMode\|ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL\|golang.org/x/sys/windows" --include=*.go .` -> none; progress.go:208 `fmt.Fprintf(r.out, "\x1b[%dA", progressBlockLines)`; progress.go:214 `fmt.Fprint(r.out, "\r\x1b[2K")`; README has no match for windows/macos/darwin.
proposed_fix: Decide and document the supported CLI platforms for 3.0.0 (README 'Platform support' section). If Windows is supported: add a `progress_windows.go` that enables virtual-terminal processing via golang.org/x/sys/windows (already an indirect dependency) and falls back to plain mode when it fails; replace the logo with ASCII or print it only when the console is UTF-8. If not: state 'Linux and macOS only' and have the Windows build auto-select `--progress plain`. Add a windows-latest/macos-latest `go build` + unit-test job (REL-19).

title: CodeQL scans only Go although the repository ships JavaScript, Python and GitHub Actions workflows
description: The CodeQL matrix is `language: [ 'go' ]`. The repository also contains browser JavaScript served on GitHub Pages (web/assets/demo.js, web/assets/site.js), Node test code (scripts/tests/test_demo.cjs), Python release tooling that executes subprocesses and parses untrusted release metadata (scripts/release-preflight.py, scripts/verify-container-platform.py, scripts/validate_docs.py), and six workflows. CodeQL supports javascript-typescript, python and actions; none are scanned. REL-16 covered schedule/autobuild/query suite but not language coverage.
evidence: .github/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml:22 `language: [ 'go' ]`; `git ls-files` shows web/assets/*.js, scripts/*.py, scripts/tests/test_demo.cjs.
proposed_fix: Change the matrix to `language: [ 'go', 'javascript-typescript', 'python', 'actions' ]` (actions and javascript-typescript need no build step), keep `build-mode: none`/autobuild only for Go, and add `timeout-minutes` while editing (REL-16).

title: CI never runs the two fuzz targets beyond their seed corpus and never shuffles test order
description: FuzzParseReference (reference_test.go:217) and FuzzVerifyingReader (integrity_test.go:122) exist but no workflow runs `go test -fuzz`, so only the seed inputs are exercised; no `-shuffle=on` run exists to catch order-dependent tests (DET-23 notes order-dependent Deduplicate behaviour). LAY-19 and PRD-22 ask for more fuzz targets but nobody noted that the existing ones are effectively unit tests in CI.
evidence: `grep -n -i "fuzz\|-shuffle" .github/workflows/*.yml` -> no matches; verify.yml:60 `run: go test -short ./... -count=1`; verify.yml:63 `run: go test -short -race ./... -count=1`.
proposed_fix: Add a short fuzz smoke step to verify.yml: `for f in FuzzParseReference FuzzVerifyingReader; do go test ./internal/manifest -run '^$' -fuzz="^${f}$" -fuzztime=30s; done` (extend as PRD-22 targets land) and run the unit suite once with `-shuffle=on`. Optionally a weekly scheduled workflow with a longer -fuzztime.

title: README documents neither proxy environment handling, platform support, shell completion, nor the API's plain-HTTP/TLS-termination expectation
description: The registry client honours HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY through the base transport's Proxy function (client.go:1080-1087; currently broken for hostname-policy proxies, REG-01) but README never mentions proxies; the API serves plain HTTP only (no TLS option anywhere in internal/api or internal/config) and README:45-47 says only 'expose it only on a trusted network or behind an authenticated gateway' without saying TLS must be terminated there; cobra's auto-generated `layerleak completion bash|zsh|fish|powershell` exists but is undocumented; there is no supported-OS statement (see GAP-04). These are the first questions a 3.0.0 adopter asks and the answers exist only in code.
evidence: `grep -n -i "TLS\|HTTPS_PROXY\|NO_PROXY\|completion\|windows\|macos" README.md` -> no matches; `grep -rn -i "tls\|certificate" internal/api internal/config cmd` -> none; client.go:1080 `if t.base.Proxy != nil { proxyURL, proxyErr := t.base.Proxy(originalRequest)`.
proposed_fix: Add three short README sections before 3.0.0: 'Platform support' (tested OS/arch, Windows caveats), 'Networking' (HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY honoured once REG-01 is fixed; egress allowlist interplay; the API listens on plain HTTP and expects TLS termination and authentication at a reverse proxy/gateway), and 'Shell completion' (`layerleak completion <shell>`). Mirror the first two in web/docs/index.html.

title: GitHub refresh tokens (ghr_) longer than 36 characters are rejected by the trailing \b
description: `\b(?:gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{82})\b` requires exactly 36 body characters for all five prefixes. GitHub's documented refresh-token example (`ghr_<redacted>`) is 80 characters (76 after the prefix) and gitleaks v7.4.0/truffleHog use `ghr_[0-9a-zA-Z]{76}`; current gitleaks uses `{36}` without a trailing anchor, which still matches a longer token as a prefix. With the trailing `\b` this rule matches neither shape for a 76-char body. Confidence is medium because GitHub's current docs no longer show a literal example.
evidence: Probe: `github refresh token ghr_ 76 => <none>`; `ghs token (36) => github_token[0:40]`; `github fine-grained pat (82) => github_token[9:102]` (fine-grained OK). Web: gitleaks release v7.4.0 introduced `ghr_[0-9a-zA-Z]{76}`; gist 'regex including new github tokens pattern' shows both 36 and 76 variants.
proposed_fix: Adopt ghr_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,76} with a post-match boundary check; or drop the trailing \b for ghr_ only.
verifier_note: Probe confirms ghr_ with a 76-char body => <none> and 36-char => github_token. Current GitHub docs (both the current and the github-ae pages) no longer show a literal example, and gitleaks uses ghr_[0-9a-zA-Z]{36} without a trailing anchor, so the real body length could not be settled from primary sources. The proposed {36,76} is harmless under either hypothesis.

title: Default-credential pairs (admin:admin, root:password, test:test, user foobar) are silently discarded even on production hosts
description: DiscardReason removes matches whose credentials equal a placeholder pair or whose username is `foobar` regardless of host, and Set.Scan drops them before normalization (detectors.go:162-169), so `https://admin:admin@prod-db.internal/` yields no finding of any disposition. A shipped image with default credentials is a finding (CWE-1392) and the user has no way to see that it was dropped.
evidence: Probe: `admin:admin real host (https://admin:admin@prod-db.internal/) => <none>`. Code policy.go:286-294 `if isPlaceholderCredentialPair(username, password) { return true } if username == "foobar" { return true }`; detectors.go:164 `if detectionpolicy.DiscardReason(match.Value) != detectionpolicy.ReasonNone { continue }`.
proposed_fix: As proposed (emit as suppressed/known_dummy or a new default_credentials reason instead of silent discard); update policy_test expectations.
verifier_note: Probe: https://admin:admin@prod-db.internal/ => <none>; policy.go:286-290 and detectors.go:164 confirmed. policy_test.go:70-83 shows this is intentional, so it is a policy choice rather than an accidental bug; kind could be 'compat'.

title: netrc_password matches the word after 'password' anywhere, including comments, at HIGH confidence
description: `(?im)\bpassword\s+([^\s#]+)` with a 4-character minimum accepts any following word; the .netrc path bump (sensitivePath) raises the result to high. Comment lines and macdef bodies produce false positives with a real-looking redacted value.
evidence: Probe: `.netrc "# password rotated quarterly\nmachine x login y password abc" => netrc_password[11:18]="rotated"(high)`. Code detectors.go:84.
proposed_fix: As proposed.
verifier_note: Probe on /root/.netrc: '# password rotated quarterly\nmachine x login y password abc' => netrc_password[11:18]="rotated"(high).

title: git_credentials_password is skipped when the stored password is percent-encoded
description: The detector locates the span with `needle := ":" + password + "@"` where `password` comes from `parsed.User.Password()` (already unescaped). git credential-store URL-encodes `@`, `/`, `#`, `:` and `%` in passwords, so the needle is not found and the match is dropped (`continue`); only the whole-URL basic_auth_url finding remains, and the structured priority/pairing is lost.
evidence: Probe on /root/.git-credentials: `https://deploy:p%40ssw0rdXyzAbc@github.com/... => basic_auth_url[0:42]` only; `https://deploy:passw0rdXyzAbc@github.com/... => basic_auth_url | git_credentials_password[15:29]`; `p%2Fssw0rd%23XyzAbc => basic_auth_url only`. Code structured.go:310-314.
proposed_fix: As proposed; report the raw encoded bytes as Value so NormalizeWithRaw's span check holds.
verifier_note: Probe: https://deploy:p%40ssw0rdXyzAbc@github.com/... => basic_auth_url only; plain password => basic_auth_url + git_credentials_password[15:29]. structured.go:310 needle uses the decoded password.

title: parseINIKeyValue keeps quotes on CRLF lines, disabling aws_shared_credentials_* for quoted Windows-style credential files
description: The value is right-trimmed only of ' ' and '\t' before the surrounding-quote check, so on CRLF input the value is `"..."\r`, the quote pair is not recognised, and the later TrimSpace leaves the quotes in place. looksLikeAWSAccessKeyID/looksLikeAWSSecretAccessKey then fail (wrong length) and the structured detector emits nothing; the generic aws_access_key_id/aws_secret_access_key regexes still fire but without profile pairing/priority.
evidence: Probe: `aws credentials CRLF quoted => aws_access_key_id[32:52] | aws_secret_access_key[80:120]` (no aws_shared_credentials_*), `aws credentials CRLF unquoted => aws_shared_credentials_access_key_id | aws_shared_credentials_secret_access_key`, `BOM => aws_shared_credentials_*` (OK). Code structured.go:263 `value = strings.TrimRight(trimmedLeft, " \t")` then :265 quote check.
proposed_fix: As proposed.
verifier_note: Probe: CRLF + quoted .aws/credentials => only generic aws_access_key_id/aws_secret_access_key (p3); CRLF unquoted => aws_shared_credentials_* (p4). structured.go:263 trims only ' \t' before the quote check.

title: Capture-boundary defects: npmrc quoted tokens include quotes (2 findings per secret), databricks/telegram/aws-secret captures are truncated or unanchored
description: (a) npmrc_auth_token `([^\s#;]+)` keeps surrounding quotes, so `_authToken="npm_..."` yields npmrc_auth_token (quoted value, span 33:75) plus npm_token (34:74): two findings and two fingerprints for one secret. (b) databricks_token `dapi[A-Za-z0-9]{32}\b` drops the modern `-2`/`-3` suffix. (c) telegram_bot_token has no trailing boundary so a 36+-char secret is cut at 35 and the remainder is visible in context. (d) aws_secret_access_key (line 74) has no trailing boundary so a 41st character is left in plaintext.
evidence: Probe: `npmrc quoted token => npmrc_auth_token[33:75]="\"npm_<redacted>\"" | npm_token[34:74]`; `databricks -3 suffix => databricks_token[0:36]` (suffix excluded); `telegram 36 chars => telegram_bot_token[4:50]` (last char excluded); `aws secret 41 chars => aws_secret_access_key[22:62]`.
proposed_fix: As proposed.
verifier_note: Probe: quoted _authToken => npmrc_auth_token[33:75] with quotes + npm_token[34:74] (two findings); dapi...-3 => databricks_token[0:36] (suffix dropped; gitleaks uses dapi[a-f0-9]{32}(?:-\d)? confirming the suffix); telegram 36-char secret => cut at 35. Item (d) is not a real-world defect because AWS secrets are exactly 40 chars, but the trailing boundary still reduces false positives.

description: Set.Scan removes only exact (value,start,end) duplicates. A lower-priority match fully contained in a higher-priority one (keyword_entropy on the password inside a basic_auth_url match; git_credentials_password inside basic_auth_url is intentional) is kept, inflating counts and creating redundant fingerprints.

title: assigned_sensitive_value has priority 4 (above specific rules) and an always-high confidence, so identical-span collisions are labelled by the generic detector
description: priorityForKeyValueDetector returns priorityStructured (4) for assigned_sensitive_value while every self-identifying regex rule is priorityLocal (3). When both match the same span, Set.Scan keeps the generic name. Today this is reachable only when ScanInput.Content is value-only with a matching Key (not produced by scanner.go), but the DET-01/DET-03 fix makes env 'CLIENT_SECRET=ghp_...' produce identical spans, after which the finding would be reported as assigned_sensitive_value instead of github_token. Separately, its base ConfidenceMedium is dead code: the key regex (client_secret|access_token|refresh_token|auth_token) always satisfies sensitiveKey, so adjustConfidence promotes every match to high.
evidence: Probe: Key=ACCESS_TOKEN Content='ghp_<redacted>' => assigned_sensitive_value[0:40](high,p4) only (github_token suppressed by same-span dedup). Probe: Key=CLIENT_SECRET Content='CLIENT_SECRET=<rnd>' => assigned_sensitive_value(high) despite base medium. Code detectors.go:856-863, :171-188, :64.
proposed_fix: Return a priority below priorityLocal (e.g. 2) for assigned_sensitive_value so specific rules win identical spans, or add a tie-break that prefers detectors with a self-identifying prefix; set the rule's base to high explicitly (or exclude the key from the score) so the declared confidence is truthful. Add a test asserting github_token wins over assigned_sensitive_value on the same span.

title: UTF-8 BOM is not stripped before INI section parsing, so a BOM-prefixed first profile is merged into 'default'
description: parseAWSSharedCredentialsEntries uses strings.TrimSpace, which does not remove U+FEFF (not a Unicode White_Space character). A file beginning with '﻿[prod]' never enters the section branch at line 212, so its entries are attributed to the implicit 'default' section. Detection still works for a single-profile file (hence the checked_ok claim), but with a later real [default] profile the two are merged and profilesWithSecrets pairing/promotion is wrong (an unpaired BOM'd access key is promoted to high by another profile's secret).
evidence: structured.go:207 `trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line.Value)` then :212 `if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "[") ...`; Go unicode.IsSpace(0xFEFF) == false (U+FEFF is category Cf, not White_Space), so '﻿[prod]' does not match.
proposed_fix: TrimPrefix("﻿") on the first line (or on content before splitLinesWithOffsets, adjusting offsets by 3), and add a BOM + two-profile test asserting section attribution.

title: README says the API 'will remain unready on an older schema'; it actually refuses to start (RequireSchema), which RELEASING states correctly

After startup, /readyz re-checks the database and schema on every probe and reports later degradation without affecting /health or /livez.'

title: Progress never counts partial targets and double-counts failed tags during resolution
description: Every ProgressUpdate emitted by scanRepository and the final snapshots in cli/scan.go pass TargetsCompleted=CompletedTargetCount and TargetsFailed=FailedTargetCount but never PartialTargetCount, and progressCounts() sums only completed+failed, so a finished sweep with one partial target renders 'Targets 1/2 complete' and a bar that never fills. During tag resolution TagsCompleted is set to TagsResolved+TagsFailed while TagsFailed is also passed, so progressLabel prints '1/3 complete, 1 failed' after zero tags resolved and progressCounts adds failed twice; in the scanning phase TagsCompleted switches to TagsResolved, so the numbers jump. Additionally scanner's ManifestFailed phase is mapped to ProgressPhaseTargetFailed (line 615-616) even when the target continues as partial, and each target emits target_done twice (scanner completion + jobs' own).
evidence: jobs/scan.go:304-306 TagsCompleted: result.TagsResolved + result.TagsFailed, TagsFailed: result.TagsFailed; jobs/scan.go:385-387, 419-421, 461-463, 481-483 omit PartialTargetCount; cli/progress.go:370-378 progressCounts = completed+failed; cli/scan.go:144-146, 186-188, 203-205 same omission. Probe: final update 'phase=completed targetsCompleted=1 targetsFailed=0 targetsTotal=2' for a sweep whose result reports completed=1 partial=1; resolving phase 'tag=idx tagsCompleted=1 tagsFailed=1' with 0 resolved.
proposed_fix: Add TargetsPartial to jobs.ProgressUpdate and progressSnapshot, include it in progressCounts and progressLabel ('%d/%d done (%d partial, %d failed)'), pass TagsCompleted=TagsResolved consistently in both phases, map scanner ManifestFailed to Scanning (with the failure message) unless the target itself failed, and suppress the duplicate target_done. Cover with a renderer test built from a partial-target ProgressUpdate.
verifier_note: jobs/scan.go:304-306 passes TagsCompleted = TagsResolved+TagsFailed together with TagsFailed, and progress.go:370-378 progressCounts adds failed again; every jobs ProgressUpdate (scan.go:385-390, 416-421, 458-463, 478-483) and the CLI snapshots (cli/scan.go:140-146, 183-189, 199-205) omit PartialTargetCount; ProgressUpdate has no TargetsPartial field (:104-119); mapScannerPhase (:615-616) maps ManifestFailed to TargetFailed. Probe counted 2 target_done events for a single target (scanner Completed mapped at :617-618 plus jobs' own at :455).

title: Scan-timeout and cancellation errors are printed twice ('context deadline exceeded context deadline exceeded') with no hint about LAYERLEAK_SCAN_TIMEOUT
description: operationErr already contains the context error (jobs/scanner return ctx.Err() wrapped or bare) and RunE then errors.Join()s ctx.Err() again; root.go collapses the joined newline into a space, so the user sees the same sentence twice and never learns which setting (LAYERLEAK_SCAN_TIMEOUT, default 30m) produced it or that exit 1 was a timeout rather than a registry failure.

Add a CLI test asserting a single, descriptive message.

title: Retire or version the 'compatible findings array' now that the scans/ record exists
description: Every scan writes two files with the same basename: the legacy array (kept 'compatible' with v1 consumers) and the redacted record. The legacy file is the only place raw values can appear (with LAYERLEAK_PERSIST_RAW_SECRETS), applies a low-confidence cap that stdout/API/DB do not, and has no schema version, so it can never evolve. A major release is the moment to make the record the single artifact (optionally embedding persisted findings) and stop writing the array by default.
evidence: results.go:302-306 publishResultArtifacts writes both; results.go:113-116 raw fields only in the legacy array; README.md:156-157 'findings/<basename>.json remains the compatible findings array'.
proposed_fix: In 3.0.0 write only findings/scans/<basename>.json by default, add a findings[] array (persistedFinding, versioned) inside the record, and offer --legacy-findings-array for one release with a deprecation notice in CHANGELOG/README.
verifier_note: publishResultArtifacts (results.go:302-306) always writes both files; raw fields exist only in the legacy array (:113-116); the array has no version field. Additionally the 3-per-group cap that distinguishes the array is effectively dead code (see CLI-25), strengthening the case for retiring or redefining the array in 3.0.0.

title: Result JSON carries no timestamps, duration or tool version; DB scanned_at is the end time
description: jobs.Result has no started_at/finished_at/duration/tool_version/detector-set version, so a stdout JSON result cannot be dated or attributed to a scanner version; only the local record adds created_at and the DB uses scannedAt taken after the scan completes (service.go:143), so long sweeps are recorded with their finish time and no duration. Deterministic ordering (sorted targets/platform results/findings, RFC3339 UTC times) is otherwise fine.
evidence: jobs/scan.go:123-153 Result struct has no time or version fields; scanservice/service.go:143 scannedAt := s.now().UTC() executes after jobs.Scan returns; cli/results.go:298 CreatedAt: time.Now().UTC() only in localScanRecord.
proposed_fix: Add started_at, finished_at (RFC3339 UTC), duration_ms and tool_version (from cli.effectiveVersion, threaded via scanservice.Request) to jobs.Result under result_schema_version 2; record StartedAt in the DB scan_runs row (migration) and expose via API/openapi.
verifier_note: jobs.Result (scan.go:123-153) has no time/duration/version fields; scanservice/service.go:143 takes scannedAt after jobs.Scan returns; only localScanRecord (results.go:298) carries created_at.

title: Debug logging writes JSON lines to os.Stderr between TTY progress frames, corrupting the 8-line redraw block
description: newLogger targets os.Stderr directly (not cmd.ErrOrStderr()), and scanner emits Debug 'scanned platform manifest' per manifest plus the CLI's own 'progress update failed' lines. In tty mode the renderer moves the cursor up progressBlockLines=8 and clears lines, so any log line printed since the last frame is overwritten or leaves stale text. Dynamic mode is also enabled purely on term.IsTerminal without honouring TERM=dumb or enabling VT processing on legacy Windows consoles.
evidence: logging.go:15 slog.NewJSONHandler(os.Stderr, ...); scanner/scan.go:473 request.Logger.DebugContext(ctx, "scanned platform manifest", ...); progress.go:207-216 fmt.Fprintf(r.out, "\x1b[%dA", progressBlockLines) then "\r\x1b[2K"; progress.go:88-99 mode selection consults only IsTerminal.
proposed_fix: Pass cmd.ErrOrStderr() into newLogger and, when the renderer is dynamic, wrap the log writer so lines are printed above the block (erase block, print log, redraw) or fall back to plain progress when LAYERLEAK_LOG_LEVEL=debug; treat TERM=dumb / CI=true as plain. Add a renderer test interleaving a log write.
verifier_note: logging.go:15 writes to os.Stderr rather than cmd.ErrOrStderr(); scanner/scan.go:472-478 logs 'scanned platform manifest' at Debug; progress.go:207-216 redraws by moving up progressBlockLines=8. Impact is limited to LAYERLEAK_LOG_LEVEL=debug (default is info, config.go:65), consistent with low severity. progress.go:88-99 selects dynamic mode purely on term.IsTerminal.

title: Second Ctrl-C is swallowed for the whole run; no way to force-quit a stuck scan
description: signal.NotifyContext keeps capturing SIGINT/SIGTERM until stop() runs, which is deferred until Execute returns. If a registry read is blocked in a non-context-aware section or a slow store Close, a second Ctrl-C does nothing; the conventional behaviour is to restore default handling after the first signal so the second one terminates the process.
evidence: root.go:15-16: ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM); defer stop()
proposed_fix: After the first signal (go func(){ <-ctx.Done(); stop() }()) restore defaults so a second signal kills the process, and print 'interrupt received, finishing...' to stderr. Consider exit code 130 for SIGINT in 3.0.0 (currently documented as 1).
verifier_note: root.go:15-16 keeps signal.NotifyContext active until Execute returns (deferred stop), so a second SIGINT is swallowed; no 130 exit code (README.md:141 documents 1 for cancellation).

title: Single-reference partial results omit tag_results, and single-tag scans report 'Tags Enumerated: 1'
description: scanSingleReference only populates TagResults when err == nil, so a partial single-tag scan (IncompleteError) has no tag_results while a completed one does, making the JSON shape depend on outcome. It also sets TagsEnumerated/TagsResolved = len(tags) (1 for tag refs), so the summary prints 'Tags Enumerated: 1 / Resolved: 1 / Failed: 0' for a plain `scan app:latest` even though no enumeration happened.
evidence: jobs/scan.go:239-246: if len(tags) > 0 && err == nil { result.TagResults = ... }; jobs/scan.go:212-213 TagsEnumerated: len(tags), TagsResolved: len(tags); cli/scan.go:389 shows tag rows when TagsEnumerated > 0; summary_test.go:115 'enumerated reference' codifies it.
proposed_fix: Populate TagResults in scanSingleReference whenever scanResult.RequestedDigest is non-empty, regardless of err (status scanned/partial/failed from the outcome), and leave TagsEnumerated/TagsResolved at 0 in reference mode; adjust TestRenderSummaryConditionalRows 'enumerated reference' accordingly.
verifier_note: The 'Tags Enumerated: 1' half is confirmed (jobs/scan.go:212-213 sets TagsEnumerated/TagsResolved = len(tags); probe shows tags_enumerated=1 for a plain tag scan). The missing-tag_results half is narrower than described: scanner only returns err != nil after a completed manifest for limits/integrity/cancellation (scanner/scan.go:287-290), and jobs/scan.go:239 gates TagResults on err == nil, so tag_results vanish only for limit/integrity-aborted partials (the exact scenario accepted by --allow-partial in TestScanCommandWritesPartialResultsOnConfiguredLimitError). A manifest-failure partial (err == nil) does include tag_results (probe: status=partial tag_results_present=true).

title: Reported artifact paths are passed through sanitizeProgressValue, mangling paths with repeated or tab whitespace
description: The 'Findings: <path>' / 'Scan record: <path>' lines collapse any run of whitespace in the real filesystem path to a single space, so a LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR containing two spaces or a tab yields a path that does not exist when copied. sanitizeProgressValue also only strips Unicode Cc controls, not Cf format characters (e.g. U+202E RTL override) that could reorder untrusted registry error text on a terminal.
evidence: cli/scan.go:244 fmt.Fprintf(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "%s: %s\n", artifact.label, sanitizeProgressValue(artifact.path)); progress.go:393-398 FieldsFunc(unicode.IsSpace || unicode.IsControl). Probe: "/data/my  results/x.json" -> "/data/my results/x.json".
proposed_fix: Print artifact paths with %q (or only strip control characters, not spaces) since they are trusted local paths; extend sanitizeProgressValue to drop unicode.Is(unicode.Cf, r) for untrusted registry text.
verifier_note: cli/scan.go:244 passes the real path through sanitizeProgressValue (progress.go:393-398 splits on unicode.IsSpace||IsControl and rejoins with single spaces). Probe: "/data/my  results/x.json" -> "/data/my results/x.json". TestScanCommandReportsDurableArtifactPaths only uses hyphenated directory names so it passes.

title: CLI opens and schema-checks PostgreSQL before scanning with no opt-out flag
description: If LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_URL is set (e.g. shared with an API deployment's env) the CLI dials, pings, checks server version and RequireSchema before any registry work, and an unreachable or un-migrated DB aborts the scan (exit 1) instead of scanning and recording persistence failure as it does for save failures. There is no --no-database / --store none flag to run a purely local scan in that environment. Error text from NewPostgresStore does not include the DSN (Validate returns fixed strings), so no credential leak.
evidence: cli/scan.go:109 store, err := openStore(cfg) before service.ScanAndSave; storage.go:24 RequireSchema: true; scan_test.go:134-147 TestScanCommandFailsWhenDatabaseIsConfiguredButUnavailable asserts the abort; storage/storage.go:220-243 Validate errors are fixed strings.
proposed_fix: Add --no-database (or --store=none|postgres) to the scan command; optionally defer opening the store until BeforeSave so a down DB becomes a recorded persistence failure with local artifacts still written, and mention the flag in README env table for LAYERLEAK_DATABASE_URL.
verifier_note: cli/scan.go:109 opens the store before scanning; storage.go:24 RequireSchema: true; postgres.go:47-63 pings, checks server version and schema at open; scan_test.go:134-147 codifies the abort. No --no-database flag exists (flags at scan.go:283-290).

description: Both files are 116 bytes with identical content; README says cmd/* are development build targets, but cmd/scanner adds nothing over the module root and doubles the import path that must be migrated to /v3. Keeping two entrypoints invites drift (e.g. a future -X Version wiring applied to one).

title: --all-tags resolves every tag serially before applying the target bound; help text lacks examples, exit codes and env cross-references
description: scanRepository issues one HEAD per tag sequentially (line 311) and only afterwards compares len(groupList) to MaxRepositoryTargets (367-370), so a 1000-tag repository with the default 250-target cap performs 1000 network round-trips before failing with no scan performed. Separately, the scan command has no Long/Example text: --help does not mention exit codes 0/1/2, LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR, LAYERLEAK_SCAN_TIMEOUT or the two artifacts, and unknown-flag errors print no 'see --help' pointer because SilenceUsage is set.
evidence: jobs/scan.go:311 resolved, err := request.Registry.ResolveManifest(ctx, ...) inside the for-tags loop; jobs/scan.go:367 if request.MaxRepositoryTargets > 0 && len(groupList) > request.MaxRepositoryTargets; cli/scan.go:38-41 Command has Use/Short/Args only; live run: `layerleak scan --bogus` -> 'unknown flag: --bogus' exit 1 with no usage hint.
proposed_fix: Fail fast when len(groups) exceeds MaxRepositoryTargets during resolution and resolve tags with bounded concurrency (e.g. 4-8) preserving deterministic ordering; add Long/Example to root and scan commands listing exit codes, artifacts and key env vars, and set cmd.SetFlagErrorFunc to append "Run 'layerleak scan --help'".

Built binary: `layerleak scan --bogus` prints only 'unknown flag: --bogus' (rc=1) and `layerleak scan` prints 'accepts 1 arg(s), received 0' with no usage pointer; cmd has no Long/Example (scan.go:38-41).

If 3.0.0 adopts any shape change from this report (skipped status, timestamps/tool_version, dropped legacy array, tag_results changes) the versions must be bumped together and the openapi minimum updated; if not, the CHANGELOG should state explicitly that the JSON schemas are unchanged at 3.0.0.
