title: json omitempty on struct-typed Platform fields never omits; JSON always carries "platform": {}
description: encoding/json's omitempty does not treat a non-pointer struct as empty, so persistedFinding.Platform (results.go:27), scanner.PlatformResult.Platform (scanner/scan.go:130), findings.Finding.Platform (findings.go:88) and manifest.Descriptor.Platform (document.go:40) are always serialised. Platform-less entries (root-manifest failures before the config is fetched, or metadata findings on unresolved manifests) therefore emit "platform": {}, which does not match the optional-field intent in openapi.yaml (PlatformResult.platform optional) or the JSON Schemas proposed in CLI-09.
evidence: Probe: json.Marshal(struct{ Platform manifest.Platform `json:"platform,omitempty"` }{}) -> {"platform":{}}. manifest/document.go:27-31 Platform is a plain struct with no MarshalJSON/IsZero.
proposed_fix: Switch these tags to `json:"platform,omitzero"` (Go 1.24+, go.mod already requires 1.25.13) or use *manifest.Platform; bump result_schema_version if the shape change is adopted and update openapi/schemas accordingly.

title: Legacy-array low-confidence cap is effectively dead code; README's 'deduplicated occurrence counts' are almost never populated
description: persistedFindingGroupKey (results.go:153-172) groups by detector, confidence, disposition, source type, manifest, platform, file path, layer, key, LINE NUMBER and FINGERPRINT. jobs.finalizeResult already runs findings.DeduplicateDetailed (findings.go:293-309, key at :465-497) whose key covers the same identity plus matchStart/matchEnd, so by the time buildPersistedFindings runs, two findings can only share a cap group if the same secret value appears at different offsets on the same line of the same file. The 3-per-group cap, occurrence_count and suppressed_occurrence_count therefore practically never fire, yet README.md:174 advertises 'deduplicated occurrence counts'. TestBuildPersistedFindingsCapsRepeatedLowConfidenceFileFindings (results_test.go:198) passes only because it feeds pre-dedup items with distinct SourceLocations that the real pipeline would have already collapsed or kept.
evidence: results.go:158-171 key includes strconv.Itoa(item.LineNumber) and item.Fingerprint; findings.go:465-476 snippetDedupKey{manifestDigest, platform, disposition, sourceLocation, layerDigest, detectorName, fingerprint, lineNumber, matchStart, matchEnd}; jobs/scan.go:647 finalizeResult calls DeduplicateDetailed before any CLI code sees the result.
proposed_fix: Either remove the cap with the legacy array (CLI-10) and drop the README bullet, or make it deliver the documented behaviour by grouping on (detector, fingerprint, manifest, platform, file path) without line/offset so repeated low-confidence hits across a file collapse into one record with a real occurrence_count; add a test that drives the real pipeline (jobs.Result after finalizeResult) rather than hand-built items.

title: Artifact publication depends on hard links and has no fallback on filesystems that lack them
description: publishResultJSON publishes via os.Link(temporary, path). Filesystems without hard-link support (FAT/exFAT removable media, some SMB/NFS/9p/FUSE mounts, certain container bind mounts) return EPERM/ENOTSUP/EXDEV, so every scan ends with 'publish result file: ...' and exit 1 even though the scan itself succeeded and stdout JSON was never reached (cli/scan.go:213-214 runs before output; :264 returns the publication error). There is no fallback and no flag to skip artifacts (see CLI-03).
evidence: results.go:77-80: path := filepath.Join(dir, name); if err := os.Link(temporary, path); err != nil { return "", fmt.Errorf("publish result file: %w", err) }. TestWriteResultArtifacts* all run on the test tmpfs/ext4 where link succeeds.
proposed_fix: When os.Link fails with an errno other than EEXIST, fall back to os.OpenFile(path, O_WRONLY|O_CREATE|O_EXCL, 0o600) + copy + Sync (preserving the no-overwrite guarantee), or write directly with O_EXCL and skip the temp file; add a unit test that injects a link failure. Pair with a --no-artifacts/--output-dir flag so JSON consumers can opt out entirely.

title: Unaccepted-partial failure message never mentions --allow-partial
description: When coverage is partial and --allow-partial was not passed, the CLI exits 1 with the bare IncompleteError text ('scan coverage is partial: N manifest(s) completed, M failed'). Nothing in the message, the summary or --help (no Long/Example, see CLI-20) tells the user that the result is usable and can be accepted with --allow-partial, so CI users typically learn of the flag only from the README.
evidence: cli/scan.go:267-268: if scanErr != nil && !acceptPartial { return exitError{code: 1, message: scanErr.Error()} }; jobs/scan.go:69-74 IncompleteError.Error() formats only status and counts.
proposed_fix: When jobs.IsIncomplete(scanErr) || limits.IsExceeded(scanErr) and hasUsablePartialResult(result), append ' (re-run with --allow-partial to accept usable partial coverage)' to the exitError message; cover with a CLI test.

title: tag_results.status vocabulary is inconsistent across modes and undocumented in openapi
description: Reference mode emits status 'scanned' (jobs/scan.go:244); repository mode emits 'resolved' or 'failed' at resolution time (:316, :341) and never updates a tag after its target completes, fails or is skipped, while the DB maps tags to 'scanned'/'partial'/'failed' (record.go:201-212). openapi.yaml:650-651 types TagResult.status as a bare string with no enum or description, so API and CLI consumers have no contract for the values. A 3.0.0 schema bump is the right moment to unify.
evidence: jobs/scan.go:244 Status: "scanned"; :316 Status: "failed"; :341 Status: "resolved"; record.go:201-212 storedScanStatus returns scanned/partial/failed; openapi.yaml:650-651: status: type: string (no enum).
proposed_fix: Define a jobs.TagStatus enum {resolved, scanned, partial, failed, skipped}, update TagResults after each target outcome in scanRepository (and in the skipped paths from CLI-04), use 'scanned' consistently in both modes, add the enum and descriptions to openapi TagResult, and bump result_schema_version with the other 3.0.0 shape changes (CLI-21).

title: Draining a sparse-file hole ignores context cancellation when MAX_LAYER_BYTES and MAX_IMAGE_LAYER_BYTES are both disabled
description: The context-aware reader wraps the *decompressed stream* beneath tar.Reader (state.go:189). Sparse holes are synthesized by archive/tar's zeroReader without touching that stream, so `io.Copy(io.Discard, reader)` in buildRegularArtifact and drainEntry runs to completion regardless of ctx, BlobTimeout or SCAN_TIMEOUT. With both byte limits set to 0 (README:198 documents 0 as 'disables'), logicalLayerBudget no longer rejects the header, so a PAX/GNU sparse entry declaring a 2^62-byte hole pins the worker (API default concurrency 1) for years at ~100 GiB/s of memset. With defaults the hole is bounded to 512 MiB and finishes in milliseconds.
evidence: Probe with limits disabled, cancel at 100 ms: 16 GiB hole → `elapsed=150ms` (cancel noticed only at the trailing data fragment); 512 GiB hole → `err=... discard remaining file bytes for "app/sparse": context canceled elapsed=4.741s`. Code: state.go:835 `if _, err := io.Copy(io.Discard, reader); err != nil` (reader is tarReader); state.go:1143-1149 drainEntry likewise; state.go:188-189 `newLayerLimitReader(newContextReader(ctx, reader), ...)`. Go reader.go sparseFileReader.Read: `nf, err = tryReadFull(zeroReader{}, bf)`.
proposed_fix: Wrap the per-entry reader: pass newContextReader(ctx, tarReader) into buildRegularArtifact and drainEntry (or check ctx every N MiB in a copy loop). The suggested hard ceiling on header.Size when limits are disabled contradicts README:198 ('0 disables'); prefer documenting that disabling both byte limits removes the bound, or clamp at math.MaxInt64 only.
verifier_note: Mechanism confirmed: buildRegularArtifact (state.go:835) and drainEntry (state.go:1144) copy from tarReader, whose sparse holes are synthesized by archive/tar's zeroReader (reader.go:752) without touching the context-wrapped stream at state.go:189. Probe with MaxLayerBytes=0 and MaxTotalBytes=0, 16 GiB hole, cancel at 100 ms: Replay returned at 154 ms only because the trailing 1-byte data fragment hit the context reader; cancellation was not observed during the hole itself. However the exposure requires the operator to disable BOTH MAX_LAYER_BYTES and MAX_IMAGE_LAYER_BYTES; at defaults logicalLayerBudget.add (state.go:239) rejects any header.Size above 512 MiB and the hole finishes in milliseconds. That is an opt-in misconfiguration, so medium overstates it.

title: PAX global headers ('g') are materialized as "other" artifacts, displace a real file of the same name, and count toward entry limits
description: archive/tar returns TypeXGlobalHeader records as entries (Name is the raw header name, typically `pax_global_header`, as written by git archive / GNU tar --pax-option). The engine's default branch stores an ArtifactTypeOther at that path, so a genuine file named pax_global_header from a lower layer is moved to DeletedArtifacts with a bogus deletion, and the metadata record consumes MAX_LAYER_ENTRIES/MAX_IMAGE_ARTIFACTS budget. Docker/containerd skip global headers.
evidence: Probe: lower layer has regular file `pax_global_header`; upper layer has a TypeXGlobalHeader record → `final[pax_global_header] present=true type="other"; entries=3; deleted=[pax_global_header(regular/text)]`. Go reader.go: `if hdr.Typeflag == TypeXGlobalHeader { mergePAX(hdr, paxHdrs); return &Header{Name: hdr.Name, Typeflag: hdr.Typeflag, ...}, nil }`. Code: state.go:395-414 default branch → `Type: ArtifactTypeOther`.
proposed_fix: Add `case tar.TypeXGlobalHeader:` that drains and continues before preparePath/put, and move the entryCount++ (state.go:238) or decrement it so metadata records do not consume MAX_LAYER_ENTRIES/MAX_IMAGE_ARTIFACTS. The proposed `tar.TypeXHeader` case is dead code: reader.go:116 never surfaces TypeXHeader to callers.
verifier_note: Probe: lower layer regular file `pax_global_header`, upper layer a tar.TypeXGlobalHeader record -> result had FinalFiles=[app/x] only and DeletedArtifacts=[pax_global_header type=regular by=sha256:u]; the real file was displaced by a ghost 'other' artifact. reader.go:106-113 returns global headers as entries with the raw Name; state.go:395-414 materializes them. Rare in real layers (BuildKit/containerd writers never emit them) but real.

title: Findings budget already exhausted on entry yields a misleading "all selected manifests failed" error and the tag sweep keeps fetching manifests for every remaining target
description: jobs.scanTarget carries findingsRetained/rawBytesRetained into Scan as ExistingFindings/ExistingRawBytes. When a previous target retained exactly MaxFindings (no diagnostic is raised at exact equality), the next Scan hits `budget.exhausted()` before the first target, breaks, and because CompletedManifestCount==0 returns allSelectedManifestsFailedError with zero PlatformResults. In jobs the error is neither a limits error nor mustPreserveScanError, so the target is recorded as *failed* with that text and the loop continues to the next tag, repeating root manifest + config fetches for up to MAX_REPOSITORY_TARGETS tags, none of which can produce findings. The `max_findings_exceeded` diagnostic only short-circuits the sweep on the success path (jobs/scan.go:451).
evidence: Probe Scan{MaxFindings:5, ExistingFindings:5} against a valid single manifest: `err=all selected manifests failed status=failed manifests=1 completed=0 failed=0 platformResults=0 diagnostics=[{Code:max_findings_exceeded ... Limit:5 Observed:5}]`. Code: scan.go:231-235 `if budget.exhausted() { budget.markExceeded(...); result.Diagnostics = append(...); break }`; scan.go:313-315 `if result.CompletedManifestCount == 0 { return result, allSelectedManifestsFailedError(result.PlatformResults) }`; jobs/scan.go:398-403 records FailedTargetCount++ and continues.
proposed_fix: As proposed. Simplest: in Scan, if the loop exits via the budget break and len(result.PlatformResults)==0, set Status=partial and return (result, nil); in jobs, also check hasDiagnosticCode on the error path or test budget exhaustion before calling scanTarget so no manifest/config fetch happens for the remaining tags.
verifier_note: Probe Scan{MaxFindings:5, ExistingFindings:5} against a valid single manifest: err=`all selected manifests failed`, Status=failed, ManifestCount=1, CompletedManifestCount=0, PlatformResults=0, Diagnostics=[max_findings_exceeded Limit:5 Observed:5]. scan.go:231-235 breaks before the first target, scan.go:313-315 then reports all manifests failed with no platform results. In jobs/scan.go:398-404 this error is neither limits nor mustPreserveScanError, so the target is counted failed and the loop continues; the short-circuit at jobs/scan.go:451 only runs on the success path. The exact-boundary case (no diagnostic raised by the previous target because budget.scan only sets exceeded on the (N+1)th match, scan.go:590) is what makes this reachable.

title: Hardlink to a symlink/other artifact is counted as a file and as a binary exclusion
description: The TypeLink branch accepts any artifact in working.final as a target, copies its (nil) content, increments FilesSeen, and because target.Scannable is false and ContentClass is not Oversize, increments FilesExcludedBinary. The resulting ArtifactTypeHardlink with empty class is then listed in FinalFiles. Coverage counters therefore misreport a link to a symlink as an excluded binary file.
evidence: Probe layer `link -> /etc/passwd` (symlink) + `hl` hardlink to `link`: `coverage={... FilesSeen:1 FilesScanned:0 FilesExcludedBinary:1 ...} files=[hl(hardlink/)]`. Code: state.go:360-366 `if target.Scannable { FilesScanned++ } else if target.ContentClass == ContentClassOversize { FilesSkippedOversize++ } else { FilesExcludedBinary++ }`.
proposed_fix: As proposed; additionally treat a hardlink whose target is a known directory as ignored rather than unsafe so it does not flip coverage to partial.
verifier_note: Probe: symlink `link` + hardlink `hl`->link gave FinalFiles=[hl type=hardlink class="" scannable=false], Coverage FilesSeen:1 FilesExcludedBinary:1. A hardlink to a directory (`hld`->d) was counted EntriesSkippedUnsafe:1 because directories are not in working.final (state.go:335-338), which also forces partial status for an entry that is merely invalid. Code at state.go:340-366 matches the description.

title: No findings are produced from file paths alone, so unscannable sensitive artifacts (keystores, private-key files with binary content) are never reported
description: scanArtifactsWithBudget skips every artifact that is not Scannable or has empty content, and the detector pass over FilePath is used only to redact provenance (scanProvenance). A binary .p12/.jks/.pfx/.kdbx keystore, an `id_rsa` in OpenSSH binary-ish format, `.gnupg/secring.gpg`, or `.docker/config.json` whose content is oversize is therefore invisible even though its presence is itself a finding for most secret scanners.
evidence: scan.go:771 `if !artifact.Scannable || len(artifact.Content) == 0 { continue }`; scan.go:820-825 scanProvenance returns matches used only by NewDetailedNormalizerWithProvenance for redaction (findings.go:168-170 comment: 'Provenance-only matches never become findings').
proposed_fix: Add a `sensitive_file` detector family driven by path patterns (id_rsa|id_ed25519 without .pub, *.p12, *.pfx, *.jks, *.kdbx, .netrc, .pgpass, .git-credentials, .aws/credentials, .docker/config.json, secring.gpg) that emits a low/medium-confidence finding with SourceType file_final/file_deleted_layer even when content is binary/oversize, fingerprinted on path+layer digest. Make it opt-out via detector selection.
verifier_note: scan.go:771 skips non-scannable/empty artifacts; scanProvenance (scan.go:820-825) results are only used for redaction. Path-only findings are a legitimate 3.0 feature request.

title: Metadata scanning ignores manifest/index/layer annotations and unknown image-config fields (e.g. BuildKit buildinfo with build args)
description: scanMetadataWithBudget covers Env, Labels, history created_by/comment/author and the fixed ConfigFields list. It never scans manifest.Annotations, index annotations, per-layer descriptor annotations (buildpacks, Jib, ko, BuildKit write build metadata there), nor unmodeled top-level config fields such as `moby.buildkit.buildinfo.v1` (base64 JSON that historically embedded build args) or vendor extensions. Because ParseImageConfig unmarshals into a fixed struct, those bytes are discarded before detection.
evidence: scan.go:681-763 iterates only Env, Labels, History and manifest.ConfigFields; document.go:384-438 ConfigFields enumerates a fixed key list; document.go:159-166 ParseImageConfig discards unknown fields; manifest.Descriptor.Annotations (document.go:39) is never passed to detectors.
proposed_fix: Add SourceTypeAnnotation inputs for manifest, index and layer descriptor annotations (key=value, sorted), and a `config.raw` fallback that scans the raw config body once (deduped by fingerprint against structured findings) so unknown fields are covered. Decode `moby.buildkit.buildinfo.v1` base64 when present. Update OpenAPI/README source-type documentation accordingly.
verifier_note: scanMetadataWithBudget (scan.go:681-763) scans only Env, Labels, History and ConfigFields; ParseImageConfig (document.go:159-166) unmarshals into a fixed struct so unknown fields are discarded; Descriptor.Annotations (document.go:39) is never fed to detectors.

title: Every layer clones the entire final map, directory set and both path indexes for transactional rollback (O(total entries × layers) churn)
description: applyLayer builds `working` by deep-copying s.final, s.dirs, s.directoryChildren and s.artifactChildren before reading a single entry, and again copies the deleted slice. For an image near the defaults (250k entries, hundreds of layers) this is tens of millions of transient map insertions and gigabytes of garbage that are not counted against MAX_RETAINED_BYTES. The BenchmarkReplayDirectoryPrefixChurn shows the cost is already measured but not addressed.
evidence: state.go:203-211 `working := &State{ final: cloneArtifactMap(s.final), deleted: append([]Artifact(nil), s.deleted...), dirs: cloneDirectoryMap(s.dirs), directoryChildren: clonePathIndex(s.directoryChildren), artifactChildren: clonePathIndex(s.artifactChildren), ... }`; state.go:699-728 clone helpers iterate every entry.
proposed_fix: Replace whole-state cloning with an undo journal: mutate s in place and record inverse operations (put/delete/addDir/removeDir with prior values) in a per-layer slice; on failure replay the journal backwards and restore coverage snapshot. Keep the existing rollback tests (TestReplayRollsBackFailedLayer, TestReplayEnforcesAggregateLimitsTransactionally) as the safety net and extend the benchmark to many layers.
verifier_note: state.go:203-211 clones final/dirs/directoryChildren/artifactChildren per layer. cloneArtifactMap shares content bytes (state.go:702-706), so the churn is map metadata only (~25 MB per clone at 250k entries), which is less dramatic than 'gigabytes' for typical images but accumulates across hundreds of layers. An undo journal is a reasonable 3.0 refactor with the existing rollback tests as safety net.

title: Exceeding MAX_RAW_FINDING_BYTES stops all detection instead of continuing with raw retention disabled
description: When the raw budget is exhausted the budget sets rawExceeded, stopped() becomes true, scanArtifactsWithBudget breaks, and every remaining file and platform is left unscanned with coverage partial. Raw retention is an operator convenience (LAYERLEAK_PERSIST_RAW_SECRETS=1); losing detection coverage because of it is a poor trade. A 3.0 can change this documented semantic (README.md:241 'exceeding it makes coverage partial').
evidence: scan.go:602-607 `if b.rawBytes > b.maxRawBytes || rawSize > b.maxRawBytes-b.rawBytes { b.rawExceeded = true; ... retainRaw = false }`; scan.go:618-620 `if b.rawExceeded { break }`; scan.go:629-631 `stopped() ... (b.exceeded || b.rawExceeded)`; scan.go:768 `if budget != nil && (budget.stopped() || ...) { break }`.
proposed_fix: Continue detection after rawExceeded with retainRaw forced false, keep coverage complete for detection, and surface a `raw_retention_truncated` diagnostic plus a `raw_bytes_retained`/`raw_findings_truncated` count; update README.md:241, web docs and the OpenAPI diagnostic enumeration; note the semantic change in the 3.0.0 CHANGELOG.
verifier_note: scan.go:602-607 sets rawExceeded, :618-620 breaks after the current finding, :629-631 stopped() then short-circuits every later scan() call and scanArtifactsWithBudget (:768). Detection coverage is indeed sacrificed for a retention convenience; README:241 documents the current semantics so changing it belongs in the 3.0 CHANGELOG.

title: golangci-lint reports six issues in the engine packages (unchecked Close, ineffectual assignment, dead TypeRegA branch, SA4003) and CI runs only go vet
description: With golangci-lint v2.5.0 defaults: state.go:960 gzipReader.Close error ignored; state.go:822 `contentClass := ContentClassText` is dead (reassigned on every path); state.go:367 and state_test.go:942 reference tar.TypeRegA, which archive/tar rewrites to TypeReg/TypeDir before returning headers (reader.go:145), so the case is unreachable; state_test.go:1031 encoder.Close unchecked; limits.go:80 `limit >= math.MaxInt64` should be `==`. verify.yml only runs `go vet` and tests, so none of this is caught.

title: Resource-bound documentation misdescribes MAX_IMAGE_ARTIFACTS, omits that oversize files are skipped, and the web docs list only a subset of 0-disable variables
description: README.md:235 calls LAYERLEAK_MAX_IMAGE_ARTIFACTS an 'Aggregate layer artifact count' but Replay enforces it as MaxTotalEntries over every tar entry including directories, symlinks, whiteouts and device nodes. README.md:229 describes MAX_FILE_BYTES as 'Maximum decompressed bytes buffered for one file' without stating that larger files are not scanned and force partial status via files_skipped_oversize. web/docs/index.html:229-234 says only seven MAX_* settings accept 0 to disable, while config.go:137-165 also accepts 0 for MAX_IMAGE_LAYERS, MAX_IMAGE_MANIFESTS, MAX_IMAGE_LAYER_BYTES, MAX_IMAGE_ARTIFACTS, MAX_RETAINED_BYTES and MAX_RAW_FINDING_BYTES.
evidence: state.go:242-244 `if options.MaxTotalEntries > 0 && s.entries+entryCount > options.MaxTotalEntries { return limits.NewExceeded(limits.Kind("image_entries"), ...)` where entryCount++ runs for every header (state.go:238). README.md:229 `Maximum decompressed bytes buffered for one file; must be positive.`; web/docs/index.html:230-234 `(MAX_LAYER_BYTES, MAX_LAYER_ENTRIES, MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES, MAX_CONFIG_BYTES, MAX_TAG_RESPONSE_BYTES, MAX_REPOSITORY_TAGS, MAX_REPOSITORY_TARGETS) accept 0`; config.go:149-165 nonNegative*FromEnv for the others.
proposed_fix: As proposed, plus add LAYERLEAK_MAX_FINDINGS_PER_SCAN to the 0-disable list in web/docs/index.html.
verifier_note: README.md:235 says 'Aggregate layer artifact count' while state.go:238-243 charges MaxTotalEntries for every tar header; README.md:229 omits that oversize files are unscanned; web/docs/index.html:229-234 lists seven 0-disable variables while config.go:149-165,197,201 accept 0 for MAX_IMAGE_LAYERS, MAX_IMAGE_MANIFESTS, MAX_IMAGE_LAYER_BYTES, MAX_IMAGE_ARTIFACTS, MAX_RETAINED_BYTES, MAX_RAW_FINDING_BYTES and also MAX_FINDINGS_PER_SCAN (which the auditor's list omits; scanner treats maxFindings<=0 as unlimited at scan.go:590/626).

title: Scanner status-classification paths lack tests: foreign-layer platforms, budget carryover at the boundary, mid-layer cancellation, repeated digests
description: scan_test.go exercises multi-arch success, config limits, layer limits, deadlines and the intra-scan max-findings boundary, but not the classification paths that produce wrong or misleading outcomes: a windows/foreign-layer manifest inside an index (LAY-01), ExistingFindings == MaxFindings / ExistingRawBytes >= MaxRawFindingBytes on entry (LAY-07), a context cancelled while a layer is streaming (expect scan_canceled diagnostic, completed layers' findings preserved, no partial state committed), a manifest listing the same layer digest twice, a layer whose Content-Length mismatches the descriptor, and an index whose second platform fails with a non-integrity error (expect partial, err nil).
evidence: Test names in scan_test.go: TestScanMultiArchImage, TestScanArtifactsSkipsNonTextArtifacts, TestScanArtifactsClassifiesExampleTestDirectories, TestScanReturnsUnderlyingManifestFailureWhenAllSelectedManifestsFail, TestScanReturnsPartialResultWhenConfigLimitExceeded*, TestScanPreservesMetadataFindingsWhenLayerLimitsExceeded, TestScanPreserves*Deadline*, TestScanMaxFindingsStopsBeforeNextPlatformAtExactBoundary, TestDetectionBudget*, TestScanMetadataKeepsCurrentAndLegacyConfigProvenanceDistinct — none cover the listed paths; probes for the first two reproduced defects.
proposed_fix: Add the roundTripFunc-based fixtures from the probes: (a) index with linux + windows(foreign layers) asserting linux completes, windows is reported as unsupported (not descriptor_media_type_mismatch), err is nil or an accepted-partial error; (b) Scan with ExistingFindings==MaxFindings asserting Status partial and a max_findings_exceeded diagnostic without 'all selected manifests failed'; (c) a transport that cancels ctx after the first layer body is half-served, asserting scan_canceled and that findings from the completed layer exist; (d) a manifest with a repeated layer digest asserting deterministic findings and two OpenBlob calls.
verifier_note: Test inventory of scan_test.go matches the auditor's list (grep of `^func `); none exercise foreign-layer platforms, ExistingFindings==MaxFindings on entry, mid-layer cancellation, or repeated digests. My probes for the first two reproduced LAY-01 and LAY-07.

title: Layer decompression trusts the advertised media type instead of sniffing the blob's magic bytes
description: decompressLayer selects gzip/zstd/none purely from manifest.LayerCompression(mediaType). A blob whose content does not match its declared compression (mislabelled by a build tool or proxy, or an uncompressed `.tar` served under a `+gzip` type) fails with `open gzip layer: gzip: invalid header` or an opaque tar error and no diagnostic code, even though the digest verified. Sniffing the first bytes (1f 8b for gzip, 28 b5 2f fd for zstd, ustar at offset 257 for plain tar) would allow either tolerant decoding or a precise `layer_compression_mismatch` diagnostic.
evidence: state.go:950-981 `switch manifest.LayerCompression(mediaType) { case "": return reader ... case "gzip": gzipReader, err := gzip.NewReader(reader) ... case "zstd": ...`; scan.go:1207 maps such errors to the generic `manifest_failed` code.
proposed_fix: Peek the first 4 bytes (bufio.Reader) before choosing a decoder; if the magic disagrees with the media type, either decode by magic and emit a `layer_compression_mismatch` diagnostic (recommended for a scanner) or fail with that specific code. Add fixtures for gzip-labelled plain tar and zstd-labelled gzip.
verifier_note: decompressLayer (state.go:950-981) selects the decoder solely from manifest.LayerCompression; mislabeled blobs surface as `open gzip layer: gzip: invalid header` and are coded manifest_failed by diagnosticForError (scan.go:1207). Reasonable improvement; medium confidence on how often mislabeling occurs in practice is fair.

title: Budget diagnostics are duplicated in Result.Diagnostics when a non-final platform exhausts MaxFindings or MaxRawFindingBytes
description: When platform N trips the findings or raw budget, scanManifestWithBudget appends budget.diagnostic() to platformResult.Diagnostics (scan.go:459-461), which Scan merges into result.Diagnostics (scan.go:296). On the next loop iteration the top-of-loop checks (scan.go:226-235) append budget.diagnostic() again, so the public result carries two byte-identical `max_findings_exceeded` (or `max_raw_finding_bytes_exceeded`) entries. Consumers that count diagnostics or render them (CLI summary, API, web) show the condition twice.
evidence: Probe: two-platform index, MaxFindings=2, layer with three tokens -> `result diag: {Code:max_findings_exceeded ... Limit:2 Observed:3}` printed twice while the single completed platform had diags=1. Code: scan.go:228 and :234 `result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, budget.diagnostic())` after scan.go:296 already appended `platformResult.Diagnostics...` containing the same scan-scoped diagnostic.
proposed_fix: Use appendDiagnostic (scan.go:1211) instead of append for the two top-of-loop budget diagnostics, or skip them when result.Diagnostics already contains a diagnostic with the same Code/Subject. Add an assertion to the LAY-07/LAY-20 budget tests that each budget code appears once in result.Diagnostics.

title: --platform is silently ignored when the reference resolves to a single image manifest rather than an index
description: Scan only consults request.Platform in the DocumentKindIndex branch (scan.go:199). For a DocumentKindManifest root (any digest reference to a platform manifest, or a single-platform tag) the selector is never compared with the image config's os/architecture/variant that is already parsed at scan.go:369, so `layerleak scan repo@sha256:<amd64 manifest> --platform linux/arm64` scans amd64 and reports success for a platform the user did not ask for. README.md:128 documents the flag only as 'Restrict a multi-platform image', so this is arguably by design, but a 3.0 is the moment to make the selector either enforced (fail with the same 'platform ... not found' error the index path uses, document.go:250) or clearly documented as index-only.
evidence: scan.go:188-197: `case manifest.DocumentKindManifest: targets = append(targets, target{descriptor: manifest.Descriptor{MediaType: document.Manifest.MediaType, Digest: requestedDigest, ...}, manifest: &document.Manifest})` with no reference to request.Platform; the only use is scan.go:199 `manifest.SelectDescriptors(document.Index, request.Platform)`. cli/scan.go:55-57 validates selector syntax only.
proposed_fix: In scanManifestWithBudget, when request.Platform is non-empty and the root was a single manifest, parse the selector and require configPlatform.Matches(selected) (scan.go:369-372), returning fmt.Errorf("platform %s not found in manifest", ...) otherwise; add a scanner test for a mismatched selector against a single-manifest root and update README.md:128 to describe the behavior.

title: Centralise the release major so the next module-path move is a one-line change
description: The v1 major is currently spelled in at least 12 independent places (workflow regexes, tag glob, preflight VERSION, test fixtures, RELEASING.md, verify.yml identity check, install commands). The same scattered edit will recur at /v4.
evidence: See MIG-03..MIG-10 evidence; container-release.yml env block (lines 33-37) has `IMAGE_NAME`, `GRYPE_VERSION`, `BUILDX_VERSION`, `BUILDKIT_IMAGE` but no module path or major constant.
proposed_fix: Add `MODULE_PATH: github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3` and `RELEASE_MAJOR: 3` to the workflow env; build the regexes as `^v${RELEASE_MAJOR}\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(-rc\.[1-9][0-9]*)?$`, use `git tag --list "v${RELEASE_MAJOR}.*"`, `go install "${MODULE_PATH}@${RELEASE_VERSION}"`, and assert `go.mod` module == MODULE_PATH. In release-preflight.py derive VERSION from a `RELEASE_MAJOR` constant and add a test that the constant matches go.mod's suffix. verify.yml can derive the expected module from go.mod's declared path and just assert it ends in `/v3`.

Dockerfile:20-23 builds only cmd/api, cmd/migrate, cmd/purge, cmd/healthcheck. README.md:85: 'The `cmd/*` packages are source build targets for development, not separately versioned install paths.'

CONTRIBUTING.md:25 '`go run ./cmd/scanner` remains a development entrypoint'; README.md:85 'The `cmd/*` packages are source build targets for development'. xs, IN 3.0.0, no dissent.

title: CLI `--format json` and the local scan record replace every real error message with "scan step failed", so the operator running the scan cannot see why it failed
description: `RedactedResult` was designed as the scan-history/API policy (hide internal error text from remote API consumers). The CLI applies the same function to stdout JSON and to the local record, so a local user gets `"error": "scan step failed"` for every failed tag, target, platform and diagnostic, while the human summary shows the real message. Secret redaction (stripping raw values) and error-message sanitization are different concerns; only the first belongs in local output. This is the kind of behavior change a major should make deliberately.
evidence: internal/cli/scan.go:253 `encoder.Encode(scanservice.RedactedResult(result))`. internal/cli/results.go:298 `Result: scanservice.RedactedResult(outcome.Result)`. internal/scanservice/record.go:255-261 `RedactedResult` calls `sanitizeStoredResult`, whose `storedErrorMessage` (:295-300) returns the constant "scan step failed" for any non-empty error and `sanitizedDiagnostics` (:285-293) does the same for diagnostic messages. Contrast summary path: internal/cli/scan.go:436-441 `summaryItemStatus` prints `sanitizeProgressValue(message)` (real text). Test confirming the policy: internal/scanservice/record_test.go:72 expects `"scan step failed"` in stored records.
proposed_fix: As proposed (split `PublicResult` from `RedactedResult`), with one guard: error strings can embed registry URLs, redirect targets and header fragments, so route them through `sanitizeProgressValue` AND the finding-value redactor before they land in the record. Keep `RedactedResult` for storage/API unchanged so record_test.go:72 still holds.
verifier_note: Mechanism confirmed: scan.go:253 `encoder.Encode(scanservice.RedactedResult(result))`, results.go:298 `Result: scanservice.RedactedResult(outcome.Result)`, record.go:295-300 `storedErrorMessage` returns the constant "scan step failed" and :285-293 does the same for diagnostics; record_test.go:72 asserts the constant. But the title overstates the impact: the top-level scan error is still printed verbatim to stderr via scan.go:268 `exitError{code: 1, message: scanErr.Error()}` → root.go:24 `fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, sanitizeProgressValue(err.Error()))`, the progress renderer shows it (:175, :192), and `IncompleteError.Error()` (jobs/scan.go:65-79) includes the cause. What is actually lost in `--format json` and the record is per-tag, per-target and per-platform error text plus diagnostics. Still a legitimate 3.0.0 contract change (IN 3.0.0), but severity low, not medium.

title: Detector identifier cleanup: inconsistent naming and identifier-not-secret detectors at high confidence
description: Detector ids are surfaced in JSON, the DB `detectors` array and (eventually) SARIF rule ids, so renames are breaking and belong in 3.0.0. Inconsistencies: `digitalocean_pat` while every other PAT is spelled `*_personal_access_token`; `stripe_key` vs `*_api_key`; `jwt` and `pem_private_key` lack the provider/format convention. `twilio_account_sid` (an `AC…` account identifier, not a credential) and `sentry_dsn` (a client-side DSN Sentry documents as safe to ship) are reported at ConfidenceHigh, which under PRD-06 would fail CI at the strictest threshold. Three ids are registered twice (`docker_auth_blob`, `aws_secret_access_key`, `cloudflare_api_token`) — that is a legitimate multi-strategy design but should be documented as such once ids become public API.
evidence: internal/detectors/detectors.go:95 `newRegexDetector("digitalocean_pat", ...)` vs :142 `"airtable_personal_access_token"`, :151 `"netlify_personal_access_token"`; :78 `"stripe_key"`; :106 `newRegexDetector("twilio_account_sid", regexp.MustCompile(`\bAC[a-f0-9]{32}\b`), 0, ConfidenceHigh, nil)`; :121 `"sentry_dsn"` ConfidenceHigh; duplicate registrations at :67/:88 (docker_auth_blob), :80-81 (aws_secret_access_key), :150/:156 (cloudflare_api_token). Count via grep: 82 registrations, 73 distinct ids plus `keyword_entropy` (:385).
proposed_fix: Use the corrected line numbers above. Build `Catalog()` from the set of ids a detector can EMIT (add an `IDs() []string` method or have Scan return a documented id list), not from Name(); add the unit test over emitted ids. Rename table as proposed plus decide whether `aws_shared_credentials_*` / `git_credentials_password` sub-ids are the canonical rule ids.
verifier_note: Substance confirmed but the evidence is wrong in detail and must be corrected before anyone acts on it: in detectors.go `stripe_key` is :72 (not :78), `digitalocean_pat` :88 (not :95), `twilio_account_sid` :99 (not :106), `sentry_dsn` :119 (not :121), `airtable_personal_access_token` :126 (not :142), `netlify_personal_access_token` :135 (not :151); duplicate registrations are `docker_auth_blob` :62/:82, `aws_secret_access_key` :74/:75, `cloudflare_api_token` :132/:139. `Default()` contains 80 registrations (lines 59-147, three span multiple lines), not 82; distinct Name() ids are 74 in detectors.go plus `terraform_cloud_token`, `heroku_api_key`, `snyk_api_token` (structured.go:27,36,96) and `keyword_entropy` (:385) = 78. The proposal also misses a larger id inconsistency: two structured detectors emit Match.Detector ids that differ from their Name() — structured.go:142/154/170 `aws_shared_credentials_access_key_id|secret_access_key|session_token` under Name() `aws_shared_credentials` (:108), and :317 `git_credentials_password` under `git_credentials` (:283) — so a Catalog() built from Name() would not list ids that actually appear in output (see PRD-26). Keep IN 3.0.0 (renames are breaking) at low severity; the `twilio_account_sid` / `sentry_dsn` confidence downgrades are well-founded.

title: Custom YAML detector rules — OUT; `layerleak detectors list` catalog command — 3.1
description: Custom rule DSLs (gitleaks-style TOML/YAML) are a large, permanent surface: regex safety (ReDoS on adversarial image content), precedence against the built-in set, entropy/policy interplay, and a compatibility promise on the rule format. The project's stated posture is 'correctness, redaction, bounded resource use ... before adding convenience' (CONTRIBUTING.md:3-5). Verdict OUT for 3.x; revisit only as an import of a widely used format. A read-only catalog command (`layerleak detectors list [--format json]`) is cheap once `Catalog()` exists (PRD-07) and gives users the transparency they actually ask for. Verdict 3.1, effort s.
evidence: internal/detectors/detectors.go:56-160 `Default()` is a hard-coded slice of 82 detector registrations; `Set` exposes only `Len()` and `Scan()` (:162-171), no enumeration or description API. CONTRIBUTING.md:3-5 'Contributions should preserve correctness, redaction, bounded resource use, OCI integrity, and predictable operation before adding convenience.'
proposed_fix: Do not build a rule DSL. In 3.1 add `layerleak detectors list` backed by `detectors.Catalog()` (id, description, confidence, strategies, example redacted match) and generate the Pages 'detectors' table from it in verify.yml so docs cannot drift.
verifier_note: detectors.go:56-150 `Default()` is a hard-coded slice; `Set` exposes only `Len()` (:152) and `Scan()` (:156) — no enumeration. CONTRIBUTING.md:3-5 quoted correctly. Rule DSL OUT is the right call for a tool whose posture is bounded adversarial parsing. Catalog command 3.1 agreed, with the PRD-07/PRD-26 caveat that the catalog must be keyed on emitted ids.

title: `--log-format text|json` for the CLI — 3.1
description: The CLI always emits JSON slog lines to stderr, interleaved with the human progress renderer; on a terminal a `debug` run is hard to read. Value medium, effort xs, risk none. Verdict 3.1 (additive). Default stays `json` for CI log-safety; `auto` (text on TTY) is optional.

title: Prometheus /metrics — 3.2; OpenTelemetry tracing — OUT
description: A `/metrics` endpoint (scan count by status, duration histogram, concurrent-slot saturation, storage errors) is a small, standard operational add for the API image and fits the existing bounded-ops posture. Value medium, effort s, risk low → 3.2. OpenTelemetry tracing adds a heavy dependency tree to a scratch image whose dependency-review policy and license gates are deliberately tight, for a service with one synchronous handler; value low today → OUT.
evidence: internal/api/handler.go:206-224 registered routes are health/livez/readyz plus five API routes; no metrics endpoint. go.mod lists five direct dependencies (cobra, lib/pq, go-digest, klauspost/compress, distribution/reference, x/term) — no telemetry libraries. .github/workflows/test.yml:33-49 dependency-review with `fail-on-severity: high` and a deny-list.

verifier_note: handler.go:206-224 registers health/livez/readyz and five /api/v1 routes, no metrics; go.mod lists cobra, lib/pq, go-digest, klauspost/compress, distribution/reference, x/term; test.yml:33-49 dependency-review `fail-on-severity: high` with the GPL/LGPL/AGPL deny list. /metrics 3.2, OTel OUT agreed.

title: Async scan jobs/worker model, webhooks, scan scheduling, Helm chart — OUT of 3.0.0; async jobs only in 3.x if API demand appears
description: The API runs scans synchronously inside the request with a concurrency semaphore and a 30-minute timeout; `--all-tags` sweeps can exceed proxy idle timeouts. An async model (202 + job resource + polling) is the right long-term shape but requires a jobs table (migration 0005), a worker loop, cancellation and retention policy — an l-size subsystem the 2026-09-09 plan explicitly deferred ('adding a major ... service subsystem first would expand the compatibility and testing work'). Webhooks and scheduling presuppose async jobs; a Helm chart presupposes users running the API in Kubernetes, for which there is no evidence yet (docker-compose is the documented deployment). Verdict: async jobs 3.x conditional; webhooks, scheduling, Helm OUT.
evidence: internal/api/handler.go:320-336 `select { case h.scanSlots <- struct{}{}: ... default: 429 }` then `scanCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(request.Context(), h.options.ScanTimeout)` and a synchronous `h.scanner.ScanAndSave(...)`. README.md:252-253 `LAYERLEAK_API_SCAN_TIMEOUT 30m`, `LAYERLEAK_API_MAX_CONCURRENT_SCANS 1`. docs/plans/2026-09-09-release-readiness.md:18-21.
proposed_fix: Record the decision in docs/plans as 'deferred pending demand'. If async is later built: `POST /api/v1/scan-jobs` → 202 `{job_id}`, `GET /api/v1/scan-jobs/{id}`, one in-process worker consuming a `scan_jobs` table with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; keep `POST /api/v1/scans` synchronous for compatibility.
verifier_note: handler.go:320-327 `select { case h.scanSlots <- struct{}{}: ... default: 429 }`, :329-336 `context.WithTimeout(request.Context(), h.options.ScanTimeout)` then synchronous `h.scanner.ScanAndSave`; README.md:252-253 30m / 1 concurrent; plan :17-21 defers 'a major ... service subsystem'. OUT/conditional placement agreed.

title: Dockerfile sets LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR for an image that never writes findings files
description: The image contains only the API, migrate, purge and healthcheck binaries; none of them calls the CLI's `writeResultArtifacts`, so `ENV LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR=/tmp/layerleak/findings` is dead configuration that suggests the API writes result files to /tmp. Clean it up alongside PRD-03.

proposed_fix: Remove Dockerfile:40, docker-compose.yml:46 and the README API-table reference if any; keep .env.example:12 only if it is documented as CLI-only.
