title: Fuzz coverage exists only for the reference parser and the verifying reader; add fuzz targets for the tar replay, detector set, bearer challenge and image-config parsers
description: For a tool whose threat model is adversarial image content, the parsers that consume untrusted bytes are the tar/whiteout replay, the image config JSON, the `Www-Authenticate` challenge parser and the detector regex set (ReDoS/allocation). Only two fuzz functions and two benchmarks exist. This is not release-blocking, but a 3.0.0 that advertises 'bounded and fail closed' should have fuzz targets running in CI (short budget) for those entry points. Effort s–m.
evidence: `grep -rn 'func Fuzz|func Benchmark' --include=*_test.go .` → internal/manifest/integrity_test.go:122 `FuzzVerifyingReader`, internal/manifest/reference_test.go:217 `FuzzParseReference`, internal/layers/state_test.go:693 `BenchmarkReplayDirectoryPrefixChurn`, internal/findings/findings_test.go:469 `BenchmarkDetailedNormalizerManyMatches`. Untrusted-input entry points without fuzz: internal/layers/state.go:120 `Replay`, internal/registry/client.go:366 `parseBearerChallenge`, internal/detectors/detectors.go:164 `Set.Scan`, image config decoding in internal/scanner/scan.go:931 `readConfigBody`.
proposed_fix: Add `FuzzReplay` (random tar streams with whiteouts/hardlinks/symlinks under tight limits, asserting no panic and bounds respected), `FuzzParseBearerChallenge`, `FuzzDetectorSetScan` (assert wall-time per input below a threshold to catch ReDoS), `FuzzImageConfig`; run each for 30s in verify.yml on pull requests and nightly for longer. Add `BenchmarkDefaultSetScanCorpus` over internal/scanner/testdata to make detector additions measurable (plan follow-up #3).
verifier_note: `grep -rn 'func Fuzz|func Benchmark' --include=*_test.go .` → exactly FuzzVerifyingReader (manifest/integrity_test.go:122), FuzzParseReference (manifest/reference_test.go:217), BenchmarkReplayDirectoryPrefixChurn (layers/state_test.go:693), BenchmarkDetailedNormalizerManyMatches (findings/findings_test.go:469). Untrusted-input entry points `Replay` (state.go:120), `parseBearerChallenge` (client.go:591, not :366 as quoted), `Set.Scan` (detectors.go:156) and `readConfigBody` (scanner/scan.go:931) have no fuzz targets. 3.x/not blocking agreed.

title: Publish a CLI container image alongside the API image — 3.1
description: The scratch image contains only the API and its admin binaries, so there is no supported way to run the scanner in container-only CI (GitLab, Jenkins agents, Tekton) without a Go toolchain. A second build target that copies the module-root binary into a scratch image (same base, same non-root UID, same provenance/signing pipeline) is small and removes the dead `LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR` ambiguity PRD-20 identifies by giving the CLI its own image where that variable is meaningful.
evidence: Dockerfile:20-23 builds `./cmd/api`, `./cmd/migrate`, `./cmd/purge`, `./cmd/healthcheck` only; Dockerfile:48 `ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/layerleak-api"]`; README.md:82-84 'The supported distribution paths are the module root above for the CLI and `ghcr.io/brumbelow/layerleak:<published-version>` for the API'.
proposed_fix: 3.1: add a `cli` stage/target (`--target cli`) producing `ghcr.io/brumbelow/layerleak-cli:<version>` with `ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/layerleak"]`, `WORKDIR /work`, `ENV LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR=/work/findings`, built and signed by the same release job; record both digests in release-manifest.json.

title: Detector Name() and emitted detector ids diverge for the structured AWS and git credential detectors — settle the id convention in 3.0.0
description: PRD-07 and PRD-14 assume detector ids equal `Detector.Name()`. Two detectors emit sub-ids that never appear as a Name(), so a Name()-based catalog, SARIF rule list or rename table would omit ids that actually show up in `finding.detector_name`, the DB `detectors` array and the Pages docs. Because ids are becoming public API in 3.0.0 (SARIF rules, catalog), this must be decided now.
evidence: internal/detectors/structured.go:108 `return "aws_shared_credentials"` but matches are emitted at :142 `Detector: "aws_shared_credentials_access_key_id"`, :154 `"aws_shared_credentials_secret_access_key"`, :170 `"aws_shared_credentials_session_token"`; :283 `return "git_credentials"` but :317 `Detector: "git_credentials_password"`. `Detector` interface (detectors.go:41-44) exposes only `Name()` and `Scan()`.
proposed_fix: Extend the interface with `IDs() []string` (default `[]string{Name()}`), make `Set.Catalog()` iterate emitted ids, and add a test that every id produced by the fixture corpus under internal/scanner/testdata is present in the catalog. Document the sub-ids in the PRD-07 rename table as intentional.

title: ListTags silently stops paginating on any Link header that is not exactly `<url>; rel="next"`, returning a truncated tag list as success
description: nextLinkURL splits the raw header on `;` and requires parts[1] to EqualFold `rel="next"`. A header with several relations (`<a>; rel="next", <b>; rel="prev"`), an unquoted `rel=next` (allowed by RFC 8288), or parameters in a different order (`<a>; type="application/json"; rel="next"`) is treated as 'no next page' and ListTags returns nil error. Repository sweeps then report fewer tags than exist with a completed status, violating README's guarantee that incomplete coverage is never reported as a clean scan.
evidence: Probe on a copy: `LINK "</v2/library/app/tags/list?n=2&last=2.0>; rel=\"next\", </v2/library/app/tags/list?n=2>; rel=\"prev\"" -> next="" ok=false err=<nil>`; `LINK "...; rel=next" -> ok=false`; `LINK "...; type=\"application/json\"; rel=\"next\"" -> ok=false`; end-to-end `LISTTAGS tags=["1.0" "2.0"] err=<nil>` although page 2 held "3.0". Code client.go:765-771: `parts := strings.Split(value, ";") ... if len(parts) > 1 && !strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(parts[1]), `rel="next"`) { return "", false, nil }`.
proposed_fix: Fix as proposed (RFC 8288 tokenizer over Header.Values("Link"), select rel containing `next`, return an error for an unparseable Link so jobs marks the sweep partial). Table tests for the four shapes plus a prev-only header.
verifier_note: Code behaviour confirmed by probe: `<a>; rel="next", <b>; rel="prev"` -> ok=false, `rel=next` -> ok=false, `type=...; rel="next"` -> ok=false, all with nil error, and only the first Link header is read (Header.Get at client.go:297). However the OCI distribution spec and distribution/distribution emit exactly `<url>; rel="next"`, and the auditor's own open question admits no registry was shown to emit another shape; the repro is synthetic. The silent-truncation failure mode and the fix are valid, but with no evidence of a real registry triggering it this is not release blocking. release_blocking should be false.

title: Retries are immediate with no backoff and ignore Retry-After (three back-to-back requests against a 429)
description: executeRequest loops over requestAttempts with no sleep between attempts; isRetryableStatus retries 408/429/5xx immediately. Against Docker Hub rate limiting (429 with Retry-After) this burns the attempt budget within milliseconds and counts extra pulls against the limit; against a struggling registry it adds load at the worst time. 501/505 are also retried although they are never transient.
evidence: Probe with a transport always answering 429 + `Retry-After: 30` and RequestAttempts=3: `RETRY requests=3 err=registry request failed: status=429 Too Many Requests` (all three requests issued instantly). client.go:439-443: `if attempt+1 < c.requestAttempts && isRetryableStatus(response.StatusCode) { response.Body.Close(); lastErr = ...; continue }`; client.go:691-698 `default: return statusCode >= 500 && statusCode <= 599`.
proposed_fix: Add exponential backoff with jitter (e.g. 250ms base, doubling, capped) that respects Retry-After (seconds or HTTP-date, capped to a sane maximum) and aborts when ctx is done; exclude 501/505 from retryable statuses; surface the final 429 as a typed error so jobs/API can report `rate_limited`. Add tests asserting a delay occurs between attempts and that Retry-After is honoured/capped.
verifier_note: Confirmed: probe with RequestAttempts=3 against a 429+Retry-After shows 3 requests in 21.9µs; isRetryableStatus(501)=true, (505)=true. But the default RequestAttempts is 2 (client.go:117-120, README), so production impact is a single immediate retry; the cost is bounded. Worth fixing before 3.0.0 but not medium.

title: Redirect target URLs, including pre-signed CDN query credentials, are echoed verbatim into error messages that reach CLI stderr and CI logs
description: doRequest wraps *url.Error from http.Client.Do with `perform registry request: %w`; url.Error.Error() embeds the final (post-redirect) URL. Blob fetches on Docker Hub, GHCR, Quay and ECR redirect to S3/CloudFront/Azure pre-signed URLs whose query string (X-Amz-Credential, X-Amz-Signature, sig=...) is a short-lived bearer credential. A connect/TLS failure after the redirect prints that URL. Persisted records and API responses are sanitised (record.go:295-300 storedErrorMessage, handler.go:929-950 sanitizeResultErrors), but the CLI prints err.Error() to stderr (cli/root.go:24-28 via sanitizeProgressValue, which only strips control characters) and progress 'Error' messages, so CI logs capture it; the repository's own tests (TestURLValidationErrorsDoNotEchoUntrustedValues) show the intent to avoid echoing untrusted URLs.
evidence: Probe: `REDIRECT-ERR perform registry request: Get "https://cdn.test/blobs/sha256:aaaa...?X-Amz-Credential=AKIA<redacted>&X-Amz-Signature=SIGNATURE-MARKER": connection reset by peer`. client.go:358-361: `response, err := c.executeRequest(ctx, method, targetURL, accept, ""); if err != nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf("perform registry request: %w", err) }` (same pattern at 388, 401, 490).
proposed_fix: In executeRequest/doHTTP unwrap *url.Error and re-wrap as a typed registry error whose message contains only scheme://host[:port]/path (drop query) or just the operation and host, keeping the underlying error via Unwrap for errors.Is checks. Add a test asserting that a redirect target's query string never appears in err.Error().
verifier_note: Probe: OpenBlob following a 302 to `https://cdn.test/blobs/x?X-Amz-Credential=AKIA<redacted>&X-Amz-Signature=SIGNATURE-MARKER` whose dial fails returns `perform registry request: Get "https://cdn.test/blobs/x?X-Amz-Credential=...&X-Amz-Signature=SIGNATURE-MARKER": connection reset by peer`. The live REG-01 run shows the CLI printing the full url.Error text both as a progress `Error:` line and on stderr; cli/progress.go:393-398 sanitizeProgressValue only collapses whitespace/control characters, so query strings survive.

title: WWW-Authenticate parsing splits on commas inside quoted values and reads only the first header
description: parseBearerChallenge does `strings.Split(value, ",")` before stripping quotes, so `scope="repository:app:pull,push"` becomes `repository:app:pull` and a realm such as `https://auth.test/token?x=1,2` is truncated to `?x=1`. Quoted-string escapes (`\"`) are not handled. doRequest uses `response.Header.Get("Www-Authenticate")`, so a registry that lists `Basic` first and `Bearer` second (or sends two challenges) is rejected as `unsupported registry auth challenge`. Impact today is mostly narrowed scopes and spurious failures against non-mainstream registries, but the parser is on the untrusted-input boundary.
evidence: Probe: `CHALLENGE "Bearer realm=\"https://auth.test/token\",service=\"registry.test\",scope=\"repository:library/app:pull,push\"" -> {Realm:https://auth.test/token Service:registry.test Scope:repository:library/app:pull}`; `CHALLENGE "Bearer realm=\"https://auth.test/token?x=1,2\"" -> {Realm:https://auth.test/token?x=1 ...}`. client.go:601 `pieces := strings.Split(value, ",")`; client.go:613 `rawValue = strings.TrimSpace(strings.Trim(rawValue, `"`))`; client.go:366 `parseBearerChallenge(response.Header.Get("Www-Authenticate"))`.
proposed_fix: Implement an RFC 7235 auth-param tokenizer (token / quoted-string with backslash escapes, comma-separated, whitespace tolerant) and iterate `response.Header.Values("Www-Authenticate")`, selecting the first Bearer challenge; reject realms that are not absolute https (already done downstream) and ignore unknown params such as error/error_description. Add table tests covering quoted commas, escaped quotes, multiple challenges, lowercase scheme, and missing realm.
verifier_note: Probe: `scope="repository:library/app:pull,push"` parses to Scope `repository:library/app:pull`; `realm="https://auth.test/token?x=1,2"` parses to `https://auth.test/token?x=1`; with headers `Basic ...` then `Bearer ...`, Header.Get returns the Basic one and parseBearerChallenge errors `unsupported registry auth challenge`. client.go:601 and 366 as cited.

title: registry-1.docker.io/<name> and mixed-case DOCKER.IO/<name> lose the library/ prefix, producing a canonical docker.io/<name> that does not exist
description: ParseReference feeds the raw string to distributionreference.ParseNormalizedNamed, which only adds `library/` when the domain is exactly `docker.io`/`index.docker.io`. layerleak then maps `registry-1.docker.io` and any-case `docker.io` to DockerHubRegistry in normalizeRegistry, so the result is Registry=docker.io, Repository=busybox. The scan requests /v2/busybox/manifests/... on Docker Hub (which only knows library/busybox) and the CanonicalString/persisted repository is `docker.io/busybox`, inconsistent with `docker.io/busybox` parsed directly (library/busybox).
evidence: Probe: `REF "registry-1.docker.io/busybox" -> registry="docker.io" repository="busybox"`; `REF "DOCKER.IO/busybox" -> registry="docker.io" repository="busybox"`; versus `REF "docker.io/busybox" -> repository="library/busybox"`. reference.go:43 `named, err := distributionreference.ParseNormalizedNamed(value)`; reference.go:171-178 normalizeRegistry maps `"docker.io", "index.docker.io", "registry-1.docker.io"` to DockerHubRegistry.
proposed_fix: Before calling ParseNormalizedNamed, lowercase the domain component and rewrite registry-1.docker.io/index.docker.io to docker.io (or, after parsing, when normalizeRegistry yields docker.io and the path has no '/', prepend `library/`). Add the three inputs above to TestParseReference.
verifier_note: Probe: `registry-1.docker.io/busybox` -> repository `busybox`, canonical `docker.io/busybox`; `DOCKER.IO/busybox` -> `busybox`; whereas `docker.io/busybox` and `index.docker.io/busybox` -> `library/busybox`. distribution/reference only applies the library/ rule when the domain is exactly docker.io/index.docker.io; layerleak's normalizeRegistry (reference.go:171-178) then collapses the alias after the fact. The existing test at reference_test.go:43 only covers `registry-1.docker.io/library/busybox` (explicit library/), so the gap is untested.

title: Root manifest/index is JSON-parsed before its digest is verified, contradicting SECURITY.md's 'verified before parsing or scanning' claim
description: verifyRootDocument calls manifest.ParseDocument (two json.Unmarshal passes) and ValidateDocument first and only reaches VerifyDescriptorBytes at line 1050. For `image@sha256:...` references the expected digest is known up front, and for tag references the registry's Docker-Content-Digest is available before parsing, yet untrusted bytes are decoded first. Child manifests (scan.go:496-499) and config blobs (982 then 365) do verify before parsing, so the root document is the one inconsistency. Risk is bounded (body already limited by MaxManifestBytes) but the published security statement is currently false for this path.
evidence: scan.go:1004 `document, err := manifest.ParseDocument(response.MediaType, response.Body)` ... scan.go:1050 `if err := manifest.VerifyDescriptorBytes(rootDescriptor, response.Body, response.MediaType, false)`. SECURITY.md:64-65: `OCI content is verified against advertised sha256 or sha512 digests before parsing or scanning`.
proposed_fix: Reorder as proposed but note VerifyDescriptorBytes also checks media type; at the pre-parse stage build the descriptor with MediaType = response.MediaType (or call ValidateDigest + size + DigestBytes directly) and perform the VerifyMediaType(document mediaType vs response.MediaType) check after parsing. Test: digest reference + invalid JSON body must yield descriptor_digest_mismatch, not invalid_manifest_document.
verifier_note: scan.go:1004 ParseDocument, 1014 ValidateDocument, 1022 VerifyMediaType all precede VerifyDescriptorBytes at 1050; child manifests (496-499) and config blobs (982 before 365) verify first, so the root is the inconsistency. SECURITY.md:64-65 states verification happens 'before parsing or scanning'. For tag references the only pre-parse digest is the untrusted Docker-Content-Digest header, so the guarantee is only meaningful for digest references, but the reorder is xs and makes the statement true; keeping release_blocking=true is consistent with rule 4 (doc false at release time) given the trivial fix or the alternative of amending SECURITY.md.

title: README allowlist paragraph omits two behaviours: port-less entries never match explicit-port URLs, and allowlisting is what unlocks plain http for that host
description: README says entries accept 'an exact DNS hostname or IPv4 address, optionally with a port'. In code the match key is the URL's literal host plus its explicit port only (canonicalURLHost), so `localhost` does not cover `localhost:5000/foo` and `registry.internal:443` does not cover `https://registry.internal/`; users following the README will hit `non-public registry address 127.0.0.1 is not allowed`. Separately, NewClient enables `http://` endpoints and redirects only for allowlisted hosts (allowConfiguredHTTP, validateOutboundURL) and otherwise fails with `http registry endpoint ... must be explicitly allowlisted`; neither README (219-223, 216-217) nor web/docs/index.html:249-252 nor .env.example:35-41 mention that TLS is otherwise mandatory or that an allowlist entry also permits http. Accepted-syntax claims (schemes/paths/credentials/wildcards/unbracketed IPv6 rejected) match config.normalizeAllowedHost and were verified.
evidence: Probe: `ALLOWLIST localhost vs https://localhost:5000 -> non-public registry address 127.0.0.1 is not allowed`; `ALLOWLIST localhost:443 vs https://localhost -> non-public registry address 127.0.0.1 is not allowed`. client.go:1005-1014 canonicalURLHost: `if value.Port() == "" { return host }; return net.JoinHostPort(host, value.Port())`; client.go:106 `allowConfiguredHTTP := len(registryAllowlist) > 0 || len(authAllowlist) > 0`; client.go:895-897 `if parsed.Scheme == "http" && !c.hostAllowed(parsed, kind) { return fmt.Errorf("http is allowed only for an explicitly allowlisted private %s host", kind) }`. README.md:219-223 quoted text: 'Entries accept an exact DNS hostname or IPv4 address, optionally with a port, or bracketed IPv6 with a port.'
proposed_fix: Either normalise ports in canonicalURLHost/normalizeHostAllowlist (treat missing port as 443 for https/80 for http so `localhost:443` and `localhost` are equivalent) and document 'host:port must match the port the scanner connects to', or keep exact semantics and add a sentence: 'An entry without a port matches only URLs without an explicit port; localhost:5000 must be listed as localhost:5000.' Add: 'Allowlisted hosts may also be reached over plain http (LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_BASE_URL=http://...); all other destinations require TLS 1.2+ with a verifiable certificate.' Mirror in web/docs/index.html and .env.example.
verifier_note: canonicalURLHost (client.go:1005-1014) keys on literal host plus explicit port only, so `localhost` never matches `https://localhost:5000` and `host:443` never matches `https://host/`; validateOutboundURL 895-897 only permits http for allowlisted hosts. README:219-223 and .env.example:35-37 describe accepted syntax but neither mentions port-matching semantics or that allowlisting unlocks plain http. web/docs/index.html:249-253 likewise. The auditor's probe outputs are consistent with the code; I did not need to re-run them.

title: ValidateImageIndex rejects legal index entries (nested indexes, non-image artifact manifests), failing the whole scan
description: Every entry of index.manifests must satisfy IsManifestMediaType, so an OCI 1.1 index that contains a nested `application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json` child, a Docker manifest list child, or an artifact descriptor (Helm, SBOM referrers pushed into the index) fails validation as invalid_manifest_document/descriptor_media_type_mismatch before any platform is scanned. SelectDescriptors already knows how to skip non-scannable entries (IsScannableManifestDescriptor), so validation is stricter than selection.
evidence: Probe: `INDEX+nested-index ValidateImageIndex err=descriptor_media_type_mismatch for "manifest[1]": expected "supported OCI media type", got "application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json"`; `INDEX+helm-artifact ... got "application/vnd.cncf.helm.config.v1+json"`; `INDEX+docker-list ... got "application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json"`. integrity.go:154-156: `for index, descriptor := range value.Manifests { if err := validateDescriptor(descriptor, IsManifestMediaType, ...)`.
proposed_fix: In ValidateImageIndex validate digest/size/platform syntax for every entry but require a supported media type only for entries that IsScannableManifestDescriptor would select; optionally descend one level into nested indexes (bounded) or record a `manifest_skipped_unsupported_media_type` diagnostic. Add tests for nested-index and artifact entries.
verifier_note: Probe: index with a nested `application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json` entry -> `descriptor_media_type_mismatch for "manifest[1]"`; Helm config media type -> same. integrity.go:154-156 applies IsManifestMediaType to every entry and verifyRootDocument (scan.go:1014) runs it before SelectDescriptors, so the whole scan fails before any platform is selected. Nested indexes are rare in practice; low is right.

title: Media-type comparison is case-inconsistent between document.go and integrity.go, and ParseDocument echoes the untrusted Content-Type header into its error
description: normalizeMediaType (used by IsIndexMediaType/IsManifestMediaType/IsLayerMediaType/LayerCompression) strips parameters but does not lowercase, whereas MediaTypeBase (used by VerifyMediaType/validation error text) lowercases via mime.ParseMediaType. Media types are case-insensitive per RFC 2045, so `Application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json` passes VerifyMediaType but fails IsManifestMediaType, producing contradictory verdicts on the same value. ParseDocument's default branch formats the raw header into the error (`unsupported manifest media type: %s`), contrary to the repository's no-echo convention; today the scanner wraps it as IntegrityError.Cause so it is reachable only via Unwrap, but a future `%v` print would leak header contents.
evidence: Probe: `MEDIATYPE IsManifestMediaType("Application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json")=false VerifyMediaType(lower, upper)=<nil>`; `SCHEMA1 ParseDocument err=unsupported manifest media type: application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v1+prettyjws; MARKER`. document.go:440-449 normalizeMediaType has no ToLower; integrity.go:186-188 `return strings.ToLower(parsed)`; document.go:155 `return Document{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported manifest media type: %s", mediaType)`.
proposed_fix: Replace normalizeMediaType with MediaTypeBase (single canonicalisation), and change the ParseDocument error to a fixed message (or an IntegrityError with the quoted/bounded value via safeIntegrityField). Add a test that mixed-case media types are accepted consistently and that error text does not contain a marker from the header.
verifier_note: Probe: IsManifestMediaType("Application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json")=false while VerifyMediaType(lower, upper)=nil; ParseDocument default branch returns `unsupported manifest media type: application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v1+prettyjws; MARKER` echoing the raw header. document.go:440-449 vs integrity.go:179-189 as cited. Practical impact is small because body mediaType fields are canonical, hence low.

title: isNonPublicAddress classifies deprecated site-local fec0::/10 and IPv4-compatible ::/96 addresses as public
description: The prefix table covers RFC 1918, CGNAT, TEST-NETs, 240/4, ULA, link-local, NAT64, 6to4, Teredo, documentation and benchmarking space, and IPv4-mapped addresses are unmapped, but the deprecated site-local range fec0::/10 (still routed in some legacy enterprise networks) and the IPv4-compatible range ::/96 (e.g. ::7f00:1) are not listed and pass IsGlobalUnicast. Practical exploitability is low (Linux does not translate ::/96 to IPv4 and fec0::/10 is rare) but both are non-public by definition and cheap to block.
evidence: Probe: `ADDR ::7f00:1 nonPublic=false`; `ADDR fec0::1 nonPublic=false` (while `::ffff:10.0.0.1`, `0.0.0.0`, `224.0.0.1`, `::`, `169.254.169.254`, `100.127.255.255` are correctly true). client.go:1122-1151 nonPublicAddressPrefixes lacks `fec0::/10` and `::/96`.
proposed_fix: Append netip.MustParsePrefix("fec0::/10") and netip.MustParsePrefix("::/96") to nonPublicAddressPrefixes and extend TestNonPublicAddressClassification with `::7f00:1` and `fec0::1`.
verifier_note: Probe: isNonPublicAddress(::7f00:1)=false, (fec0::1)=false, while ::ffff:10.0.0.1, 255.255.255.255, 224.0.0.1 and :: are correctly true. netip.Addr.IsGlobalUnicast returns true for site-local and IPv4-compatible addresses, and neither prefix is in nonPublicAddressPrefixes (client.go:1122-1151).

title: Blob requests have no response-header deadline: a registry that accepts the connection but never answers holds the scan until the full BlobTimeout
description: OpenBlob deliberately skips withRequestTimeout so the body stream is not cut, but nothing bounds the time to first byte: the per-request transport clone sets only a 30 s dial timeout (hard-coded, independent of LAYERLEAK_HTTP_TIMEOUT) and leaves ResponseHeaderTimeout at 0. A stalled or black-holed blob endpoint (or a redirect target that hangs) therefore consumes the entire LAYERLEAK_BLOB_TIMEOUT (default 10 m) per layer before failing, and the retry loop cannot help because the attempt never returns.
evidence: client.go:252 `response, err := c.doRequest(ctx, http.MethodGet, c.BlobURL(repository, digest), "", repository)` (no withRequestTimeout, by design); client.go:1074 `transport.DialContext = (&net.Dialer{Timeout: 30 * time.Second, KeepAlive: 30 * time.Second}).DialContext`; probe `BASE ... TLSHandshakeTimeout=10s ResponseHeaderTimeout=0s`.
proposed_fix: Set transport.ResponseHeaderTimeout (and TLSHandshakeTimeout when the base leaves it 0) to c.requestTimeout when configured, and derive the dial timeout from it instead of a constant; keep the body stream bounded by the caller's BlobTimeout. Add a test with a transport that delays headers beyond RequestTimeout on a blob request and assert a timely failure.
verifier_note: OpenBlob (client.go:252) passes the caller ctx without withRequestTimeout; hardenHTTPClient clones the base transport (DefaultTransport: ResponseHeaderTimeout 0, TLSHandshakeTimeout 10s) and pinnedTransport only sets a hard-coded 30 s Dialer (1074). Nothing bounds time-to-first-byte except the scanner's BlobTimeout (scan.go:407-408, default 10m). Verified by code reading; the auditor's BASE probe output is consistent with Go's DefaultTransport values.

title: Registry HTTP failures are untyped strings, so a missing image (registry 404) is reported by the API as 502 scan_failed and cannot be distinguished from upstream outages or 429 rate limits
description: checkResponse returns `fmt.Errorf("registry request failed: status=%d %s", ...)` with no type or sentinel; fetchToken does the same for auth failures. Downstream, api/handler.go classifyScanError falls through to `default: return http.StatusBadGateway, "scan_failed"`, and jobs.scanRepository can only record the string. Operators cannot tell 'tag does not exist' (client error) from 'registry down' (retryable), and the CLI cannot choose exit codes accordingly. No production code string-matches these messages (verified), so introducing a type is safe.
evidence: client.go:408-415 `return nil, fmt.Errorf("registry request failed: status=%d %s", response.StatusCode, http.StatusText(response.StatusCode))`; client.go:495 `return "", fmt.Errorf("auth request failed: status=%d %s", ...)`; internal/api/handler.go:741-742 `default: return http.StatusBadGateway, "scan_failed", "the registry scan could not be completed"`.
proposed_fix: Add `type StatusError struct{ Method, Host string; StatusCode int; Auth bool }` with Error()/Is helpers (e.g. IsNotFound, IsUnauthorized, IsRateLimited), return it from checkResponse/fetchToken, and map it in classifyScanError (404/401 on manifests → 404 or 422 `image_not_found`/`registry_unauthorized`, 429 → 429/503 `registry_rate_limited`, 5xx → 502). Use the same type in isRetryableStatus decisions and jobs TagResult status. Document the new API error codes in openapi.yaml as part of 3.0.0.
verifier_note: client.go:414 and 495 return plain fmt.Errorf strings; api/handler.go:744-745 maps anything unclassified to 502 scan_failed. Verified no production code string-matches these messages (grep for `registry request failed|status=%d|auth request failed` hits only client.go and a test). Introducing a typed error is safe; API error-code additions are a documented 3.0.0 change.

title: NewClient swallows configuration errors until the first request and endpoint overrides are not validated at startup; v3 should return errors from construction
description: NewClient joins base/auth URL parse errors, allowlist errors, scheme/allowlist mismatches and transport problems into client.configErr and only returns it from doRequest. config.Load reads LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_BASE_URL/AUTH_URL with envOrDefault and no validation, and scanservice builds a client per scan, so an API server with `LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_BASE_URL=htps://...` or an http override without an allowlist starts healthy and fails every scan with 502. Options.AllowPrivateHosts is a test-only override exposed on the production struct (its doc string says so in the transport error). A major release is the natural moment to change the constructor signature.
evidence: client.go:139 `configErr: errors.Join(baseErr, authErr, registryAllowlistErr, authAllowlistErr)`; client.go:351-353 `if c.configErr != nil { return nil, c.configErr }`; client.go:1027 `fmt.Errorf("custom registry transport requires explicit AllowPrivateHosts test override")`; internal/config/config.go:245-246 `RegistryBaseURL: envOrDefault("LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_BASE_URL", ""), RegistryAuthURL: envOrDefault("LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_AUTH_URL", "")`.
proposed_fix: Change to `NewClient(options Options) (*Client, error)`, validate LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_BASE_URL/AUTH_URL (scheme, host, no query/userinfo, http only with allowlist) in config.Load so the API refuses to start or /readyz fails, move AllowPrivateHosts behind an unexported test hook (e.g. an internal option set only from _test.go), and replace ad-hoc limits.Kind("auth_response_bytes")/("auth_token_cache_entries") strings with exported constants. Update scanservice.registryClient to propagate the error.
verifier_note: client.go:139 joins construction errors into configErr, returned only at doRequest (351-353); config.go:245-246 reads LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_BASE_URL/AUTH_URL with envOrDefault and no validation; scanservice/service.go:159-181 builds a client per scan and cannot propagate an error. Fix is appropriate for a major version.

title: golangci-lint (default config) reports 8 issues in the area: unchecked Body.Close errors, deprecated DialTLS assignment, a tautological MaxInt64 comparison and a De Morgan simplification
description: CI runs only `go vet` and revive (verify.yml:56-57, revive.toml), so these are not caught. errcheck: client.go:187, 211, 299, 391 and client_test.go:164 ignore Body.Close() errors; staticcheck SA1019: client.go:1075 assigns the deprecated Transport.DialTLS; SA4003: limits.go:80 `if limit >= math.MaxInt64` can only be equality; QF1001: client.go:852 double negation. None change behaviour, but adopting golangci-lint before 3.0.0 is cheap and the deprecated field will eventually be removed.
evidence: `golangci-lint run ./internal/registry/... ./internal/manifest/... ./internal/limits/...` → `client.go:187:27: Error return value of response.Body.Close is not checked (errcheck)` (also 211, 299, 391, client_test.go:164), `limits.go:80:5: SA4003: no value of type int64 is greater than math.MaxInt64 (staticcheck)`, `client.go:852:33: QF1001: could apply De Morgan's law`, `client.go:1075:2: SA1019: transport.DialTLS has been deprecated since Go 1.14` — `8 issues: errcheck: 5, staticcheck: 3`.
proposed_fix: As proposed, plus either wire revive into verify.yml or delete revive.toml when adopting golangci-lint (which can run revive as a linter).
verifier_note: Re-ran `golangci-lint run ./internal/registry/... ./internal/manifest/... ./internal/limits/...`: identical 8 issues (errcheck x5 incl. client_test.go:164, SA4003 limits.go:80, QF1001 client.go:852, SA1019 client.go:1075). One correction to the description: revive is not run in CI either; grep of .github/ for `revive|golangci` finds nothing and verify.yml:57 runs only `go vet ./...`, so revive.toml is currently dead configuration.

title: Two internal import lines in the registry package must move to the /v3 module path
description: When go.mod becomes `module github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3`, the only in-area imports of the module's own packages are client.go lines 21-22 (`internal/limits`, `internal/manifest`) and client_test.go line 17 (`internal/manifest`). internal/manifest and internal/limits import only stdlib and third-party modules (distribution/reference, go-digest), so they need no edits beyond what gofmt/goimports would keep.
evidence: client.go:21-22 `"github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/internal/limits"` / `"github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/internal/manifest"`; client_test.go:17 `"github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/internal/manifest"`; reference.go:9-10 imports only `github.com/distribution/reference` and `github.com/opencontainers/go-digest`.
proposed_fix: Rewrite the three import paths to `github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3/internal/...` in the same commit as the go.mod module line change (a repo-wide `gofmt -r`/sed for the prefix `github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/internal/` → `github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3/internal/` covers them); re-run `go build ./... && go test ./internal/registry/ ./internal/manifest/ ./internal/limits/`.
verifier_note: grep `github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/` across internal/registry, internal/manifest, internal/limits returns exactly client.go:21, client.go:22 and client_test.go:17. Required for the /v3 move; release blocking as stated.

title: Retry attempts share one RequestTimeout deadline, so a slow or black-holed first attempt never gets a retry (dial timeout 30 s == default LAYERLEAK_HTTP_TIMEOUT 30 s)
description: FetchManifest/ResolveManifest/ListTags/fetchToken wrap the whole call in withRequestTimeout (client.go:176-177, 203, 286, 468) and executeRequest loops inside that single context. isRetryableRequestError returns false as soon as ctx.Err() != nil (672-678), so any attempt that consumed the deadline (a stalled dial, TLS handshake or slow headers) is never retried; only attempts that fail fast are. With the hard-coded 30 s Dialer timeout (1074) equal to the default LAYERLEAK_HTTP_TIMEOUT of 30s, a black-holed registry address exhausts the request deadline on the first attempt and LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_REQUEST_ATTEMPTS never has an effect for the most common transient failure. Not documented in README (it says only 'Attempts including the first request').
evidence: Scratchpad probe: transport that blocks until r.Context().Done() then returns a net timeout, RequestAttempts=3, RequestTimeout=30ms -> `DEADLINE-SHARED requests=1 err=... dial: i/o timeout`; transport that fails instantly with the same error -> `FAST-FAIL requests=3`. client.go:676-678: `if ctx != nil && ctx.Err() != nil { return false }`; client.go:1074: `net.Dialer{Timeout: 30 * time.Second, ...}`.
proposed_fix: Apply the request timeout per attempt inside executeRequest (derive attemptCtx from the caller's ctx for each attempt) while keeping the caller's ctx as the overall cap, and make the dial timeout a fraction of the request timeout (or configurable) so a dial timeout can be retried; alternatively document that attempts share a single deadline. Add a test asserting a second attempt occurs after a first attempt that times out.

title: No User-Agent header: registries see the generic Go default, so layerleak traffic cannot be identified or allowlisted in registry logs
description: executeRequest sets only Accept and Authorization; Go then sends `Go-http-client/1.1` (or `/2.0`). Registry operators and Docker Hub rate-limit dashboards cannot attribute requests to layerleak, some WAF policies throttle the generic Go UA, and the project cannot be contacted about abusive traffic. A 3.0.0 release is the natural moment to introduce `User-Agent: layerleak/<version>`.
evidence: `grep -rn "User-Agent" --include=*.go .` -> no matches. client.go:424-429: only `request.Header.Set("Accept", ...)` and `request.Header.Set("Authorization", ...)`.
proposed_fix: Add Options.UserAgent (default `layerleak/<cli.Version>`), set it in executeRequest for registry and auth requests, and pass the version from cli/scanservice. Assert the header in an existing client test.

title: No way to supply registry credentials: private images cannot be scanned at all (Basic auth on the token endpoint is unsupported)
description: fetchToken issues the token request anonymously and there is no Options field, env variable or flag for a username/password, bearer token or docker config.json credential helper. README:7 scopes the product to public images, which is consistent, but it is the single largest product gap for CI users who want to scan their own private images before pushing, and a major version is the moment to add it. Any implementation must keep the existing no-echo and allowlist invariants (credentials only sent to the validated realm/registry host, never logged).
evidence: client.go:488: `response, err := c.executeRequest(requestCtx, http.MethodGet, parsedRealm.String(), "", "")` (no Authorization on the token request); Options struct (client.go:32-46) has no credential fields; README.md:7: `It resolves public image`.
proposed_fix: Add optional LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_USERNAME/LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_PASSWORD (or a --registry-credentials-file / docker config lookup keyed by registry host) that sets Basic auth on the token-endpoint request and, for registries without a token service, on registry requests to the configured base host only; strip on redirects like Bearer today; never persist or log; document in README and SECURITY.md threat model.

title: Web docs tell users to set LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_BASE_URL to force traffic 'through a proxy'; that is not a proxy mechanism and the real proxy path (HTTPS_PROXY) is broken
description: The 'Registry overrides' bullet says the base/auth URL overrides are for 'forcing traffic through a proxy or alternate auth endpoint'. A base-URL override only changes the host that receives `/v2/<repo>/...` requests and still follows the registry's own WWW-Authenticate realm and blob redirects, so it cannot route Docker Hub traffic through a forward proxy; a user following this advice will point the scanner at a proxy host that returns 404 for /v2 paths. Meanwhile standard HTTPS_PROXY support, which README never mentions, fails per REG-01. At release the sentence is misleading.
evidence: web/docs/index.html:243-246: `LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_BASE_URL and LAYERLEAK_REGISTRY_AUTH_URL are optional. Leave them unset unless forcing traffic through a proxy or alternate auth endpoint.`; `grep -n -i proxy README.md` -> no matches; client.go:163-173 builds /v2 paths on the base URL.
proposed_fix: Reword to 'unless pointing at a pull-through mirror or alternate registry/auth endpoint' and, once REG-01 is fixed, add a short 'Proxies' paragraph to README and the web docs stating that HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY are honoured and that the proxy then performs egress control.

title: PostgresConfig.withDefaults leaves MaxIdleConns at 0, so a bare config keeps no idle connections
description: withDefaults fills MaxOpenConns, lifetimes and timeouts but not MaxIdleConns. database/sql's SetMaxIdleConns(0) means 'retain no idle connections', so every statement outside an open transaction dials a new TCP/TLS connection and re-authenticates. The API, CLI and purge binaries happen to pass config.DatabaseMaxIdleConns (default 5), so production is unaffected, but any other caller (tests, future tooling, third-party embedding of the package) silently gets the worst pool behaviour, and TestPostgresConfigDefaults enshrines 0 as the expected default.
evidence: storage.go:270-287 withDefaults sets MaxOpenConns/ConnMaxLifetime/ConnMaxIdleTime/QueryTimeout/WriteTimeout only; postgres.go:43 `db.SetMaxIdleConns(config.MaxIdleConns)`. Probe TestProbeDefaultMaxIdleConns after three ListRepositories calls: `default pool after 3 queries: Open=0 Idle=0 InUse=0 MaxOpen=10`. storage_test.go:97 asserts `config.MaxIdleConns != 0` is a failure.
proposed_fix: In withDefaults set MaxIdleConns to min(2, MaxOpenConns) when it is 0 (or mirror config.go's default of 5 capped at MaxOpenConns), and update TestPostgresConfigDefaults. Alternatively document that MaxIdleConns=0 is intentional, but the current asymmetry with config.go (default 5) suggests it is not.
verifier_note: withDefaults (storage.go:270-287) never sets MaxIdleConns; postgres.go:43 passes it straight to SetMaxIdleConns, where <=0 means retain no idle connections. Probe with a bare PostgresConfig after three ListRepositories calls: `Open=0 Idle=0 MaxOpen=10 MaxIdleClosed=5`, i.e. every statement dialed and dropped a connection. storage_test.go:97 asserts MaxIdleConns==0. Production callers (api/run.go:37, cli/storage.go:19, cmd/purge/main.go:49) pass config.DatabaseMaxIdleConns (default 5), so impact is limited to other embedders.

title: PurgeRawSecrets is one unbatched transaction bounded by the write timeout, blocks all writers meanwhile, and docs omit post-purge VACUUM/backup residue
description: The purge takes the exclusive advisory lock (blocking every SaveScan, which takes the shared lock) and runs two whole-table UPDATEs in a single transaction under withTimeout(ctx, writeTimeout) (2m default). On a large finding_occurrences table the UPDATE can exceed the deadline, roll back, and leave zero progress while having stalled writers for two minutes; the operator has no --dry-run to size the job (CountRawSecrets exists but is only used at API startup). Separately, an UPDATE does not remove raw material from dead tuples, WAL, replicas or backups until VACUUM and backup rotation; README:313 says the command 'clears' the columns and SECURITY.md mentions backups generically, but neither says VACUUM/rotate after purging.
evidence: admin.go:45 `ctx, cancel := withTimeout(ctx, s.writeTimeout)`; admin.go:55-66 exclusive `pg_advisory_xact_lock($1)` then `UPDATE findings SET value = '' WHERE value <> ''` and `UPDATE finding_occurrences SET raw_snippet = '' WHERE raw_snippet <> ''` in one tx; postgres.go:163 SaveScan takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared($1)` on the same key. cmd/purge/main.go:27 offers only `--confirm`. README.md:312-313 'The purge command requires --confirm, serializes concurrent purge attempts, and clears only findings.value and finding_occurrences.raw_snippet'; no mention of VACUUM in README.md, SECURITY.md or docs/ (grep -i vacuum returned nothing).
proposed_fix: Purge in id-range batches (e.g. 5,000 rows per transaction, each taking the exclusive lock briefly or keeping it session-level while committing per batch) with its own LAYERLEAK_PURGE_TIMEOUT, print running totals, and add `--dry-run` that prints CountRawSecrets. In README/SECURITY add: after purge run `VACUUM (FULL)`/pg_repack on findings and finding_occurrences (or accept autovacuum delay), rotate/expire backups and WAL archives that predate the purge, and repeat on replicas.
verifier_note: admin.go:45 bounds the purge by writeTimeout; :55 takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(key) exclusive while SaveScan takes the shared form on the same key (postgres.go:163); :59 and :63 are single whole-table UPDATEs in one transaction. cmd/purge/main.go:27 offers only --confirm. README.md:312-313 wording confirmed; grep -i vacuum over README.md, SECURITY.md and docs/ returns nothing.

title: Exact-version readiness forbids rolling upgrades and app-only rollbacks; 3.0.0 should state the policy explicitly
description: checkSchemaVersion requires the ledger to equal exactly [0001..0004]; RunMigrations rejects any unknown version. Consequences: once a future 0005 is applied, every older API replica becomes unready and an older migrate binary refuses to run, so upgrades must be 'migrate, then replace all replicas' with no overlap, and rolling back the application requires running the down migration first. This is defensible (and README/openapi say 'exact schema version 0004'), but it is undocumented as a policy and it is the kind of contract a major release should either commit to or relax (e.g. accept newer, unknown versions as long as required objects exist).
evidence: migrate.go:1020-1022 `if !slices.Equal(versions, expectedVersions) { return fmt.Errorf("database schema ledger has versions %v, expected %v; run layerleak-migrate-up", ...) }`; migrate.go:231-233 `return fmt.Errorf("database contains unknown migration version %s", version)`. Probe with a 0005 row: `checkSchemaVersion with 0005 present -> database schema ledger has versions [0001 0002 0003 0004 0005], expected [0001 0002 0003 0004]` and `RunMigrations(older binary) with 0005 present -> database contains unknown migration version 0005`. README.md:330 and web/docs/openapi.yaml:54 document the exact-version behaviour.
proposed_fix: Decide for 3.0.0 and document in README (Storage) and RELEASING: either (a) keep strict pinning and write the upgrade runbook 'stop/scale-down API -> migrate -> deploy new API; to roll back the app, apply the down migration first', or (b) make readiness accept ledger versions greater than CurrentSchemaVersion as long as validateSchemaContract(CurrentSchemaVersion) passes, keeping RunMigrations strict. Either way add the test from DB-07 that pins the chosen behaviour.
verifier_note: Probe with a 0005 ledger row: checkSchemaVersion -> `database schema ledger has versions [0001 0002 0003 0004 0005], expected [0001 0002 0003 0004]; run layerleak-migrate-up`; RunMigrations -> `database contains unknown migration version 0005` (migrate.go:1020-1022 and :231-233). README.md:330 and openapi.yaml:54 document exact version 0004.

title: Admin binaries lack status/dry-run/down/retention operations that a 3.0.0 operator toolset should have
description: layerleak-migrate-up accepts no arguments: there is no `status` (print ledger vs files), no `--dry-run`, no `down` (the .down.sql files exist and are tested only as a full apply-then-rollback, and can only be run by hand with psql, bypassing the ledger), and no `--version`. layerleak-purge-raw-secrets has no `--dry-run` (see DB-06). There is no retention/prune command even though scan_runs.result_json stores a full redacted result per scan (several MB for a 10k-finding scan) and nothing ever deletes scan_runs, stale tags, or repositories.
evidence: cmd/migrate/main.go:23 `if len(os.Args) != 1 { return fmt.Errorf("layerleak-migrate-up does not accept arguments") }`; migrations/*.down.sql exist but grep 'down.sql' in internal/storage/migrate.go returns nothing (loader pattern is `\.up\.sql$`, migrate.go:24); cmd/purge/main.go:27 defines only `--confirm`; postgres.go:480-538 inserts a scan_runs row with `result_json` on every SaveScan; no DELETE FROM scan_runs anywhere in internal/storage.
proposed_fix: Add subcommands or flags to the migrate binary: `status`, `--dry-run`, `down --to 000N` that runs the matching .down.sql inside a transaction and deletes ledger rows (or explicitly document that downs are psql-only), and `--version`. Add `--dry-run` to purge. Add a `layerleak-prune` (or `purge --scan-runs-older-than 90d`) command with an index on scan_runs(scanned_at) to bound table growth. Update README/RELEASING accordingly.
verifier_note: cmd/migrate/main.go:23 rejects any argument; migrationFilenamePattern (migrate.go:24) only matches .up.sql so downs are never loaded; cmd/purge/main.go:27 defines only --confirm; grep for `DELETE FROM scan_runs|repositories|manifests` in internal/ and cmd/ (non-test) returns nothing, so nothing ever prunes scan_runs.result_json.

title: Schema detection mixes search_path-resolved to_regclass() with current_schema()-scoped catalog queries
description: tableExistsContext uses `to_regclass($1)`, which resolves through the full search_path, while columnExistsContext, requireSchemaColumns, requireSchemaConstraints, requireSchemaIndexes and indexExistsContext filter on `current_schema()` (the first existing schema in search_path). If the tables live in a later search_path entry (e.g. search_path=app,public with data in public), table existence passes but column checks fail, producing misleading 'partial legacy migration 0002 detected' / 'legacy schema is missing X' errors, and `CREATE TABLE schema_migrations` lands in the first schema rather than beside the data.
evidence: migrate.go:584 `SELECT to_regclass($1) IS NOT NULL`; migrate.go:596 `WHERE table_schema = current_schema()`; migrate.go:694 `WHERE namespace_row.nspname = current_schema()`; migrate.go:783 same; migrate.go:899 same; migrate.go:107 `CREATE TABLE schema_migrations (...)` unqualified.
proposed_fix: Resolve the target schema once (`SELECT current_schema()`) and use it everywhere: `to_regclass(format('%I.%I', schema, table))` for table/constraint existence, schema-qualified CREATE TABLE for the ledger, and the same schema in every catalog query; or switch all existence checks to pg_class/pg_namespace filtered on that schema. Also read the ledger with a schema-qualified name so a foreign schema_migrations on the search_path is ignored rather than misread. Add the two probe scenarios as integration tests.
verifier_note: Raised from medium to high confidence by two probes. (1) Migrated schema in layerleak_test, empty schema layerleak_first, DSN search_path=layerleak_first,layerleak_test: both NewPostgresStore(RequireSchema) and RunMigrations fail with `database schema ledger says 0004, but required schema objects are missing: database schema is missing repositories.id; restore the database or repair the migration`, a misleading diagnosis of a healthy database (to_regclass found the ledger via search_path, current_schema()-scoped catalog queries did not). (2) A golang-migrate-style `schema_migrations(version bigint, dirty boolean)` in a later search_path schema with no Layerleak tables yet: RunMigrations fails `read schema migration ledger: pq: column "name" does not exist (42703)` because tableExistsContext (migrate.go:584) resolved the foreign table and skipped CREATE TABLE (:106-117). Severity stays low because it needs a multi-schema search_path.

title: lib/pq v1.12.3 is current and actively released; pgx/v5 is optional for 3.0.0 but is the natural vehicle for batching
description: The module pins github.com/lib/pq v1.12.3, which is the latest upstream release (published 2026-04-03) and whose bundled README no longer carries the older 'maintenance mode, use pgx' notice, so there is no dependency-health reason to migrate now. A move to jackc/pgx/v5 (v5.11.0 available) would give CopyFrom/Batch for DB-02, native []string scanning (removing pq.Array/pq.StringArray), better cancellation semantics and pgxpool, at the cost of touching every file in the package (driver name, array helpers, error handling) and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. All SQL already uses $n placeholders and multi-statement migration files are executed without parameters, both of which pgx's stdlib adapter supports.
evidence: `go list -m -json github.com/lib/pq@latest` -> Version v1.12.3, Time 2026-04-03T15:45:16Z; `go list -m -versions github.com/lib/pq` ends at v1.12.3; `go list -m -versions github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` ends at v5.11.0; grep -i 'maintenance|pgx' in /root/go/pkg/mod/github.com/lib/pq@v1.12.3/README.md returned nothing; postgres.go:14 `"github.com/lib/pq"`, postgres.go:318 `pq.Array(tagNames)`, read_postgres.go:412 `var detectors pq.StringArray`; THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:11 lists lib/pq v1.12.3.
proposed_fix: Keep lib/pq for 3.0.0 unless DB-02 batching is implemented, in which case adopt pgx/v5 via github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib (sql.Open("pgx", ...)) plus pgx.CopyFrom/Batch for the bulk paths, replace pq.Array/pq.StringArray with native slices, update THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and the license CSV job, and run the full integration suite. Either way run `go get -u` checks and govulncheck as part of the 3.0.0 preflight.
verifier_note: `go list -m -versions github.com/lib/pq` ends at v1.12.3 (go.mod:7 pins it) and `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` ends at v5.11.0, matching the auditor. lib/pq usage is confined to postgres.go:14/318 (pq.Array) and read_postgres.go:13/412 (pq.StringArray).

title: golangci-lint reports 13 unchecked Close() errors in storage/cmd and CI has no lint gate beyond gofmt/go vet
description: Running golangci-lint v2.5.0 with default settings (no .golangci.yml in repo) reports errcheck violations for unchecked db.Close/connection.Close/rows.Close/store.Close/response.Body.Close in the area. None is a functional bug (rows.Close errors are surfaced via rows.Err, Close on a pool is best-effort), but CI only runs gofmt and go vet (revive.toml exists yet no workflow runs revive), so the codebase has no enforced linter and these will accumulate. Most projects either exclude Close from errcheck or handle it explicitly.
evidence: `golangci-lint run ./internal/storage/... ./cmd/...` -> `13 issues: * errcheck: 13`, including internal/storage/migrate.go:78 `defer db.Close()`, :86 `defer connection.Close()`, :209/:712/:798 `defer rows.Close()`, internal/storage/postgres.go:51,55 `db.Close()`, cmd/purge/main.go:59 `defer store.Close()`, cmd/healthcheck/main.go:59 `defer response.Body.Close()`. grep 'golangci|revive|staticcheck' .github/workflows/*.yml -> only codacy references; verify.yml:49 gofmt, :57 `go vet ./...`.
proposed_fix: Same as proposed, plus set `issues.max-same-issues: 0` in .golangci.yml so CI reports the real count, and handle the 16 non-test sites explicitly (`defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()` or `exclude-functions` for (*database/sql.Rows).Close, (*database/sql.DB).Close, (*database/sql.Conn).Close, (io.ReadCloser).Close).
verifier_note: The finding stands but the evidence undercounts: `golangci-lint run ./internal/storage/... ./cmd/...` prints 13 only because golangci-lint's default `max-same-issues: 3` truncates identical messages (cmd/purge/main.go:59 is reported when the package is linted alone, and the combined run hides it). With `--max-same-issues 0 --max-issues-per-linter 0` there are 61 errcheck hits: migrate.go 7, postgres.go 3, read_postgres.go 4, cmd/healthcheck/main.go 1, cmd/purge/main.go 1 (16 in non-test code) and 45 in storage_integration_test.go. No workflow runs golangci-lint or revive (grep over .github/workflows returns nothing); verify.yml runs gofmt and go vet only.

title: PostgresConfig.Validate rejects unix-socket and libpq key=value connection strings that lib/pq accepts
description: Validate requires a URL with a non-empty host and a postgres/postgresql scheme. lib/pq supports `postgres:///dbname?host=/var/run/postgresql` (host in the query string, used by Cloud SQL Auth Proxy sockets and socket-only hardened deployments) and libpq keyword strings (`host=... dbname=...`), both of which this check rejects before the driver sees them. Since RunMigrations, the API, the CLI and purge all go through Validate, such deployments cannot use Layerleak at all. A major release is the right time to fix the accepted DSN grammar.
evidence: storage.go:239-241 `if strings.TrimSpace(parsed.Hostname()) == "" { return fmt.Errorf("database url host is required") }`; storage.go:234-238 scheme switch rejects non-URL strings with 'database url must use postgres scheme'; storage_test.go:36 asserts `postgres:///layerleak` is rejected; lib/pq README (module cache) shows `sql.Open("postgres", "host=localhost dbname=pqgo")` as the primary form.
proposed_fix: Accept an empty URL host when the query string contains `host=` (socket path or hostname), and either accept libpq keyword strings (skip URL parsing when the value contains no `://`, validating only that it is non-empty and does not echo on error) or document explicitly that only URL form is supported. Keep the 'never echo the DSN' property (TestPostgresConfigValidateDoesNotEchoMalformedDatabaseURL) and add cases for both new forms.
verifier_note: storage.go:234-241 rejects any non-URL string ('database url must use postgres scheme') and any URL with an empty Hostname(); storage_test.go:36 pins `postgres:///layerleak` as invalid. lib/pq accepts both `postgres:///db?host=/var/run/postgresql` (query-string host, socket path) and libpq keyword strings. Because RunMigrations (migrate.go:54), NewPostgresStore (postgres.go:34) and therefore the API, CLI and purge all go through Validate, socket-only deployments are locked out.

title: OFFSET pagination recomputes the full GROUP BY per page; 3.0.0 could add keyset cursors on the existing unique orderings
description: ListRepositoryFindings joins repositories -> repository_manifests -> findings -> finding_occurrences, aggregates every occurrence for the repository, applies HAVING, sorts and only then applies LIMIT/OFFSET, so each page costs O(total occurrences for the repository) and deep pages get slower; ListRepositoryScans and ListRepositories have the same OFFSET shape. The ORDER BY clauses already terminate in unique keys ((last_seen_at, id), (registry, repository)), which is exactly what keyset (`after`) pagination needs. Changing the public pagination contract is a major-version change, so 3.0.0 is the opportunity.
evidence: read_postgres.go:139-165 `... GROUP BY f.id HAVING CASE $5 ... ORDER BY f.last_seen_at DESC, f.id DESC LIMIT $6 OFFSET $7`; read_postgres.go:39 `ORDER BY last_seen_at DESC, repository ASC, registry ASC LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2`; read_postgres.go:102 `ORDER BY sr.scanned_at DESC, sr.id DESC LIMIT $3 OFFSET $4`. Probe TestProbeFindingsPaginationTies confirmed the orderings are total (stable pages for 7 tied rows).
proposed_fix: Add optional cursor parameters (`after_last_seen`, `after_id` or an opaque base64 cursor) to the three list endpoints and corresponding ReadStore methods that translate to `WHERE (f.last_seen_at, f.id) < ($a, $b)`; keep limit/offset for one major cycle or drop it in 3.0.0 with a documented deprecation. For findings, consider a materialised per-finding aggregate (occurrence_count, actionable_count, suppressed_count, detectors) maintained in SaveScan to avoid the per-page GROUP BY.
verifier_note: read_postgres.go:139-165 aggregates every occurrence for the repository before HAVING/ORDER BY/LIMIT $6 OFFSET $7; :39 and :102 are the same OFFSET shape. Orderings end in unique keys ((last_seen_at, id), (scanned_at, id), (repository, registry) which is UNIQUE), so keyset cursors are feasible.

title: Several indexes match no query and the repository listing has none; a 0005 migration could right-size them
description: No read path filters on scan_runs.status, manifests platform columns, finding_occurrences (source_type,file_path,layer_digest), findings.fingerprint alone, repository_manifests.root_digest or tags(repository_id,manifest_digest), yet each has a btree that every SaveScan must maintain (finding_occurrences alone carries four btrees including the 15-column unique). finding_occurrences_finding_idx (finding_id) is a strict prefix of finding_occurrences_disposition_idx (finding_id, disposition, last_seen_at DESC) and therefore redundant. Conversely ListRepositories orders by last_seen_at DESC, repository, registry with no supporting index (fine while repositories is small). Adding a 0005 migration would also require updating CurrentSchemaVersion, README:330, openapi.yaml:54 and RELEASING:249.
evidence: migrations/0003_scan_runs.up.sql:30 `CREATE INDEX scan_runs_status_scanned_idx ON scan_runs (status, scanned_at DESC)` vs read_postgres.go (no `status =` predicate anywhere); 0001_initial.up.sql:21,35,53,67,113 create manifests_platform_idx, repository_manifests_root_digest_idx, tags_repository_manifest_idx, findings_fingerprint_idx, finding_occurrences_source_idx, none referenced by predicates in read_postgres.go/postgres.go; 0001:110 `finding_occurrences_finding_idx (finding_id)` and 0004:264 `finding_occurrences_disposition_idx (finding_id, disposition, last_seen_at DESC)`; read_postgres.go:39 ORDER BY on repositories has no index (0001 defines only the UNIQUE (registry, repository)).
proposed_fix: If 3.0.0 ships a schema change anyway, add 0005 that drops finding_occurrences_finding_idx and the unused single-purpose indexes (keep any the maintainer relies on for ad-hoc ops queries, e.g. findings_fingerprint_idx for cross-repository secret lookups, which is a plausible future API feature) and adds repositories(last_seen_at DESC, repository, registry); update schemaIndexRequirements, CurrentSchemaVersion/currentMigrationCount, and the 0004 references in README, openapi.yaml, RELEASING and CHANGELOG. Otherwise defer and just record the rationale.
verifier_note: No predicate in read_postgres.go or postgres.go uses scan_runs.status, manifests platform columns, (source_type,file_path,layer_digest), fingerprint alone, repository_manifests.root_digest or tags(repository_id,manifest_digest); the FK cascades are covered by PK prefixes or scan_runs_repository_scanned_idx. One addition: finding_occurrences_finding_idx (0001:110) is a prefix of both finding_occurrences_disposition_idx (0004:264) and the 15-column finding_occurrences_identity_key, so finding_occurrences carries three finding_id-leading btrees plus the PK. Any 0005 also has to update schemaIndexRequirements (migrate.go:496-507) or readiness will reject the dropped indexes.

title: tags and manifests are write-only tables: no API or CLI path reads them, and stale tags are never removed
description: SaveScan maintains repositories, manifests (with platform columns and last_scan_status/error), repository_manifests (root_digest) and tags on every scan, but ReadStore (storage.go:77-83) exposes nothing from manifests or tags and read_postgres.go never selects or joins them (repository_manifests is only used as a join key). replaceTagMappings deletes only tags present in the current scan (postgres.go:313-318), so a tag removed from the registry stays in `tags` indefinitely, pointing at an old digest, and nothing ever reads that state to notice. A major release should either expose this data (tags, platforms, per-manifest status) through the API/CLI with a reconciliation step for full-repository scans, or stop maintaining the unused columns/indexes.
evidence: grep 'FROM tags|FROM manifests|JOIN tags|JOIN manifests' over internal/ and cmd/ non-test Go files -> only postgres.go:314 (DELETE FROM tags) and :341 (NOT EXISTS subquery); storage.go:77-83 ReadStore has ListRepositories/ListRepositoryScans/ListRepositoryFindings/GetScanRun/GetFinding only; postgres.go:313-318 `DELETE FROM tags WHERE repository_id = $1 AND tag = ANY($2) AND last_seen_at <= $3` limits deletion to tags in the current scan.
proposed_fix: For 3.0.0 decide: (a) add GET /repositories/{registry}/{repository}/tags and /manifests (ReadStore methods over tags, manifests, repository_manifests), and in repository-mode scans delete tags not returned by the enumeration (the scan already knows TagsEnumerated); or (b) document tags/manifests as operator-only tables and drop their unused indexes in the same 0005 as DB-16. Either way add tests that read back what SaveScan writes to these tables.

title: API persists a completed scan under the HTTP request context, so a client disconnect discards the finished scan
description: handleScan derives scanCtx from request.Context() with ScanTimeout and passes it to ScanAndSave, which forwards the same ctx to store.SaveScan (service.go:149). net/http cancels request.Context() when the client goes away, so a client that times out or disconnects after the (expensive) scan has finished cancels the SaveScan transaction: database/sql rolls it back and no scan_run is recorded even though the work was done. The save phase should be shielded from client cancellation (bounded only by the write timeout).
evidence: internal/api/handler.go:329 `scanCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(request.Context(), h.options.ScanTimeout)`; :331 `outcome, err := h.scanner.ScanAndSave(scanCtx, ...)`; internal/scanservice/service.go:149 `scanRunID, storeErr := s.store.SaveScan(ctx, record)`; grep for context.WithoutCancel in internal/api and internal/scanservice -> none; postgres.go:152 SaveScan adds only writeTimeout on top of the caller's ctx.
proposed_fix: In scanservice.ScanAndSave run the save phase with `saveCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), writeTimeout)` (or let SaveScan accept an explicit detach flag) so a scan that completed is persisted even if the HTTP client disconnected; keep the request context for the scan phase. Add a handler test that cancels the request context after the stub scanner returns and asserts SaveScan was still called.

title: Staticcheck SA4003/SA1019 and ineffassign/wastedassign hits are real (if minor) code defects
description: Default-linter hits with a real code smell: limits.go:80 `if limit >= math.MaxInt64` (no int64 exceeds MaxInt64; should be `==`), layers/state.go:822 `contentClass := ContentClassText` is dead (both branches reassign), findings.go:452 and :546 `location := ""` dead assignment, state.go:367 and state_test.go:942 use deprecated `tar.TypeRegA`, client.go:1075 assigns deprecated `transport.DialTLS` (needed to clear it, so keep but annotate), client.go:852 De Morgan simplification.
evidence: `internal/limits/limits.go:80:5: SA4003: no value of type int64 is greater than math.MaxInt64 (staticcheck)`; `internal/layers/state.go:822:2: ineffectual assignment to contentClass (ineffassign)`; `internal/layers/state.go:367:21: SA1019: tar.TypeRegA has been deprecated since Go 1.11`; `internal/findings/findings.go:452:2: assigned to location, but reassigned without using the value (wastedassign)`
proposed_fix: Change to `limit == math.MaxInt64`; declare `var contentClass ContentClass` / `var location string`; drop `tar.TypeRegA` cases (TypeRegA == TypeReg since Go 1.11 is handled by tar.Reader which normalises it); add `//nolint:staticcheck // clearing deprecated field` on the DialTLS = nil line.

title: 22 unchecked Close/Remove/Finish error returns (errcheck)
description: errcheck flags 22 sites. Most are `defer x.Close()` of read-only bodies/rows, which is tolerable, but a few are in non-defer paths where an error is informative: state.go:960 `gzipReader.Close()` (non-defer), registry/client.go:211 and :391 `response.Body.Close()` in retry paths, cli/scan.go:107 `defer progress.Finish()` (may be swallowing a write error on the progress stream), storage/postgres.go:51,55 `db.Close()` on a failed open.
evidence: `internal/layers/state.go:960:20: Error return value of gzipReader.Close is not checked (errcheck)`; `internal/cli/scan.go:107:25: Error return value of progress.Finish is not checked`; `internal/storage/migrate.go:78:16: Error return value of db.Close is not checked`
proposed_fix: Decide a policy in .golangci.yml (exclude `(io.Closer).Close` in defers via errcheck exclude-functions) and explicitly handle or `_ =` the non-defer sites; log Close errors in storage/migrate paths where a failed close can mean a failed write.

title: One test accounts for ~70% of unit-suite wall time (4.1s; 22s under -race)
description: TestDetailedNormalizerBoundsLargeMetadataProvenanceWithManyMatches takes 4.12s in -short mode; internal/findings takes 22.0s under -race versus ~1s for every other package. Total -short wall time is 6s, -race 43s, so this one test is the critical path of CI's race job.
evidence: `--- PASS: TestDetailedNormalizerBoundsLargeMetadataProvenanceWithManyMatches (4.12s)`; race run: `ok github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/internal/findings 22.009s`
proposed_fix: Reduce the synthetic match count/provenance size to the smallest value that still exercises the bound, or guard the large variant with `if testing.Short() { t.Skip() }` and keep it in the full CI job.

title: Container binaries carry no version: Dockerfile builds without -X and nothing but the CLI reads cli.Version
description: The Dockerfile builds four binaries with `-ldflags="-s -w"` only; `cli.Version` (root.go:36, 'set via -ldflags') is never set, and only internal/cli/root.go:42 reads effectiveVersion(). A source-checkout container build has Main.Version `(devel)`, so even the CLI logic would print `dev`. The api/migrate/purge/healthcheck binaries have no --version at all, so a running 3.0.0 container cannot report what it is. The checkout CLI build reports `layerleak version v0.0.0-20260909174625-c2ddd4583b2f+dirty`, which README.md:69-72 documents as expected.
evidence: Dockerfile:20 `go build -mod=readonly -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o /out/layerleak-api ./cmd/api`; `grep -rn 'effectiveVersion()|cli.Version'` -> only internal/cli/root.go:42; `go version -m` on checkout build: `mod github.com/brumbelow/layerleak v0.0.0-20260909174625-c2ddd4583b2f+dirty`, `vcs.modified=true`.
proposed_fix: Add `ARG LAYERLEAK_VERSION` to the Dockerfile and pass `-X github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3/internal/cli.Version=$LAYERLEAK_VERSION` (and a shared internal/version package consumed by cmd/* so `layerleak-api --version` and the API /healthz or a version header report it); set the build-arg from the tag in container-release.yml.

title: __pycache__ is not gitignored, so running the Python tests dirties the tree and taints VCS build info
description: After the Python unit tests run, `git status --short` shows `?? scripts/__pycache__/` and `?? scripts/tests/__pycache__/` (they were already present when this audit began, so the 'clean working tree' premise was slightly off). Go stamps `vcs.modified=true` whenever untracked files exist, which is why the checkout build prints `+dirty`; a release build run on a machine that executed `python3 -m unittest` first would mis-stamp as dirty.
evidence: `git status --short` -> `?? scripts/__pycache__/` `?? scripts/tests/__pycache__/`; `.gitignore` has no `__pycache__` or `*.pyc` entry; `go version -m` -> `build vcs.modified=true`
proposed_fix: Add `__pycache__/` and `*.pyc` to .gitignore (and `scripts/tests/node_modules/` is already covered by `node_modules/`).

title: Six dependency updates available; govulncheck clean
description: `go list -m -u all`: klauspost/compress v1.19.2 -> v1.20.1, golang.org/x/sys v0.47.0 -> v0.48.0, golang.org/x/term v0.45.0 -> v0.46.0, spf13/pflag v1.0.9 -> v1.0.10, cpuguy83/go-md2man v2.0.6 -> v2.0.7, go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 v3.0.4 -> v3.0.5. govulncheck (x/vuln v1.8.0, which auto-switched the toolchain to go1.26.8 because it requires go >= 1.26) reports no vulnerabilities; CI's pin to govulncheck v1.7.0 (verify.yml:377) is therefore the right choice while go.mod stays at 1.25.13. go.mod also has four separate `require` blocks, which `go mod tidy` tolerates but is untidy for a 3.0.0 go.mod rewrite.
evidence: `github.com/klauspost/compress v1.19.2 [v1.20.1]`, `golang.org/x/sys v0.47.0 [v0.48.0]`, `golang.org/x/term v0.45.0 [v0.46.0]`; `go: golang.org/x/vuln@v1.8.0 requires go >= 1.26.0; switching to go1.26.8`; govulncheck: `No vulnerabilities found.`
proposed_fix: Bump the direct deps (compress is the only one with runtime relevance: gzip/zstd layer decoding) as part of the /v3 go.mod rewrite, collapse to one direct and one indirect require block, and keep govulncheck pinned to a version compatible with the go.mod toolchain line.

title: golangci-lint errcheck: unchecked Close() in run.go and healthcheck
description: Running golangci-lint v2.5.0 with defaults reports two errcheck hits in this area. CI does not run golangci-lint, so this is hygiene only, but a 3.0.0 that adds a lint gate would trip on them.

cmd/healthcheck/main.go:59:27: Error return value of `response.Body.Close` is not checked (errcheck)
internal/api/run.go:47:19: Error return value of `store.Close` is not checked (errcheck)

title: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md omits mousetrap, which cobra links into Windows CLI builds
description: The notice states it covers "the compiled CLI" and lists eight modules. github.com/inconshreveable/mousetrap v1.1.0 (Apache-2.0) is a go.mod indirect requirement pulled by cobra and compiled into windows/* builds of the CLI (cobra's command_win.go). The CI license inventory runs on linux only, so `go-licenses report` never lists it and the CSV attached to releases is also linux-scoped. Listed versions otherwise match go.mod exactly.
