title: Dockerfile polish: builder on Debian oldstable, HEALTHCHECK conflates liveness with DB readiness, /tmp sticky bit may not survive COPY
description: (a) Docker Hub offers golang:1.27.1-trixie; the build stays on bookworm (oldstable), so the copied /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt tracks Debian 12's ca-certificates package. (b) HEALTHCHECK runs layerleak-healthcheck which probes /readyz (database ping + schema); under plain Docker/Compose a database outage marks the API container unhealthy even though the process is fine, and Kubernetes ignores HEALTHCHECK entirely; README:394-395 documents the behaviour but not the implication. (c) `install -d -m 1777 /out/rootfs/tmp` followed by `COPY --from=build --chown=10001:10001 /out/rootfs/tmp /tmp` copies directory contents, not the directory; BuildKit creates the destination with default mode, so the 1777 sticky bit is likely lost (compose masks this with a tmpfs mount; `docker run` without --tmpfs would not). Could not verify (c) here because no Docker daemon is running.
evidence: Dockerfile:5 `golang:1.27.1-bookworm@sha256:...`; Docker Hub tags -> '1.27.1-trixie' available; Dockerfile:24 `install -d -m 1777 /out/rootfs/tmp`, :33 `COPY --from=build --chown=10001:10001 /out/rootfs/tmp /tmp`; Dockerfile:45-46 `HEALTHCHECK ... CMD ["/usr/local/bin/layerleak-healthcheck"]`; cmd/healthcheck/main.go:45 requests `/readyz`
proposed_fix: (a) move to golang:1.27.x-trixie when convenient. (b) add one README sentence that the Docker HEALTHCHECK is a readiness probe and Kubernetes users should wire /livez and /readyz themselves. (c) drop the tar/ADD rewrite; at most add `docker run --rm --entrypoint /usr/local/bin/layerleak-healthcheck` style stat verification to scripts/verify-container-platform.py if the maintainer wants a regression guard.
verifier_note: (a) confirmed: Docker Hub lists golang:1.27.1-trixie. (b) confirmed but already documented: cmd/healthcheck/main.go:45 requests /readyz; README.md:394-395 says so. (c) is most likely wrong: BuildKit's COPY uses tonistiigi/fsutil; copy/copy.go `copyDirectoryOnly` creates a missing destination with `os.Mkdir(dst, stat.Mode())` (source mode including ModeSticky), and copy.go:554 calls `copyFileInfo(fi, parentDir.srcPath, parentDir.dstPath)` for the parent directory, whose copy_unix.go implementation does `os.Chmod(name, m)` with the source mode (and then applies --chown). So the 1777 sticky bit on /tmp is preserved regardless of umask. Cannot be executed here (no daemon), but the implementation evidence contradicts 'likely lost'.

title: Consider pgx/v5 (database/sql stdlib mode) for the Postgres driver; lib/pq is actively released again so this is optional
description: The task brief describes lib/pq as maintenance-only. The evidence is more nuanced: lib/pq v1.12.3 was released 2026-04-03 (six releases since v1.11.1) and its README at this version no longer carries the "maintenance mode, use pgx" banner. Usage is narrow (two sql.Open("postgres") calls, pq.Array once, pq.StringArray once), so swapping to `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib` (v5.11.0, 2026-09-07) would be a small change that gains context-aware cancellation on all paths, structured *pgconn.PgError codes, PGSERVICEFILE/PGPASSFILE support and better prepared-statement/TLS handling. Since 3.0.0 already changes the module path, it is the cheapest time to do it, but it is not required for release.
evidence: internal/storage/postgres.go:14 `"github.com/lib/pq"`, :38 `sql.Open("postgres", ...)`, :318 `pq.Array(tagNames)`; internal/storage/read_postgres.go:412 `var detectors pq.StringArray`; internal/storage/migrate.go:74 `sql.Open("postgres", databaseURL)`; `go list -m -json github.com/lib/pq@latest` -> Version v1.12.3, Time 2026-04-03; pgx/v5@latest -> v5.11.0 2026-09-07
proposed_fix: If adopted: replace the blank import with `_ "github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib"`, `sql.Open("pgx", url)`, pq.Array -> `pgtype.FlatArray[string]` or pass `[]string` directly (pgx stdlib handles text[] natively), update THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and the license CSV, and re-run the postgres integration suite. Otherwise record the decision to stay on lib/pq in CHANGELOG so the question is closed for 3.x.
verifier_note: internal/storage/postgres.go:14 imports lib/pq, :38 sql.Open("postgres"); migrate.go:74 sql.Open("postgres"); read_postgres.go:412 pq.StringArray; `go list -m -u all` shows no newer lib/pq than v1.12.3; grep of the lib/pq@v1.12.3 README for 'maintenance' or 'pgx' returns nothing, confirming the banner is gone. Correctly flagged as optional.

title: Contradiction on 3.0.0 API scope: API-12 (async scan-job model with migration 0005) and API-13 (opt-in bearer auth) are recommended for 3.0.0 inside /api/v1, while PRD-16 schedules bearer auth for 3.1 and PRD-18 marks async jobs OUT of 3.0.0 (only if demand appears). DB-08 (exact-version readiness) and the README/CHANGELOG '0004' wording depend on whether 0005 ships.
description: The decision changes CurrentSchemaVersion, README:330, openapi.yaml:54, RELEASING:249, the CHANGELOG and the migration ledger tests; starting the RC without it risks a second RC.
proposed_fix: Maintainer decision before the rc.1 branch: pick one list; if 0005 ships, grep -rn '0004' README.md RELEASING.md web/docs/openapi.yaml CHANGELOG.md internal/storage/migrate.go and update all hits together.

title: Contradiction on result_schema_version: MIG-22 says result_schema_version=1 and record_schema_version=1 must NOT change; PRD-04 says bump result_schema_version to 2 with a published JSON Schema; API-14 says omitting the empty platform object requires v2; CLI-21 and DOC-13 leave it open; CLI-24 wants the omitempty fix.
description: The wire contract text in CHANGELOG, README, UPGRADING and openapi.yaml, the web/testdata fixtures and TestDocumentedScanResponsesMatchHandler all encode this number; an inconsistent decision will fail validate_docs in the release workflow.
proposed_fix: Decide v1-frozen vs v2; then run `grep -rn 'result_schema_version\|record_schema_version' --include='*.go' --include='*.json' --include='*.yaml' --include='*.md' .` and ensure every occurrence, fixture and test agrees; run scripts/validate_docs.py and `go test ./internal/api -run TestDocumentedScanResponsesMatchHandler`.

title: Contradiction on the v1 deprecation pointer: PRD-27 recommends a final v1 tag marking the root module `// Deprecated:`; MIG-20 recommends README wording plus the pkg.go.dev banner now and an optional v1.0.1 later; but MIG-05/REL-01/CFG-22 move every release regex, tag glob and ruleset to v3-only, and the tag ruleset covers only v1.* today. A v1.0.1 tag could not pass the protected workflow after the v3 rewrite.
description: If the maintainer wants the deprecation pointer, the workflow needs a v1 lane (or the tag must be cut before the regex rewrite, which violates RELEASING's RC/soak policy); if not, PRD-27 should be dropped and README must explain that root-path @latest stays v1.0.0.
proposed_fix: Decide; if yes, add a lightweight 'deprecation-pointer' workflow lane or cut the v1.0.1 tag from a v1 branch before the regex rewrite and extend the ruleset to both patterns; verify with `go list -m -versions github.com/brumbelow/layerleak` after publication.

title: Contradiction on foreign/Windows-layer platforms: LAY-01 proposes excluding windows/foreign-layer platforms from default selection (like attestations) or reporting them as failed-unsupported partials; REG-03 asks skip-with-diagnostic vs fetching the layer from the registry blob endpoint; REG-12 proposes an OS-only selector/default-linux selection. Each changes exit codes and partial semantics for `layerleak scan golang:latest` differently.
description: This is the highest-impact behaviour change for everyday scans of official images and must be described in CHANGELOG/compat notes; three different fixes cannot all ship.
proposed_fix: Pick one policy (recommended: skip foreign-layer manifests with a `platform_skipped` diagnostic and add `--platform linux` OS-only selection), then add scanner/document tests for golang:1.25-style indexes and confirm the README 'incomplete coverage is never a clean scan' sentence is still true for the chosen semantics.

title: Fingerprint semantics are pulled in opposite directions: DET-09 proposes a per-database keyed HMAC, while PRD-13 (baseline/ignore file by fingerprint) and PRD-09 (SARIF partialFingerprints) require fingerprints that are stable across installs and CI runners; DB identity UNIQUE(manifest_digest, fingerprint) was not analysed by anyone (see GAP-06).
description: An HMAC with a per-database key makes baseline files non-portable and SARIF deduplication in GitHub code scanning unstable across runners; the alternative keeps the offline-oracle weakness DET-09 describes.
proposed_fix: Decide the contract in writing (recommend: keep sha256 of the raw value but stop publishing it for low-entropy/short values, or publish a truncated hash); then grep -rn 'fingerprint' internal/findings internal/storage migrations web/docs/openapi.yaml and document it in README and openapi.

title: site.js reveal/IntersectionObserver logic is dead: [data-reveal] and .is-visible have identical styles
description: web/assets/site.js:16-46 observes every `[data-reveal]` element and adds `is-visible`, but web/assets/styles.css:1020-1028 defines `[data-reveal] { opacity: 1; transform: none; }` and `[data-reveal].is-visible { opacity: 1; transform: none; }`, so the class toggle has no visual effect. Thirty lines of JS plus a reduced-motion override (styles.css:1164-1167) maintain an animation that no longer exists; the 2026-09-09 alert ledger shows this area was already touched for lint reasons.
proposed_fix: Either delete the observer block from site.js, the `data-reveal` attributes from the three HTML files and the two CSS rules, or restore an actual fade (`[data-reveal]{opacity:0;transform:translateY(8px)}` gated behind `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` so no-JS and reduced-motion users still see content). Deleting is the smaller, safer change for a release.
verifier_note: styles.css:1020-1028 defines identical `opacity: 1; transform: none` for `[data-reveal]` and `[data-reveal].is-visible`; site.js:16-46 observes and toggles the class with no visual effect. Deleting is the safer release change.

title: Dockerfile sets LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR=/tmp/layerleak/findings in the image but README documents only the API_ADDR image default; the variable is unused by the API binary
description: Dockerfile:38-39 sets two image-level environment defaults: `ENV LAYERLEAK_API_ADDR=0.0.0.0:8080` and `ENV LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR=/tmp/layerleak/findings`. README.md:251 documents the first ('image default is 0.0.0.0:8080') but the LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR row (README.md:206) says only 'auto'. The only consumer of cfg.FindingsDir is the CLI (internal/cli/scan.go:213 -> writeResultArtifacts); layerleak-api, layerleak-migrate-up, layerleak-purge-raw-secrets and layerleak-healthcheck never write local result files, so the ENV is inert in the shipped image. Either the image default should be documented (and the tmpfs mount in docker-compose.yml justified by it) or the dead ENV removed so operators do not look for result files under /tmp/layerleak/findings.
evidence: Dockerfile:38-39: 'ENV LAYERLEAK_API_ADDR=0.0.0.0:8080\nENV LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR=/tmp/layerleak/findings'; `grep -rn FindingsDir internal cmd` (non-test) -> only internal/config/config.go:53,:272 and internal/cli/scan.go:213 / internal/cli/results.go:181,:287; README.md:206: '| `LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR` | auto | Saved result directory. |'
proposed_fix: Remove `ENV LAYERLEAK_FINDINGS_DIR=/tmp/layerleak/findings` from the Dockerfile (no bundled binary uses it), or if it is kept for a future in-image CLI, add 'image default is /tmp/layerleak/findings' to the README/web config rows the same way API_ADDR is annotated.

title: Trailing bytes after a gzip/zstd stream fail the layer even though the digest verified, because the decompressed stream is drained past the tar end-of-archive
description: After tar.Reader returns io.EOF the engine copies the remainder of the *decompressed* reader to io.Discard. compress/gzip in multistream mode then tries to parse another member header; any padding or garbage after the gzip trailer yields gzip.ErrHeader, and klauspost returns a magic mismatch for zstd. containerd/moby only drain the compressed blob (for digest computation) and never read the decompressed stream past the archive, so such blobs pull and run fine but fail in Layerleak with `drain layer: gzip: invalid header`, failing the platform.
evidence: Probe appending 512 zero bytes or 'trailing-garbage' to a valid gzip layer: `err=apply layer sha256:trail: drain layer: gzip: invalid header files=[] layersCompleted=0` for both cases. Code: state.go:416-417 `if _, err := io.Copy(io.Discard, limitedReader); err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("drain layer: %w", err) }` followed by the raw-blob drain at :419.
proposed_fix: Keep the current fail-closed behavior. Optionally map this error at state.go:416-417 to a dedicated diagnostic code (e.g. `layer_trailing_data`) instead of the generic manifest_failed so operators can distinguish it, and add the three fixtures (concatenated members pass; trailing zeros/garbage fail with that code).
verifier_note: Behavior reproduced (`drain layer: gzip: invalid header` for 512 zero bytes and for garbage; concatenated gzip members work), but the compat premise is wrong. containerd's core/diff/apply/apply.go reads trailing data from the DECOMPRESSED stream after archive.Apply (`// Read any trailing data` / `io.Copy(io.Discard, rc)`) and returns the error, so such a blob fails to unpack under containerd too; moby's layer_store applyTar also drains the decompressed stream (it ignores the error). Layerleak's fail-closed behavior is therefore containerd parity, and the recommended 'stop at tar EOF for containerd parity' change would move AWAY from parity and could hide a payload appended after the archive.

title: Recommended mechanical rewrite procedure and validated gotcha list
description: (f) A tool such as marwan-at-work/mod (`mod upgrade --mod-name=github.com/brumbelow/layerleak --version=3`) or icholy/gomajor (`gomajor path github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3`) works, but the repo has no cross-module consumers and only import lines reference the path, so plain `go mod edit` + sed is simpler and auditable. Gotchas checked in a scratch copy: test files are covered by the same sed; go.sum is byte-identical (no self-dependency); gofmt import grouping unchanged; `go mod tidy -diff` clean; cmd/scanner dev entrypoint compiles; Dockerfile uses relative package paths (`./cmd/api` etc.) so it is unaffected; `go install .` and `go install .../v3@ver` both produce a binary named `layerleak`; Codacy (revive/tslint) and CodeQL autobuild do not reference the module path; docs/reviews CSV and web/index.html contain only GitHub URLs (unchanged).
evidence: Scratch run: `go mod edit -module github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3` + sed -> `module: github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3`, `remaining old imports: 0`, `gofmt -l: []`, BUILD_OK, VET_OK, TIDY_OK, `all modules verified`, GOSUM_UNCHANGED, `ls bin` -> `layerleak`, `ok github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3/internal/cli`, `ok github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3/internal/api`.
proposed_fix: Single commit sequence: (1) `go mod edit -module github.com/brumbelow/layerleak/v3`; (2) the sed from MIG-02; (3) `gofmt -l .` must be empty; (4) `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go mod tidy -diff && go test -short ./... -count=1`; (5) apply MIG-03..MIG-18 edits in the same PR so CI (verify.yml:40) stays green; (6) `grep -rn 'brumbelow/layerleak' --include='*.go' --include='*.yml' --include='*.md' --include='*.html' --include='*.py' .` and confirm the only remaining non-/v3 hits are GitHub URLs, ghcr.io image names and the CHANGELOG/README sentences that intentionally describe the frozen root path.
verifier_note: Reproduced the full sequence in the scratch copy (go mod edit + sed, gofmt empty, build/vet/tidy -diff/go.sum unchanged, `go install .` -> `layerleak`). The 'grep for remaining non-/v3 hits' step should also exclude internal/api/handler_test.go:419/430 repository fixtures and the ghcr.io image name.

title: .gitignore lacks __pycache__/, so running the release scripts' Python tests dirties the working tree
description: The working tree was clean at c2ddd45, but after another audit step ran `python3 -m unittest` for scripts/, `git status` now shows untracked `scripts/__pycache__/` and `scripts/tests/__pycache__/`. A release preflight that checks for a clean tree, or a contributor running the tests before committing, will trip on these. Outside the registry area but observed while verifying the tree was untouched.
evidence: `git status --short` -> `?? scripts/__pycache__/` and `?? scripts/tests/__pycache__/`; `grep -n "pycache\|\.pyc" .gitignore` -> no output.
proposed_fix: Add `__pycache__/` and `*.pyc` to .gitignore.

title: 0004 adds constraints NOT VALID and VALIDATEs them in the same transaction, which gives none of the lock relief that pattern exists for
description: The NOT VALID + separate VALIDATE CONSTRAINT idiom reduces locking only when VALIDATE runs in a later transaction (it then needs SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE instead of ACCESS EXCLUSIVE). Here every ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID (lines 193-239) and every VALIDATE (241-259) execute inside the single transaction applyMigration opens for the whole file (migrate.go:258-265), so the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks taken by the ALTER TABLEs are held until commit regardless and the full-table validation scans run under them. The split is harmless but misleading, and it matters for the lock-queue problem in DB-03 and for how future large-table migrations are written.
evidence: 0004_storage_hardening.up.sql:194 `ADD CONSTRAINT repositories_registry_not_blank CHECK (BTRIM(registry) <> '') NOT VALID` ... :241 `ALTER TABLE repositories VALIDATE CONSTRAINT repositories_registry_not_blank;` in the same file; migrate.go:265 `tx.ExecContext(ctx, migration.SQL)` executes the file as one transaction.
proposed_fix: Leave 0004 unchanged (its checksum is frozen, see DB-17) but add a comment-free note in RELEASING/CONTRIBUTING: for future migrations that must validate constraints on large tables, put the VALIDATE CONSTRAINT statements in a separate numbered migration file so they run in their own transaction under the weaker lock; alternatively drop the NOT VALID/VALIDATE split in new migrations when both halves would share a transaction.

False positives: depguard 50 (default deny-list), revive 50 (all exported/package-comments, which revive.toml disables; running revive with the repo's enabled rules via a scratch config yields 0 issues), bodyclose 1 (OpenBlob returns the body to the caller), exhaustive 9 (every switch has a default), gosec 9 (G101 on string constants/test tokens, G302 on chmod 0700 of a directory, G304 reading migration files by design, test-only G306/G402), noctx 6 (integration tests), contextcheck 3 (deferred rollback intentionally uses a fresh context). title: Cosign/gh identities use 'Brumbelow' capitalization while every other reference (module, GHCR, Pages, workflow guard) is lowercase; exact-match identity must be confirmed on the first RC
verifier_note: The open question is answered: `gh api repos/brumbelow/layerleak` returns full_name 'Brumbelow/layerleak' and owner.login 'Brumbelow'. GITHUB_REPOSITORY and the OIDC job_workflow_ref (hence the Fulcio SAN) use the repository's canonical casing, so the documented `--certificate-identity 'https://github.com/Brumbelow/layerleak/.github/workflows/container-release.yml@refs/heads/main'` (README.md:447, SECURITY.md:111, RELEASING.md:317) already matches what the workflow itself verifies with `${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}` (container-release.yml:706, :1208). The lowercase forms in go.mod, GHCR and the Pages origin are required by Go/OCI/Pages and are not evidence of a mismatch. No documentation change is needed; confirming the SAN on the first RC is a harmless checklist item but not a defect.
